Finally, we prove that this property applies to double-shelling convex geometries, $D$-geometries, convex geometries with the $n$-Carousel property and $q$-acceptant convex geometries, thus unifying and extending the existing results regarding the tractability of optimization.

papers.title: Estimation of the entropy of normal populations under prior information
papers.abstract: In many practical applications, prior knowledge about unknown parameters is available in the form of ordering constraints, and incorporating such information into the inferential procedure can improve the efficiency of the resulting estimators. In this paper, we consider the problem of estimating Shannon's entropy of two normal populations with ordered location parameters under a general location-invariant loss function. We derive the maximum likelihood estimator, the restricted maximum likelihood estimator, and the uniformly minimum variance unbiased estimator. Furthermore, we obtain an estimator that dominates the best affine equivariant estimator. In addition, we propose a smooth estimator that improves upon the best affine equivariant estimator. Moreover, we obtain improved estimators with respect to the Pitman closeness criterion. We consider interval estimation and construct several confidence intervals, such as asymptotic confidence intervals, bootstrap confidence intervals, highest posterior density credible intervals, and the intervals based on generalized pivotal quantities. A Monte Carlo simulation study is conducted to assess the performance of the proposed point and interval estimators. Finally, the proposed methods are illustrated by using two real data sets.

papers.title: Index and Robustness of Mixed Equilibria: An Algebraic Approach
papers.abstract: We present two results regarding the relation of the index of equilibria and the index of fixed points, and the index of equilibria and payoff-robustness: any integer can be the index of an isolated completely mixed equilibrium of a finite game. In a particular class of isolated completely mixed equilibria, called monogenic, the index can be 0, +1 or -1 only. In this class non-zero index is equivalent to payoff-robustness. We also discuss extensions of the method of computation to extensive-form games, and cases where the equilibria might be located on the boundary of the strategy set. These results follow from a new method of computing indices of equilibria, which we also develop in this paper, that is based on algebraic properties of the system of polynomials describing completely mixed equilibria.

papers.title: Importance sampling and active subspace in quasi-Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) is widely used in computational finance, and its efficiency strongly depends on the smoothness and effective dimension of the integrand. In this work, we propose a three-step approach, referred to as the IS\_AS\_PI method, which sequentially applies importance sampling (IS), the active subspace (AS) method and preintegration (PI). The proposed method overcomes the problem of empirical failure in constructing active subspaces when nonzero payoff gradients are rarely sampled. Here, empirical failure means that the estimated gradient information matrix is zero and thus provides no useful directions. We establish the orthogonal invariance of active subspaces and IS-active subspaces under suitable conditions. The method is applied to pricing Asian and basket options and estimating the Delta of Asian options under the Black--Scholes model. Numerical experiments show that the proposed method avoids this empirical failure in the deep out-of-the-money cases. Moreover, in all experiments, the proposed method with Laplace IS achieves the largest variance reduction factors, indicating the best performance, among the methods compared.

papers.title: Approximation classes for adaptive anisotropic space-time finite element methods. An almost characterization
papers.abstract: We study the approximation of $L_p$-functions, $p\in (0,\infty]$, on cylindrical space-time domains $Ω_T:=[0,T]\times Ω$, $0<T<\infty$, $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ Lipschitz, $d\in \mathbb{N}$, with respect to continuous anisotropic space-time finite elements on prismatic meshes. In particular, we propose a suitable refinement technique which creates (locally refined) prismatic meshes with sufficient smoothness and the desired anisotropy, and prove complexity estimates. Furthermore, we define a (quasi-)interpolation operator on this type of meshes and use it to characterize the corresponding approximation classes by showing direct and inverse estimates in terms of anisotropic Besov norms.

papers.title: A general equivalence relation on the global class of morphisms of a category
papers.abstract: We introduce a general equivalence relation on the global class of morphisms of a category that subsumes several classical notions of equivalence in mathematics. We show that group-action equivalence relations, pullback equivalence relations, and coarse analysis-operator-based equivalence relations on continuous Bessel families are special cases of this general definition.

papers.title: Online Coordinated Scheduling of EV Battery Charging and Heating in Cold Environments
papers.abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) adoption in cold regions is hindered by degraded EV charging performance at low temperatures, which necessitates effective battery thermal management during charging. Given the coupling of battery charging and heating dynamics, this paper explores the benefits of online coordinated charging and heating control, rather than performing them separately. Specifically, we first build queue models for both battery charging and thermal dynamics. Then, we formulate an optimization problem to minimize the system cost of a charging station, which allows us to coordinate charging and heating through maintaining queue stability. To solve the problem, we develop an online coordinated charging and heating control algorithm using Lyapunov optimization techniques. The proposed algorithm is prediction-free and has provable feasibility and optimality guarantees. Numerical experiments based on real-world data demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our proposed method compared to existing benchmarks.

papers.title: Remarks on modules of finite projective dimension
papers.abstract: We investigate homological and depth-theoretic properties of finitely generated modules of finite projective dimension over Noetherian local rings. A central theme is the study of criteria for freeness and reflexivity derived from the torsion-freeness or reflexivity of tensor products of the form \( M \otimes_R M \) and \( M \otimes_R M^* \). Under mild homological assumptions, we prove that such properties of these tensor products impose strong structural constraints on \( M \), often forcing it to be free. These results generalize classical theorems of Auslander beyond the regular case. The second part of the paper is devoted to the dimension and support of Ext-modules, particularly \( \operatorname{Ext}^i_R(M, R) \) for critical values of \( i \), when \( M \) has finite projective dimension. We establish sharp bounds on their Krull dimensions, analyze their behavior for prime and equidimensional modules, and relate these findings to the grade conjecture and other homological conjectures, i.e., whenever $\operatorname{grade}(M) = \operatorname{ht}(\operatorname{Ann}(M))$ where Gdim$(M)<\infty$. We consider the problem that asks whenever is \( \pd_R(M \otimes_R N) = 1 \)? Applications include new cases of a question of Jorgensen, which asks whether \( \operatorname{pd}(M) < i \) whenever \( \operatorname{Ext}^i_R(M, M) = 0 \) and \( M \) has finite projective dimension over a complete intersection ring. Finally, we examine the projective dimension of prime ideals in rings that fail chain conditions.

papers.title: Traveling waves near shear flows for the inhomogeneous Euler equations with non-constant density
papers.abstract: We investigate the existence and nonexistence of traveling wave solutions near monotonic shear flows with non-constant background density for the two-dimensional inhomogeneous Euler equations in a finite channel. For any small $τ>0$, first, we construct nontrivial traveling waves with velocity and density in $H^{5/2-τ}$ and $H^{3/2-τ}$, respectively, showing that inviscid damping fails at these regularities. Second, when the distorted Rayleigh operator has no eigenvalues, we prove that such traveling wave solutions cannot exist in higher regularity spaces ($H^{5/2+τ}$ for velocity and $H^{3/2+τ}$ for density).

papers.title: Decomposable shuffles
papers.abstract: We develop a combinatorial and order-theoretic framework for shuffles, understood as ordered partitions of the natural numbers. We introduce decomposable shuffles as generalised sums of finite ordinals, copies of $ω$, and copies of its dual $ω^*$, indexed by countable scattered linear orders. These building blocks are called benches, ladders and snakes, respectively. We introduce a subclass, layered shuffles, and for this subclass we construct an explicit finite-address representation which reduces comparison in the induced order on $\mathbb N$ to lexicographic comparison of integer tuples. We determine the order types of represented layered shuffles, establish that all represented orders are scattered, and define an involution that realises order duality. Finally, we introduce a hierarchical composition on bench-free injective uniform shuffles of fixed sign. For each sign, this operation yields a monoid graded by reduced degree. Its degree-one component is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb N)$ and consists precisely of the invertible elements.

papers.title: Schopieray's Galois-modular extension conjecture
papers.abstract: Plavnik, Schopieray, Yu, and Zhang have drawn attention to those (automatically premodular) fusion subcategories of modular fusion categories which are submodules for the Galois action on the ambient category. In particular, they showed that a subcategory is a Galois submodule if and only if its centralizer is integral. In the other direction, Schopieray has conjectured that every premodular fusion category can be embedded as a Galois-closed subcategory of a modular category; Schopieray calls such an embedding a \emph{Galois-modular extension}. We prove Schopieray's conjecture for pseudounitary categories; in the nonpseudounitary case, we prove that every braided fusion category admits a "Galois nondegenerate extension" but we do not know it to be modular. Along the way we record some general comments about the minimal nondegenerate extension problem for braided fusion categories.

papers.title: Sample-wise Constrained Learning via a Sequential Penalty Approach with Applications in Image Processing
papers.abstract: In many learning tasks, certain requirements on the processing of individual data samples can arguably be formalized, in an intelligible way, as strict constraints of the underlying optimization problem, rather than by means of arbitrary penalties that often require heavy trial-and-error tuning. In this paper we show that, in these scenarios, learning can be carried out exploiting a sequential penalty method that allows to explicitly deal with constraints. For the proposed algorithm we show that, under classical assumptions and in the considered learning scenario, penalty subproblems can provably be solved in finite time with suitable guarantees of approximate stationarity in expectation; we also show that, when the latter condition is guaranteed for the subproblems, the overall sequential scheme possesses almost sure convergence properties to KKT-stationary points of (general) constrained problems. The results of experiments on sandbox and real-world image processing tasks show that the method is indeed viable to be used in practical deep learning scenarios.

papers.title: On cohomological dimensions of totally disconnected locally compact groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce Mackey functors for a t.d.l.c. group and define the cohomological dimension of this group over the Mackey category. We then compare this dimension to the rational discrete cohomological dimension defined by Castellano and Weigel, as well as to the Bredon cohomological dimension of that t.d.l.c. group with respect to the family of compact open subgroups. We also extend results about the geometric dimension of a t.d.l.c. group.

papers.title: The variety of orthogonal frames
papers.abstract: An orthogonal n-frame is an ordered set of n pairwise orthogonal vectors. The set of all orthogonal n-frames in a d-dimensional quadratic vector space is an algebraic variety V(d,n). In this paper, we investigate the singularities and components of the variety V(d,n), as well as the algebraic properties of the quadratic ideal I(d,n) generated by the orthogonality relations, which cuts out V(d,n) set-theoretically. By a general result of Ananyan and Hochster, these objects satisfy increasingly strong regularity conditions when d becomes large compared to n; we establish optimal effective bounds to quantify this behavior. We give criteria for the ideal I(d,n) to be prime or a complete intersection, thereby resolving open problems proposed by Conca and Welker. We give criteria for the variety V(d,n) to be normal or factorial. We provide strong evidence in support of the conjecture that I(d,n) defines V(d,n) scheme-theoretically. As applications, we improve the existing bounds for when the Lovász-Saks-Schrijver ideals of simple graphs satisfy these four properties.

papers.title: Critical metrics for the quadratic curvature functional on complete four-manifolds
papers.abstract: We study complete four-dimensional Riemannian metrics on connected manifolds that are critical for the curvature functional $\A(g)=\int_M|\Rm|^2\,\vol$ and have finite curvature energy. If $\langle\Ract\E,\E\rangle\ge0$, where $\E=\Ric-\frac14\Scal\,g$ and $\Ract$ is the curvature action on symmetric two-tensors, then the metric is either Einstein or locally isometric to a product of surfaces of constant Gaussian curvatures $c$ and $-c$, with $c\ne0$. This extends the corresponding compact classification to the complete setting with finite curvature energy.

papers.title: On classifications of third- and fourth-order symmetric tensors by eigenvalues
papers.abstract: This paper addresses two fundamental problems posed by Qi regarding the sufficiency of eigenvalues for the classification of symmetric tensors in the two-dimensional setting. For $2\times2\times2$ and $2\times2\times2\times2$ complex symmetric tensors, we classify their equivalence classes using canonical forms of their associated binary cubics and quartics. We then determine the number of eigenpair classes and the multiplicities of zero eigenvalues for the canonical forms over the complex domain. We demonstrate that these spectral counts do not distinguish all real equivalence classes. Finally, we extend this approach to derive canonical forms and classification for real third- and fourth-order linear partial differential equations in two variables using their bijective relationship to binary forms.

papers.title: A polynomial dimension-dependence analysis of Bramble--Pasciak--Xu preconditioners
papers.abstract: We investigate the dimension dependence of Bramble--Pasciak--Xu~(BPX) preconditioners for simplicial $\mathbb{P}_1$ finite element discretizations of high-dimensional partial differential equations and establish that the condition numbers of BPX-preconditioned systems grow only polynomially with the spatial dimension. Our analysis requires a careful derivation of the dimension dependence of several fundamental tools in the theory of finite element methods, including elliptic regularity, the Bramble--Hilbert lemma, trace inequalities, and inverse inequalities. We further analyze an averaged Scott--Zhang-type quasi-interpolation operator, and show that its associated constants scale polynomially with the dimension. Building on these ingredients, we prove a multilevel norm equivalence theorem and derive a BPX preconditioner with explicit polynomial bounds on its dimensional dependence. The analysis is motivated in part by recent tensor and quantum finite element methods, where dimension-explicit conditioning estimates for BPX preconditioners play an important role.

papers.title: Interpretation of a Discrete de Rham method as a Finite Element System
papers.abstract: Within the framework of Finite Element Systems (FES) we define a numerical method for computing differential forms, inspired by the Discrete de Rham (DDR) method. The discrete $L^2$ product of DDR is given a new interpretation, as a computable approximation of the true $L^2$ product on local spaces of forms defined by partial differential equations. Without significantly modifying the numerical method itself, this point of view provides an alternative approach to the analysis. The conformity and consistency properties we obtain are stronger than those previously shown, even in low dimensions. We can also recover some of the other results that have been proved about DDR, from those that have already been proved, in principle, in the general context of FES. Parts of the analysis involve a conjectural hypothesis of stability of constants, with respect to small mesh perturbations, that we detail. We also bring VEM, the Virtual Element Method, into the discussion. For convenience, background material on the FES framework is reviewed.

papers.title: Closed Colored Models and Demazure Crystals
papers.abstract: We construct and study solvable lattice models whose partition functions are Demazure characters. Two types of colored generalizations of the five-vertex model can be defined that are called the open and closed models. States of both models are associated with Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns, or equivalently, semistandard Young tableaux. We characterize the tableaux arising from states of the closed model and prove that they form a Demazure crystal. This is stronger than identifying the partition function as a Demazure character: it requires constructing Kashiwara crystal operators on the states through lattice moves and recoloring. For the open model, Brubaker, Bump, Buciumas, and Gustafsson showed that the states realize (crystal) Demazure atoms. We also give a new, independent proof of their result. Bump and Naprienko considered bosonic models involving a parameter t. In these models, the edges and vertices are constructed by fusion of simpler edge and vertex types. Taking t=0 produces bosonic analogs of the open model. By reversing the fusion order, we construct closed bosonic models and establish their Yang-Baxter equations, yielding a Demazure-Lusztig recursion for the partition functions. At t=0, these models specialize to bosonic analogues of the closed five-vertex model, and we prove that their states form Demazure crystals.

papers.title: Distributional properties of first jump times of CBI processes with jump sizes in given Borel sets
papers.abstract: We derive an expression for the joint distribution function of the first jump times of a continuous state and continuous time branching process with immigration (CBI process) with jump sizes in given Borel sets having finite total Lévy measures, where by total Lévy measure, we mean the sum of the measures appearing in the branching and immigration mechanisms of the CBI process in question. Our result generalizes a corresponding result of He and Li (2016), who considered this problem in case of a single Borel set having finite total Lévy measure.

papers.title: Spectral decomposition and entropy for open set-valued maps
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the dynamics of set-valued maps whose graphs are open and such that the image of each point is an open and connected set. Building upon the work of P. Duarte and M. Torres, who introduced and analyzed the combinatorial structure of the final recurrent set, we incorporate the notions of transitivity and mixing, thereby bringing their framework into the spirit of Smale's spectral decomposition theorem. We also demonstrate that such maps exhibit infinite topological entropy, and we establish a connection between transitive open set-valued maps and transitive Anosov diffeomorphisms.

papers.title: Matrix-valued regular functions of a quaternionic variable - a decomposition and some approximation results
papers.abstract: A quaternionic matrix-valued regular function is a map $F: Ω\rightarrow M_n(\mathbb{H})$ whose entries are (left) regular functions of a quaternionic variable, where $Ω$ is a domain in $\mathbb{H}$. Given any $n \times n$ matrix-valued regular function $F(q)$ over $\mathbb{H}$ having norm at most $1$, we derive a decomposition of $F(q)$ in the form $U \star \begin{bmatrix} ||F(q_0)|| & 0\\0 & G(q)\end{bmatrix} V$ for some constant unitary matrices $U, V$, some vector $q_0$ and an $(n-1) \times (n-1)$ matrix-valued regular function $G(q)$, where $\star$ denotes the star product over $\mathbb{H}$. We use this to prove a Fisher-type approximation result for matrix-valued regular functions $F(q)$ on the quaternionic unit ball $\mathbb{B}$: if $F(q)$ has norm at most $1$ and is continuous on the boundary of the ball, then $F(q)$ can be uniformly approximated by a convex combination of matrix-valued rational unitary functions on $\overline{\mathbb{B}}$.

papers.title: One-sided Hom shifts
papers.abstract: We prove that it is decidable whether a one-sided shift of finite type is conjugate to a one-sided Hom-shift, and whether a tree-shift of finite type is conjugate to a Hom tree-shift. The proof uses Williams's theory for one-sided shifts

papers.title: Simple and Sharp Generalization Bounds via Lifting
papers.abstract: We bound the supremum of stochastic processes using a rate-distortion functional analogous to classical entropy integrals. A lifting argument embeds the process into a higher-dimensional space with permutation symmetry, reducing the analysis to a stationary process. This gives a two-sided characterization of the supremum of Gaussian processes, including cases where Dudley's entropy integral is not sharp. Combining the sharpness of Dudley's integral for stationary processes with information-theoretic arguments gives a proof of the majorizing measure theorem. The method also yields localized generalization bounds without a slicing argument. As an application, we derive risk bounds for empirical risk minimization over Lipschitz images of Sobolev ellipsoids. Our proof does not use the majorizing measure theorem.

papers.title: A Markovian Approach for Cross-Category Complementarity in Choice Modeling
papers.abstract: In modern retail and e-commerce, customers often purchase multiple items across distinct product categories, exhibiting both substitution and complementarity. We consider the cross-category assortment optimization problem where retailers jointly determine assortments across categories to maximize expected revenue. Most prior work on the topic either overlooks complementarity or proposes models that lead to intractable optimization problems, despite being based on the multinomial logit (MNL) choice model. We propose a sequential multi-purchase choice model for cross-category choice that incorporates complementarity through a Markovian transition structure across categories, while allowing general Random Utility Maximization (RUM)-based choice models to capture the within-category substitution. We develop an Expectation-Maximization algorithm for estimation, and a polynomial-time algorithm for unconstrained assortment optimization that yields the optimal solution when the within-category substitution follows a Markov chain choice model. Furthermore, we introduce an empirical metric to quantify the strength of complementarity across product categories and conduct extensive numerical experiments using both synthetic data and a large-scale transaction-level dataset from a major U.S. grocery store. Our model improves predictive accuracy and model fit in both synthetic and real-data experiments and improves expected revenue in synthetic settings with complementarity. It also reveals intuitive market structures such as brand-loyal cross-category purchasing. Overall, we believe that our model provides a theoretically grounded and practical framework for modeling complementarity and making better cross-category assortment decisions.

papers.title: Constructing and transforming standard resolutions of local modules
papers.abstract: We construct standard resolutions for analytic local modules on complex hypersurfaces using standard basis methods, with extensions to complete intersections. The algebraic version over arbitrary infinite fields is also suggested. Applications include derived category formula of local hypersurface blow-ups, revealing new connections between standard bases and categorical geometry.

papers.title: Global well-posedness and asymptotic behavior of large strong solutions to the 3D full compressible Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients
papers.abstract: It is well known that the global well-posedness of the Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients is a challenging problem, especially in multi-dimensional space. In this paper, we study the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent coefficients in the whole space. When the initial density and the initial temperature are linearly equivalent to some large constant states, we establish the first result on the global existence of large strong solution. Moreover, the optimal decay rates of the solution to its associated equilibrium are established when the initial data belong to $L^{p_0}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ for some $p_0\in[1,2]$.

papers.title: Irreducible representations of tree automorphism groups into Pontryagin spaces
papers.abstract: Let G = Aut(T) be the automorphism group of a regular tree T. We study continuous irreducible representations of G that preserve a continuous strongly nondegenerate sesquilinear form of finite index on a Hilbert space. These are already classified for index 0 (unitary case) and for index 1. We show that there are no more representations for index > 1, which completes the classification.

papers.title: Exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s with Compactly Supported Diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract: We show that for diffeomorphisms of closed simply-connected $4$-manifolds dissolving under a single stabilization, there is a natural induced diffeomorphism on an exotic copy of $\RR^4$. We thereby construct uncountably many exotic copies of $\RR^4$ with nontrivial compactly supported mapping class groups of arbitrarily large rank. This follows from a modification of the construction of the diffeomorphism corks of arXiv:2407.04696 that makes their exteriors simply-connected.

papers.title: Hamilton cycles in pseudorandom graphs: resilience and approximate decompositions
papers.abstract: Dirac's classical theorem asserts that, for $n\ge 3$, any $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree at least $\frac{n}{2}$ is Hamiltonian. Furthermore, if we additionally assume that such graphs are regular and sufficiently large, then, by the breakthrough work of Csaba, Kühn, Lo, Osthus, and Treglown, they admit a decomposition into Hamilton cycles and at most one perfect matching, solving the well-known Nash-Williams conjecture. In the pseudorandom setting, it has long been conjectured that similar results hold in much sparser graphs. We prove two overarching theorems for graphs that exclude excessively dense subgraphs, which yield asymptotically optimal resilience and Hamilton-decomposition results in sparse pseudorandom graphs. Firstly, our results imply that for every fixed $γ>0$, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that if $G$ is a spanning subgraph of an $(n,d,λ)$-graph satisfying $δ(G)\ge\bigl(\tfrac12+γ\bigr)d$ and $d/λ\ge C$, then $G$ must contain a Hamilton cycle. Secondly, we show that for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is $C>0$ so that any $(n,d,λ)$-graph $G$ with $d/λ\ge C$ contains at least $\bigl(1-\varepsilon\bigr)\tfrac d2$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles, and, finally, we prove that the entire edge set of $G$ can be covered by no more than $\bigl(1+\varepsilon\bigr)\tfrac d2$ such cycles. All bounds are asymptotically optimal and significantly improve earlier results on Hamiltonian resilience, packing, and covering in sparse pseudorandom graphs.

papers.title: Interpolation in Polynomial Spaces of p-Degree
papers.abstract: We recently introduced the Fast Newton Transform (FNT), an hierarchical algorithm for performing multivariate Newton interpolation in arbitrary downward closed polynomial spaces of spatial dimension $m$. Here, we analyze the FNT in the context of a specific family of downward closed sets $A_{m,n,p}$, defined as all multi-indices with $\ell^p$ norm less than $n$ with $p \in [0,\infty]$. The FNT performs with time complexity $\mathcal{O}(|A_{m,n,p}|mn)$ on the induced downward closed polynomial spaces $Π_{m,n,p}$. We show that the $Π_{m,n,p}$ choice compared to the tensor product spaces $Π_{m,n,\infty}$, reduces time complexity by a factor of $ρ_{m,n,p}$, decaying super exponentially with spatial dimension when $m \lesssim n^p$. We showcase the efficiency of the FNT by computing activity scores in sensitivity analysis.

papers.title: Period relations for Rankin-Selberg convolutions for $\mathrm{GL}(n)\times\mathrm{GL}(n)$
papers.abstract: Using the modular symbol approach, we prove the rationality and period relations for certain critical values of Rankin-Selberg L-functions for $\mathrm{GL}(n)\times\mathrm{GL}(n)$ over any number field that contains a CM field.

papers.title: Branch-and-Cut for Mixed-Integer Nash Equilibrium Problems
papers.abstract: We consider mixed-integer Nash equilibrium problems in which each player solves a mixed-integer optimization problem parameterized in the rivals' strategies. We distinguish standard Nash equilibrium problems (NEPs), where the parameterization acts only on the cost functions, and generalized NEPs (GNEPs), where the strategy spaces may also depend on the rivals' strategies. We introduce a branch-and-cut (B&C) algorithm for such games that, upon termination, either computes a pure Nash equilibrium or decides that none exists. The main idea is a bilevel reformulation based on the Nikaido--Isoda function. Using bilevel-optimization techniques, we obtain a tractable relaxation of this reformulation and embed it into a B&C framework. Depending on the setting, we derive sufficient conditions for the existence of suitable cuts and finite termination. For GNEPs, we adapt intersection cuts (ICs) from bilevel and mixed-integer linear optimization. Such cuts exist under assumptions that hold, e.g., for pure-integer GNEPs with decoupled concave objectives and linear coupling constraints. Since ICs may become arbitrarily shallow, we complement them with a fallback strategy that fixes recurring integer profiles and ensures finite termination in a relevant setting. For NEPs, suitable cuts always exist via best-response inequalities, and our method terminates finitely whenever the set of best-response sets is finite. This holds, e.g., if (i) the cost functions are concave in the players' own continuous strategies and the strategy sets are polyhedral, or (ii) the cost functions only depend on the player's own strategy and the rivals' integer strategy components. Numerical results on various NEPs and GNEPs show that our tailored B&C method outperforms directly applying the state-of-the-art bilevel solver MibS on the tested integer and generalized knapsack instances.

papers.title: Co-evolving vertex and edge dynamics in dense graphs
papers.abstract: We consider a random graph in which vertices can have one of two possible colours. Each vertex switches its colour at a rate that is proportional to the number of vertices of the other colour to which it is connected by an edge. Each edge turns on or off according to a rate that depends on whether the vertices at its two endpoints have the same colour or not. We prove that, in the limit as the graph size tends to infinity and the graph becomes dense, the graph process converges, in a suitable path topology, to a limiting Markov process that lives on a certain subset of the space of coloured graphons. In the limit, the density of each vertex colour evolves according to a Fisher-Wright diffusion driven by the density of the edges, while the underlying edge connectivity structure evolves according to a stochastic flow whose drift depends on the densities of the two vertex colours.

papers.title: Accelerated Approximate Optimization of Multi-Commodity Flows on Directed Graphs
papers.abstract: We provide $m^{1+o(1)}kε^{-1}$-time algorithms for computing multiplicative $(1 - ε)$-approximate solutions to multi-commodity flow problems with $k$-commodities on $m$-edge directed graphs, including concurrent multi-commodity flow and maximum multi-commodity flow. To obtain our results, we provide new optimization tools of potential independent interest. First, we provide an improved optimization method for solving $\ell_{q, p}$-regression problems to high accuracy. This method makes $\tilde{O}_{q, p}(k)$ queries to a high accuracy convex minimization oracle for an individual block, where $\tilde{O}_{q, p}(\cdot)$ hides factors depending only on $q$, $p$, or $\mathrm{poly}(\log m)$, improving upon the $\tilde{O}_{q, p}(k^2)$ bound of [Chen-Ye, ICALP 2024]. As a result, we obtain the first almost-linear time algorithm that solves $\ell_{q, p}$ flows on directed graphs to high accuracy. Second, we present optimization tools to reduce approximately solving composite $\ell_{1, \infty}$-regression problems to solving $m^{o(1)}ε^{-1}$ instances of composite $\ell_{q, p}$-regression problem. The method builds upon recent advances in solving box-simplex games [Jambulapati-Tian, NeurIPS 2023] and the area convex regularizer introduced in [Sherman, STOC 2017] to obtain faster rates for constrained versions of the problem. Carefully combining these techniques yields our directed multi-commodity flow algorithm.

papers.title: A Riemannian approach for PDE-constrained shape optimization over the diffeomorphism group using outer metrics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the use of outer metrics, in particular Sobolev-type metrics on the diffeomorphism group in the context of PDE-constrained shape optimization. Leveraging the structure of the diffeomorphism group we analyze the connection between the push-forward of a smooth function defined on the diffeomorphism group and the classical shape derivative as an Eulerian semi-derivative. We consider in particular, two predominant examples on PDE-constrained shape optimization. An electric impedance tomography inspired problem, and the optimization of a two-dimensional bridge. These problems are numerically solved using the Riemannian steepest descent method where the descent directions are taken to be the Riemannian gradients associated to various outer metrics. For comparison reasons, we also solve the problem using other previously proposed Riemannian metrics in particular the Steklov-Poincaré metric.

papers.title: On almost Gallai colourings in complete graphs
papers.abstract: We investigate a rainbow analogue of the Ruzsa--Szemerédi problem. For $t \in \mathbb{N}$, we say that a colouring of $E(K_n)$ is almost $t$-Gallai if no two rainbow $t$-cliques share an edge. Motivated by a lemma of Berkowitz on bounding the modulus of the characteristic function of clique counts in random graphs, we study the maximum number $τ_t(n)$ of rainbow $t$-cliques in an almost $t$-Gallai colouring of $E(K_n)$. For every $t \ge 4$, we show that $n^{2-o(1)} \leq τ_t(n) = o(n^2)$. For $t=3$, surprisingly, the behaviour is substantially different. Our main result establishes that $$\left ( \frac{1}{2}-o(1) \right ) n\log n \le τ_3(n) \le O\big (n^{\sqrt{2}}\log n \big ),$$ which gives the first non-trivial improvements over the simple lower and upper bounds. Our proof combines various applications of the probabilistic method and a generalisation of the edge-isoperimetric inequality for the hypercube.

papers.title: Quantum Velocity Averaging (or Not...) in the Semiclassical Regime
papers.abstract: This paper discusses the possibility of applying the velocity averaging theorems in [F. Golse, P.-L. Lions, B. Perthame, R. Sentis: J. Funct. Anal. 76(1):110--125, 1988] to the Wigner equation governing the quantum evolution of the Wigner transform of quantum density operators. Our first main results address the case of the Wigner function of a special class of density operators associated to mixed states, whose Hilbert-Schmidt norm is of order $\hbar^{d/2}$, where $d$ is the space dimension and $\hbar$ the reduced Planck constant. In space dimension $d=1$, we prove that the density function belongs to the Sobolev space $H^s(\mathbb R)$ for some $s>0$. In the case of pure states, we first obtain a characterization of the Wigner transform of rank-one quantum density operators, and apply this characterization (1) to analyze a rather general setting in which velocity averaging cannot apply to the Wigner functions of a family of rank-one density operators whose evolution is governed by the von Neumann equation, and (2) to obtain a quick derivation of Madelung's system of quantum hydrodynamic equations. This derivation provides a physical explanation of one key assumption used in the proof of the negative result (1) described above.

papers.title: NumPSLA -- An experimental research tool for pseudoline arrangements and order types
papers.abstract: We present a program for enumerating all pseudoline arrangements with a small number of pseudolines and abstract order types of small point sets. This program supports computer experiments with these structures, and it complements the order-type database of Aichholzer, Aurenhammer, and Krasser. This system makes it practical to explore the abstract order types for 12 points, and the pseudoline arrangements of 11 pseudolines.

papers.title: On the surjectivity of Galois representations attached to Drinfeld $A$-modules of rank $2$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, where $q$ is a prime power and let $A:= \mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$ and $F:= \mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$. By~\cite{PR09}, the adelic image of the Galois representation attached to a generic Drinfeld $A$-module $\varphi$ of rank $2$ over $F$ satisfying $\mathrm{End}_{\bar{F }}(\varphi)=\varphi(A)$ is open, and determining when it is surjective remains a subtle problem. To resolve this question, in this article, we study the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic surjectivity of the Galois representations attached to $\varphi$, where $\mathfrak{p} \in Ω_A:= \mathrm{Spec}(A) \setminus \{ (0) \}$. There are two directions to investigate this problem: one by fixing the prime $\mathfrak{p}$, and the other by fixing $\varphi$. In the horizontal direction, for a fixed $\mathfrak{p} \in Ω_A$, we give explicit and easily verifiable conditions on Drinfeld $A$-modules $\varphi$ of rank $2$ over $F$ which ensure the surjectivity of the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic Galois representation $ρ_{\varphi,\mathfrak{p}}$. This work extends~\cite{Ray24} to arbitrary $\mathfrak{p}$, and, for $\mathfrak{p}=(T)$, recovers the results of~\textit{loc. cit.} under weaker hypotheses. In the vertical direction, we show that for a fixed Drinfeld $A$-module $\varphi$ of rank $2$ over $F$, whose coefficients satisfy certain congruence and valuation conditions, the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic Galois representation $ρ_{\varphi,\mathfrak{p}}$ is surjective for all $\mathfrak{p} \in Ω_A$. This recovers the example of \cite{Zyw11} and yields new examples beyond those considered in \cite{Zyw25}. As a consequence, we obtain the surjectivity of the associated adelic Galois representation.

papers.title: Quadratic obstructions to Small-Time Local Controllability for the multi-input bilinear Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: We investigate the small-time local controllability (STLC) near the ground state of a bilinear Schrödinger equation when the linearized system is not controllable. It is well known that, for single-input systems, quadratic terms in the state expansion can then lead to obstructions to the STLC of the nonlinear system. In this work, we extend this phenomenon to the multi-input setting, presenting the first example of multi-input quadratic obstructions for PDEs. Our results build upon our previous study of such obstructions for ODEs and provide a functional framework for analyzing them in the bilinear Schrödinger equation.

papers.title: Control of Human-Induced Seismicity in Underground Reservoirs Governed by a Nonlinear PDE-ODE System
papers.abstract: Induced seismicity caused by fluid extraction or injection in underground reservoirs is a major challenge for safe energy production and storage. This paper presents a robust output-feedback controller for induced seismicity mitigation in geological reservoirs described by a coupled 3D PDE-ODE model. The controller is nonlinear and robust (MIMO Super-Twisting design), producing a continuous control signal and requiring minimal model information, while accommodating parameter uncertainties and spatial heterogeneity. Two operational outputs are regulated simultaneously: regional pressures and seismicity rates computed over reservoir sub-regions. Closed-loop properties are established via explicit bounds on the solution and its time derivative for both the infinite-dimensional dynamics and the nonlinear ODE system, yielding finite-time or exponential convergence of the tracking errors. The method is evaluated on the Groningen gas-field case study in two scenarios: gas production while not exceeding the intrinsic seismicity of the region, and combined production with CO$_2$ injection toward net-zero carbon operation. Simulations demonstrate accurate tracking of pressure and seismicity targets across regions under significant parameter uncertainty, supporting safer reservoir operation while preserving production objectives.

papers.title: Curved $\infty$-Local Systems And Projectively Flat Riemann-Hilbert Correspondence
papers.abstract: We generalize the higher Riemann-Hilbert correspondence in the presence of scalar curvature for a (possibly non-compact) smooth manifold $M$. We show that the dg-category of curved $\infty$-local systems, the dg-category of graded vector bundles with projectively flat $\mathbb Z$-graded connections and the dg-category of curved representations of the singular simplicial set of the based loop space of $M$ are all $A_\infty$-quasi equivalent. They provide dg-enhancements of the subcategory of the bounded derived category of twisted sheaves whose cohomology sheaves are locally constant and have finite-dimensional fibers. In the ungraded case, we reduce to an equivalence between projectively flat vector bundles and a subcategory of projective representations of $π_1(M; x_0)$. As an application of our general framework, we also prove that the category of cohesive modules over the curved Dolbeault algebra of a complex manifold $X$ is equivalent to a subcategory of the bounded derived category of twisted sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules which generalizes a theorem due to Block to possibly non-compact complex manifolds.

papers.title: On the Lottery Problem: Tracing Stefan Mandel's Combinatorial Condensation
papers.abstract: Stefan Mandel is said to have won the lottery 14 times. He never disclosed the recipe he called combinatorial condensation, which enabled him to hit the Romanian lottery jackpot in the early phase of his betting career. Combinatorial condensation is frequently mixed up with another strategy known as buying the pot, which Stefan Mandel was pursuing later on. On occasion, he dropped a few hints on combinatorial condensation. The hints are applied in this work to narrow down and assess his initial recipe. The underlying theory resembles what a weekend mathematician, as he once referred to himself, may have encountered in the 1960s. The cardinality of the (15, 6, 6, 5) and (49, 6, 6, 5) lottery schemes shows that Stefan Mandel probably wasn't aware of lottery designs. First concepts on such topics had been available at that time, but coherent theories on combinatorial designs took off only in later decades. There is no absolute evidence beyond doubt, but the size of actual covering designs and the associated efforts allow the following hypothesis: Stefan Mandel most likely pioneered in constructing a (15, 6, 5) covering design many years before others published about it, which he applied in the Romanian lottery. Calculations indicate that he took considerable risks that his method might fail, because he limited himself to a subset of 15 numbers out of 49 numbers. The risks explain why he later changed his strategy from combinatorial condensation to buying the pot.

papers.title: Asymptotic geometry of non-abelian Hodge theory and Riemann--Hilbert correspondence, rank three $\widetilde{E}_6$ case
papers.abstract: We prove the Geometric P=W conjecture in rank 3 on the three-punctured sphere. We describe the topology at infinity of the related character variety. We use asymptotic abelianization of harmonic bundles away from the ramification divisor and an equivariant approach near the branch points to find the WKB (also known as Liouville--Green or phase-integral) expansion of the involved maps. We analyze the Stokes phenomenon governing their behavior.

papers.title: Transport-Free Lower Bounds for Ollivier--Ricci Curvature in Higher-Order Networks: Scope, Tightness, and Computational Applications
papers.abstract: We study how the Bauer--Jost--Liu curvature bound applies to hypergraph Ollivier--Ricci curvature (ORC) and how its accuracy depends on local mass and geometry. An explicit weighted-graph representation shows how the graph theorem applies. A transport construction transfers the bounds to monotone pairwise hyperedge aggregations. We analyze endpoint cancellation under laziness, quantify the exact improvement over the earlier mixture bound, and characterize the extremal geometry at fixed endpoint and overlap statistics. Further results quantify worst-case slack, stability, and exactness on isolated hyperedges. A capacity-constrained short-detour refinement uses additional geometric information and improves monotonically as the query budget increases. As a computational application, a threshold cascade preserves exact transport decisions. Numerical verification and public-hypergraph experiments examine tightness, walk dependence, and aggregation, including evaluations on 42,940 finite pairwise comparisons and 64,620 public-data instances. Together, the results specify the scope, equality mechanisms, and computational uses of BJL-type hypergraph bounds.

papers.title: Turning non-smooth points into rational points
papers.abstract: In a recent paper, the author and Stöhr established a bound on the number of iterated Frobenius pullbacks needed to transform a non-smooth purely inseparable point on a regular geometrically integral curve into a rational point. In this paper we improve this result, by establishing a new bound that is sharp in every characteristic $p>0$.

papers.title: Maximal Inequalities for Empirical Processes under General Mixing Conditions
papers.abstract: This paper provides a bound for the supremum of sample averages over a class of functions for a general class of mixing stochastic processes with arbitrary mixing rates. Regardless of the speed of mixing, the bound is comprised of a concentration rate and a novel measure of complexity. The speed of mixing, however, affects the former quantity implying a phase transition. Fast mixing leads to the standard root-n concentration rate, while slow mixing leads to a slower concentration rate whose speed depends on the mixing structure. Our findings are applied to obtain new Glivenko-Cantelli type results.

papers.title: Periodic Tunnel Systems: Reeb Graph Representations and Circular Max-Flow
papers.abstract: Inspired by the study of transport properties in materials science, we investigate the Reeb graph of a map \(f:X\to\Ss\), interpreting \(X\) as a periodic tunnel system in which transport takes place. The map \(f\) encodes a chosen periodic direction and induces a directed structure on the graph. Under constructibility, we establish a lifting result for directed paths that makes precise how the graph represents tunnel segments in \(X\). To turn this representation into a numerical transport descriptor, we equip the graph with cross-sectional capacities defined, in a Riemannian setting, by weighted Hausdorff-measure integrals. Under boundary regularity and Morse assumptions in dimension \(d\ge2\), we establish continuity over regular Reeb values and continuity of the total capacity across fibers. Taking edgewise infima gives the bottleneck capacities for a circular max-flow formulation, which measures flow through fibers of the map to the circle without choosing an arbitrary inlet or outlet. The resulting descriptor is computable by linear optimization and is related to minimum-cost circulations. For nonnegative real capacities, we prove that the max-flow value is invariant under periodic unrolling: the same descriptor is obtained whether the medium is modeled by a toroidal cell or by its periodic replication along the chosen direction. Simulations on periodic point clouds illustrate the construction and the effects of imposing source--target cuts.

papers.title: Characteristic polynomials and eigenvalues of tensors
papers.abstract: We lay the geometric foundations for the study of the characteristic polynomial of tensors. For symmetric tensors of order $d \geq 3$ and dimension $2$, and symmetric tensors of order $3$ and dimension $3$, we prove that only finitely many tensors share any given characteristic polynomial, unlike the case of symmetric matrices and the case of non-symmetric tensors. We propose precise conjectures for the dimension of the variety of tensors sharing the same characteristic polynomial, in the symmetric and non-symmetric settings.

papers.title: The Geometry of Latent Spaces: Projective Invariants, Structural Identification, and Ratio-Scale Measurement
papers.abstract: Latent variable modeling of discrete ordinal data typically relies on Euclidean priors or continuous divergence bounds, inducing a topological mismatch that leaves models vulnerable to factor score indeterminacy, rotational unidentifiability, and Neyman-Scott incidental parameter bias. We introduce an axiomatic, coordinate-free framework that constructs continuous latent coordinate spaces directly from empirical partial orders without extrinsic probability measures. By parameterizing ordinal choice topologies via a regularized log-odds field on a continuous projective product manifold $(\mathbb{P}^1)^Q$, pairwise field differences preserve the invariants of the projective linear group $\mathrm{PGL}(2, \mathbb{R})^Q$. Spectral decomposition of the integrated invariant Gramian matrix reduces the identification fiber strictly to the one-dimensional dilation group $\mathbb{R}_{>0}^Q$. This establishes ratio-scale measurement with generalized specific objectivity, transcending the restrictive uniform-discrimination assumptions of the Rasch model, identically resolving both classical rotational ambiguity and Guttman's factor score indeterminacy. We prove that an indicator array $P \ge 2Q+2$ is topologically necessary and sufficient to anchor a $Q$-dimensional metric space and structurally resolves incidental item parameters without joint, marginal, or conditional estimation. Finally, leveraging Hadamard differentiability and Hanson-Wright operator concentration, we establish that the projective spectral estimator is strongly consistent, asymptotically normal, and achieves optimal parametric concentration at rate $\mathcal{O}_P(P^{-1/2})$.

papers.title: The Fundamental theorem of tropical differential algebra over nontrivially valued fields and the radius of convergence of nonarchimedean differential equations
papers.abstract: We prove a fundamental theorem for tropical partial differential equations, analogous to the fundamental theorem of tropical geometry in this context. We extend results from Aroca et al., Falkensteiner et al. and from Fink and Toghani for the case of trivial valuation as introduced by Grigoriev to differential equations with power series coefficients over any valued field. Crucial ingredients are the framework for tropical partial differential equations introduced by Giansiracusa and Mereta and a result on infinite intersections of projections of fibers of tropicalizations, which we prove using Hrushovski and Loeser's model-theoretic interpretation of Berkovich analytification. As a corollary of the fundamental theorem, we show that the radius of convergence of solutions of an ordinary differential equation over a nontrivially valued field can be computed tropically.

papers.title: A proof of Ryser's circulant Hadamard conjecture
papers.abstract: We show that an $n\times n$ circulant Hadamard matrix must satisfy a family of congruence equations that have solutions only when $n \leq 4$, proving Ryser's 1963 conjecture that no such matrices exist for $n>4$.

papers.title: Distinction and quadratic base change for regular supercuspidal representations
papers.abstract: In this article, we study Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations based on the machinery developed by Hakim and Murnaghan to study distinguished representations, and the fundamental work of Kaletha on parameterization of regular supercuspidal representations. For regular supercuspidal representations, we give some new interpretations of the numerical quantities appearing in Prasad's formula, and reduce the proof to the case of tori. The proof of Prasad's conjecture then reduces to a comparison of various quadratic characters appearing naturally in the above process. We also have some new observations on these characters and study the relation between them in detail. For some particular examples, we show the coincidence of these characters, which gives a new purely local proof of Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations of these groups. We also prove Prasad's conjecture for regular supercuspidal representations of G(E), when E/F is unramified and G is a general tamely ramified quasi-split reductive group.

papers.title: Functional Data Representation with Merge Trees
papers.abstract: In this paper, we address the problem of representing functional data using tools from algebraic topology. We model functions through merge trees, which, like the more widely used persistence diagrams, are invariant under homeomorphic reparameterizations of their domain. This invariance allows statistical analyses that are robust to functional misalignment. We study a recently introduced metric for merge trees, establish its stability properties, and prove the consistency and convergence rates of a corresponding class of estimators. To illustrate the advantages of our topological approach to functional data analysis, we apply it to the AneuRisk65 dataset, replicating a well-known supervised classification task that made this dataset a benchmark for misaligned functional data. We also compare our results with those obtained using the Fisher-Rao metric, which further supports the effectiveness of the proposed method. The supplementary material includes an extensive comparison between merge trees and persistence diagrams, outlining their similarities and differences to help analysts choose the most suitable representation for a given application.

papers.title: Frames generated by the functional calculus and function frames of a normal operator
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that sequences generated by the functional calculus $(f(T)(e_n))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ can be equivalently written as function sequences $(f_n(T) g)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$, when $T$ is normal and $g$ a cyclic vector for $T$. Here, $(e_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of vectors, $T$ is a bounded normal operator, $f$ and $(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ are functions defined on a neighborhood of the spectrum $σ(T)$, and $g$ is a cyclic vector for $T$. After that, we characterize the frame property of such sequences in terms of the approximate point spectrum of $T^*$. Examples include certain operators (normal operators, compact operators, unilateral shifts, multiplication operators on Hardy spaces, etc.) that either generate only Riesz bases or allow redundancy. Our bridge theorem makes explicit the structural equivalence between frames generated by the functional calculus and function frames.

papers.title: Intersections of translates of finite-dimensionally valued frame spaces are conditionally slice-full and almost slice-full
papers.abstract: In recent work, the topology of frame spaces $\mathcal{F}_{(X,μ),n}$ has been studied via Stiefel manifolds, revealing in particular a connectedness property for intersections of their translates when $\operatorname{span}(\{a_j\}_{j \in J}$ is not too large, in fact when $\operatorname{codim}(\operatorname{span}\{a_j^l\}_{(j,l) \in J \times [\![1,n]\!]}) \geq 3n$, where $\{a_j\}_{j \in J}$ is the translating family \cite{ElIdrissiKabbajMoalige2023}. The investigation of the connectedness of the intersections of translates of the frame space can be extended to questions about the algebro-geometric and measure-theoretic structure of such intersections. The present article addresses these questions by uncovering an almost-linear structure within intersections of translated frame spaces. We show that the set of non-frames in finite-dimensional Hilbert $C^*$-modules inherits the structure of a slice-wise real affine algebraic subvariety. As a consequence, it is a small subset in a precise measure-theoretic sense. In particular, we prove that for any finite-dimensional Hilbert $C^*$-module $\mathcal{H}$ and any countable collection of translates of the frame space $\mathcal{F}_{(X,μ),\mathcal{H}}$, the intersection is conditionally slice-full in $L^2(X,μ;\mathcal{H})$ and almost surely slice-full. We inform the reader that the notions of slice-wise real affine algebraic subvarieties (although related to ind-varieties), conditionally slice-full subsets and slice-full subsets (although related to shy sets) of a Hausdorff topological vector space are, to our knowledge, both new.

papers.title: Hecke Algebra-valued Poincaré Series and Geometric Factorization of Affine Weyl Groups
papers.abstract: This paper studies affine Weyl groups through the geometry of geodesic tubes and their hyperbolic stabilizers. We introduce a geometric framework relating affine Weyl group factorizations to Hecke-algebra-valued Poincaré series and zeta functions on quotient complexes. Using this framework, we prove a conjecture describing the connection between geodesic tubes and factorizations of Poincaré series for affine Weyl groups. We also establish partial results toward a Hecke-algebra-valued zeta identity for simply connected groups, including the cases of types $\widetilde{A}_{n-1}$ and $\widetilde{C}_n$. These results highlight the interaction between affine Weyl group geometry, Hecke algebras, and zeta functions arising from Bruhat--Tits buildings.

papers.title: Infinite periodic groups of even exponents
papers.abstract: We give a new proof that free Burnside groups of sufficiently large even exponents are infinite. The method is very flexible and can also be used to study (partially) periodic quotients of any group which admits an action on a hyperbolic space satisfying a weak form of acylindricity.

papers.title: Asymptotics of principal evaluations of Schubert polynomials for layered permutations
papers.abstract: Denote by $u(n)$ the largest principal specialization of the Schubert polynomial: $ u(n) := \max_{w \in S_n} \mathfrak{S}_w(1,\ldots,1) $ Stanley conjectured in [arXiv:1704.00851] that there is a limit $\lim_{n\to \infty} \, \frac{1}{n^2} \log u(n), $ and asked for a limiting description of permutations achieving the maximum $u(n)$. Merzon and Smirnov conjectured in [arXiv:1410.6857] that this maximum is achieved on layered permutations. We resolve both Stanley's problems restricted to layered permutations.

papers.title: On kernel Mengerian orientations of line multigraphs
papers.abstract: A kernel of a digraph is an independent set $K$ such that every vertex outside $K$ has an arc to a vertex in $K$. We present a polyhedral description of kernels in clique-acyclic orientations of line multigraphs. Given a digraph $D$, let $FK(D)$ denote its fractional kernel polytope, and let $σ(D)$ denote the linear system defining $FK(D)$. A digraph $D$ is called kernel perfect if every induced subdigraph has a kernel, called kernel ideal if the fractional kernel polytope of every induced subdigraph is integral, and called kernel Mengerian if the defining system of every induced subdigraph is totally dual integral. We show that a clique-acyclic orientation of a line multigraph is kernel ideal if and only if it is kernel Mengerian. These equivalent properties hold precisely when the orientation is kernel perfect and has no even-cycle obstruction.

papers.title: Site Percolation on Multi-dimensional Lattice
papers.abstract: Sites in an infinite d-dimensional lattice, open with probability greater or equal to 1/d, form an infinite open path.

papers.title: Stochastic and Noisy Oracles in Smooth Continuous Optimization
papers.abstract: We review models of inexact computational oracles in smooth continuous optimization and their implications for the convergence, computational complexity, and attainable accuracy of optimization algorithms. We adopt a framework in which zeroth-,first-, and second-order oracles are characterized by quantitative error bounds and may accept additional control parameters that influence both their accuracy and computational cost. We introduce deterministic and stochastic oracle models and illustrate their properties through a variety of examples, including finite-difference approximations, stochastic gradients, and randomized derivative estimators. Particular attention is given to the distinction between absolute and relative errors, bias and variance, and stochastic function evaluations with independent or coupled randomness. A central theme of the review is the use of common analytical tools to recover and compare convergence and complexity guarantees under different oracle models. For deterministic and stochastic first-order methods, we show how a general descent inequality leads to complexity bounds under various assumptions on the objective function and all proposed oracle models. In the stochastic setting, we develop bounds on expected stopping times and the accuracy that can be guaranteed under different oracle conditions. We also examine the total computational complexity of algorithms relying on specific oracle constructions and briefly review models of inexact second- order information and their use in optimization algorithms.

papers.title: Initial Subcategories via Free Presentations of the Constant Functor
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a small category. We characterize the full initial subcategories of $\mathcal{C}$ as precisely those whose representables give a free presentation of the constant functor $Δ_{\mathcal{C}}\mathbb{K}:\mathcal{C}\to\mathrm{Vect}$. Such a presentation yields a formula for the limit of any functor $\mathcal{C} \to \mathrm{Vect}$ as the kernel of a morphism between products of evaluations. When the linearized endomorphism ring of every object is local, we show that a minimal free presentation, whenever one exists, determines the unique minimal full initial subcategory, up to equivalence. Bass's characterization of perfect rings gives a sufficient condition for the existence of such presentations. In particular, every finite category with no nonidentity endomorphisms, such as a finite poset, contains a unique minimal initial full subcategory. In the poset case, our results recover the minimal initial subposet constructed in [BDL27] and [DL26]. When $\mathcal{C}$ is the free category on a finite quiver, we give an explicit construction of its minimal initial full subcategories, show that every such subcategory arises from this construction, and provide algorithms with time-complexity bounds.

papers.title: Stochastic Linesearch Methods for Stochastic Variational Inequality Problems: Parameter-Free Schemes and Non-Monotone Variants
papers.abstract: Much of the existing convergence guarantees and rate statements for stochastic variational inequality (SVI) problems are limited to stochastic approximation schemes that employ constant or diminishing steplength sequences bounded by some reciprocal of the Lipschitz constant $L$ of the map. This requires both knowing such constants and may lead to debilitatingly small steplengths, afflicting the scheme with potentially poor performance. We propose a parameter-free stochastic extragradient method with periodically restarted linesearch (\textbf{SEG-LS}) for solving pseudomonotone and monotone SVI problems. The resulting stepsize sequence is neither monotone nor requires prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant $L$. We show that the iteration and sample complexities for computing a point whose residual has norm at most $ε$ in expectation are $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ and $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-4})$, respectively. These results improve to $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-1})$ and $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ in the monotone setting. In addition, we propose a periodically restarted biased stochastic linesearch method (\textbf{B-SLAM}) for solving non-monotone SVIs under strict copositivity. The resulting iteration and sample complexities are $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ and $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-4})$, respectively. Preliminary numerics support these findings and display promise.

papers.title: The complexity of tilting
papers.abstract: Many explicit constructions in algebra are not first-order definable in classical finitary logic, but are, however, definable in infinitary logic. The aim of this paper is to show how infinitary logic can be used to lift model-theoretic results in arithmetic to a quantifier-sensitive form. We apply this idea to a deep result of Jahnke and Kartas on the model theory of perfectoid fields. Our main result is that a first-order sentence $φ$ holds in the tilt $k^{\flat}$ of a perfectoid field $k$ if and only if a certain sentence $φ^{\natural}$ holds in a non-principal ultrapower of $k$, where $φ^{\natural}$ does not depend on $k$ and is only slightly more complicated than $φ$ itself. In particular, tilting preserves the Lévy hierarchy in a precise sense. To this end, we prove that the Standard Decomposition of a valued field at a constant $t$ is infinitarily interpretable by formulas of rank at most 1.

papers.title: String-averaging bargaining in solidarity cooperative games
papers.abstract: We consider the situation that the grand set of all players, in a cooperative game in characteristic function form with a nonempty core, consists of recognizable subsets of players. The underlying assumption is that the players of each subset have something in common between themselves which is not shared by the players of other subsets. For example, the members of these subsets are distinguishable by their nationalities or by their geographic locations or by some other market-related economic or social property. In addition to the agreement of all players to play the game to reach a point in the core, the members of each subset want to steer the iterative orbit of the bargaining process to a point in the core that will reflect the strength of their solidarity within their subset. This is why we call such subsets solidarity sets. The solidarity means that players of a solidarity set are willing to participate in coalitions that include only members of their solidarity set and are not willing to participate in coalitions of other solidarity sets. The question is how can such a game be played? Is there an iterative bargaining scheme that will generate a sequence of payoffs that converges to a point in the core which reflects the solidarity of the members of the solidarity sets? We propose bargaining schemes that allow the members of each solidarity set to perform, independently from other solidarity sets and, therefore, simultaneously in time, a full but finite sweep of intercoalitional collaboration. Then the end-points of all these sweeps are combined into a single payoff vector via a convex combination wherein the coefficients of the convex combination may reflect some a priori knowledge about the relative strengths of the different solidarity sets. These bargaining schemes are applied to a new type of cooperative game that we call solidarity cooperative game (SCG).

papers.title: An explicit bound on the extremal function for complete graph minors
papers.abstract: Kostochka and Thomason independently proved that every graph with density at least $β\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ has a $K_t$ minor, for some constant $β$. Thomason later proved that the least such density is $(0.319\ldots+o(1))\,t\sqrt{\log t}$. However, the $o(1)$ term in this formula is not explicit, so the formula gives no bound for any specific value of $t$. The goal of this paper is a bound of the form $β\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ that holds for every $t$, with $β$ small. We prove that, for every integer $t\geqslant2$, every graph with density at least $4.5\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ has a $K_t$ minor.

papers.title: Nonlinear Maps Between Irreducible Representations in Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Equivariant linear maps cannot mix non-isomorphic irreducible representations, whereas nonlinear activations can. We develop a degree-resolved version of this nonlinear interaction picture and use the resulting block inventory to construct Specht Triple, a residual on unordered graph triples. On a synthetic structural benchmark with a frozen GIN backbone, Specht Triple reduces aggregate standardised test MSE by 11.05% relative to a parameter-matched Projector Control using the same irreducible projectors and complete linear equivariant space. The results support irreducible decomposition as an inductive bias for nonlinear higher-order equivariant processing.

papers.title: Box-Cone Representations of Bound-Factor RLT Constraints in Semidefinite Relaxations
papers.abstract: Linear inequalities can generate large constraint systems in semidefinite relaxations of binary quadratic programs, making the quadratic subproblems of splitting methods expensive to solve. We develop a box-cone representation of bound-factor reformulation-linearization technique (RLT) constraints in semidefinite relaxations of binary quadratic programs. These constraints arise by multiplying each original linear inequality by every binary variable and its complement and linearizing the resulting products. Our key observation is that all products generated by one inequality share a common slack and admit an exact representation in the standard cone over the unit box. This box-cone representation processes the inequalities through independent explicit projections, without introducing a separate nonnegative slack for each scalar RLT inequality. We illustrate the computational use of the representation within standard two-block alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). The resulting subproblems require linear solves with a reusable factorization and explicit cone projections, without enlarging the semidefinite matrix. Experiments on 257 binary quadratic programs compare this implementation with SDPNAL+. A second application groups Max-Cut triangle inequalities into box cones and uses the resulting bounds within an existing branch-and-bound framework. Tests on 220 graphs show competitive performance with MADAM using only triangle cuts. Together, these applications illustrate the representation's usefulness as a building block for first-order methods.

papers.title: On kinetic alignment models with rough communication kernel
papers.abstract: We prove the weak maximum principle and the Cucker-Smale flocking theorem for a general class of kinetic alignment models with rough communication kernels. This includes the classical Cucker-Smale and Motsch-Tadmor systems with defining kernel $φ$ assumed to be merely continuous or even $φ\in L^\infty$ for solutions in the Lebesgue class $f\in L^1$. For such models the characteristic flow-map is not well-defined and therefore the classical approaches of Cucker-Smale \cite{CS2007a,CS2007b} or Ha-Liu-Tadmor \cite{HL2009,HT2008} break down. We develop a new method adopted to rough settings based on Ambrossio's probabilistic representation of solutions and construction of dynamic barriers. All proofs are performed in the framework of so called bounded communication protocols, a non-smooth variant of regular protocols introduced in \cite{Shv-CPAM, Shv-EA} and representing a broad range of models of collective dynamics.

papers.title: Meshless Latent Dynamics Models for Model Order Reduction of time-dependent Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: Latent dynamics learning has emerged as a prominent approach for Model Order Reduction (MOR) of time-dependent, parameterized Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). Traditional autoencoder-based approaches are intrinsically tied to fixed spatial discretizations during both training and inference, motivating the development of meshless methodologies. In this context, conditioning provides a natural mechanism for representing temporal evolution through spatially continuous functions, enabling mesh-agnostic Latent Dynamics Models (LDMs). In this work, we introduce a unified mathematical framework for mesh-agnostic LDMs based on conditioning in Neural Fields (NeFs). Leveraging a taxonomy of conditioning mechanisms (weak, strong, and pure), we formulate meshless LDMs as NeFs conditioned on a latent state. We establish a Universal Approximation Theorem (UAT) for this class of models and analyze their stability by deriving Lipschitz bounds for different conditioning mechanisms. Our analysis reveals an expressivity--stability trade-off, providing insight into why more expressive conditioning, despite its higher representational capacity, can potentially degrade performance during temporal extrapolation. Finally, we provide a comprehensive comparison of meshless and mesh-based architectures in the continuous limit of the spatial discretization, showing that meshless models guarantee grid-independent Lipschitz bounds, unlike mesh-based counterparts. Our experiments across Burgers' equation, Navier--Stokes flow past a cylinder, and linear advection show that meshless LDMs can achieve predictive accuracy comparable to or better than their mesh-based counterparts while using only 2% of the trainable parameters and exhibiting nearly constant error across spatial discretizations.

papers.title: When can Optimally Trained Transformers Achieve Near-Lossless Token Prediction for non-Markovian Data?
papers.abstract: There exists little mathematical theory explaining why Transformer architectures are empirically successful even for non-Markovian data. To this end, this paper studies next-token prediction via stochastic optimal control theoretically trained Transformers for such sources, where we consider either stationary and ergodic non-Markovian sources or those which are hidden Markov models of some finite order (possibly non-stationary). In either case, we first obtain error bounds via finite models with finite window approximations. For stationary ergodic sources, the resulting error is bounded by an entropy gap; for $N$th order Markovian sources, it decays at an exponential rate $α^{\lfloor M/N\rfloor}$, where $M$ is the window length and $α$ is determined by filter stability (and the Dobrushin coefficients of the transition and measurement kernels). We then construct a Transformer of depth $M+1$, one head per layer, realizing the truncated filter, and we optimally train it with stochastic control developed in earlier work, which rigorously returns a near optimal Transformer. In particular, we show that for a non-Markovian source, either under stationarity and ergodicity for general models or under filter stability for hidden Markov models, an optimally trained Transformer has arbitrarily small performance error with increasing context length, data, and approximation refinement. Numerical studies accompany the theory.

papers.title: Rational curves of submaximal quantum index
papers.abstract: On a complex toric surface, oriented real rational curves tangent to the toric boundary at real points are distinguished by their value of quantum index. Using variants of usual Welschinger multiplicities, G. Mikhalkin defined enumerative invariants $W_{\tildeΔ}^κ$ that are provided by a signed count of oriented real rational curves with given quantum index $κ$ and fixed tangency points on the boundary of the positive quadrant (the tangency orders being encoded by $\tildeΔ$). We prove that, for most toric surfaces and tangency orders, the invariant $W_{\tildeΔ}^κ$ is zero in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $κ$. This is done by enumerating tropical curves with Block--Göttsche multiplicities. Additionally, we prove that, in many situations, the lower bound, given by the absolute value $|W_{\tildeΔ}^κ|$ of $W_{\tildeΔ}^κ$, for the number of oriented real rational curves is not sharp close to the tropical limit in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $κ$.

papers.title: Erdős--Straus Conjecture: Modular Inversion in Mordell Classes
papers.abstract: We examine modular inversion of strict Grid certificates in a ceiling continued-fraction construction for the Erdős--Straus equation. The six Mordell classes modulo $840$ form four inversion orbits. Prime-input pattern frequencies in the pairs $121 \leftrightarrow361 $ and $289 \leftrightarrow 529$ have equal asymptotic limits for every fixed cutoff.

papers.title: CuPIQP: A Batched and Differentiable QP Solver on GPUs for Robot Learning and Control
papers.abstract: Quadratic programs (QPs) are fundamental building blocks of many robotic tasks such as inverse kinematics, whole-body control, and model predictive control. Extending these methods to large-scale robot learning and control requires solving many QPs concurrently and, for end-to-end learning, differentiating through their solutions. Efficient batched optimization is therefore essential to bringing established model-based methods into GPU-based robotics pipelines. We present \textsc{cuPIQP}, a batched and differentiable QP solver on GPUs based on a proximal interior-point method, with unified support for dense, sparse, and multistage problems. The solver exploits parallelism across independent QPs and their internal structure while preserving per-problem numerical updates and termination decisions. Benchmarks with up to 16384 QPs per batch demonstrate solve-time speedups of up to $18.8\times$ over \textsc{Moreau} and $4.26\times$ over eight-core \textsc{PIQP}. In an end-to-end learning task, \textsc{cuPIQP} accelerates training by $4.6\times$ over \textsc{QPAX} and $7.8\times$ over \textsc{Moreau}. By reducing the computational cost, \textsc{cuPIQP} provides efficient, reusable infrastructure for integrating model-based optimization into large-scale robot learning and control.
