Motivated by these results, we then construct a quasi-stationarity diagnostic using simulation-based inference: a recurrent neural network (RNN), trained on particle approximations of non-linear effective flows, estimates posterior probabilities of decorrelation. The learned diagnostic is then transferred to collective-variable traces of high-dimensional particle approximations. We investigate the behavior and robustness of this diagnostic on a set of numerical experiments, comparing it to the MCMC diagnostic of Binder et al.\ on both synthetic examples and a molecular system, in and out of its training prior distribution. When its prior assumptions hold, the RNN diagnostic outperforms the MCMC diagnostic in ROC analysis, is less conservative, fails less often, and has an interpretable decision threshold.

papers.title: Formal Neighborhood Equivariant Cohomology and Kirwan Surjectivity at Singular Values
papers.abstract: Let \(G\) be a compact Lie group acting Hamiltonianly on a symplectic manifold \(M\) with moment map \(μ:M\to\g^*\). For a singular value \(a\) of \(μ\), the symplectic quotient \(μ^{-1}(a)/G\) is stratified and the classical Kirwan map is not defined. We introduce a \emph{formal neighborhood equivariant cohomology} \(\cH_G^*(a)\) using the slice-groupoid Cartan sheaf and the closed embedding \(μ^{-1}(a)/G\hookrightarrow N_a/G\) for a \(G\)-invariant neighborhood \(N_a\) of \(μ^{-1}(a)\). We define a formal Kirwan map \[κ_{\mathrm{formal}}:H_G^*(M)\longrightarrow \cH_G^*(a).\] We prove that it is surjective under a local equivariant homotopy retraction condition on the slice level sets \[ C_x=μ_x^{-1}(a|_{\g_x})\subset S_x, \] which is satisfied. We also prove an equivariant tubular neighborhood theorem for singular level sets: under real analytic/proper or \(G\)-invariant Whitney stratified assumptions, there exists a \(G\)-invariant open neighborhood \(U\) of \(μ^{-1}(a)\) and a \(G\)-equivariant strong deformation retraction \(U\toμ^{-1}(a)\). When such a neighborhood exists, the formal cohomology is canonically isomorphic to the Borel equivariant cohomology of the level set, and the formal Kirwan map is the classical restriction map. The formal framework therefore yields a Kirwan-type map at the singular value with the surjectivity property. As an application we recover the even-degree surjectivity theorem of Delarue--Ramacher--Schmitt for \(S^1\)-actions and clarify why odd-degree surjectivity fails in general.

papers.title: University Research and Leadership in the Age of AI: Mobilizing Intellectual Capacity and Building the Infrastructure for Discovery
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is expected to disrupt research across academia, changing how knowledge is produced and how research is organized. Recent developments in mathematics provide an early example of strong AI research capabilities and the professional disruption accompanying them. Universities should respond by building the scientific, computational, and organizational capacity to develop AI and shape the research it enables. The relationship is reciprocal: AI can advance disciplinary research, while scientific questions, experimental evidence, and disciplinary expertise can guide AI development. This article proposes connecting shared computational resources with sustained technical teams, interdisciplinary research, experimental facilities, and knowledge infrastructure that makes findings traceable and reusable. It distinguishes three commitments with different resource requirements: operating existing models, developing AI for disciplinary research, and investigating the foundations of AI. Commercial services can support this agenda alongside institutional capabilities for independent investigation, evaluation, and preservation of the research record. Consortia and national facilities can broaden participation and support capabilities beyond individual campuses. Initial programs should assess scientific value, total costs, and contributions to AI development, with expansion guided by evidence. These changes require sustained funding, professional support, and recognition of the work that makes research reliable and cumulative. Building this capacity will enable universities to pursue new research directions, train future researchers, and exercise scientific leadership as AI transforms academic inquiry.

papers.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
papers.abstract: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As consequences, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family, and each critical spherical catenoid admits a smooth family of free boundary constant mean curvature deformations in its supporting ball. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$.

papers.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
papers.abstract: Let $V_{g,n}$ be the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of hyperbolic surfaces of genus $g$ with $n$ cusps. The fixed-$n$ large-genus expansion of Mirzakhani and Zograf has correction terms polynomial in $n$ of degree $2i$ at order $g^{-i}$, and ceases to be uniform when $n$ is of order $\sqrt g$. We prove an asymptotic expansion in powers of $1/g$ that holds uniformly in all $n\ge0$, with coefficients analytic in a density parameter that ranges over a compact interval, including the limits $n/g\to0$ and $n/g\to\infty$. Its leading term is explicit, contains no undetermined constant and has relative error $O(1/g)$; truncation at an order proportional to $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\exp(-a\sqrt g))$ for some $a>0$. For fixed $n$ this confirms Zograf's conjecture that the constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics is $1/\sqrtπ$. We also determine, at every cusp density, the limits of the volume ratios $V_{g,n}/V_{g-1,n+2}$ and $V_{g,n+1}/(2gV_{g,n})$ and, in all degrees, the asymptotics of the ratios of adjacent coefficients of the one-boundary volume polynomial; this answers two questions of Mirzakhani. The proof deforms mixed $κ_1$--$ψ$ intersection numbers into pure $ψ$ intersection numbers along a family whose recursion has nonnegative coefficients, fixes the overall constant through Painlevé I without assuming resurgence, and recovers individual volumes by a local limit theorem in the number of cusps. As an application, the spectral gap of a Weil--Petersson random surface with $n\gg\sqrt g$ cusps tends to zero in probability; this removes the restriction $n/g\to0$ from a theorem of Shen and Wu.

papers.title: An unconditionally convergent BDF2-type finite element integrator for the inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation
papers.abstract: We propose and analyze a fully discrete numerical scheme to approximate solutions to the inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (iLLG) equation, a state-of-the-art model to describe the dynamics of the magnetization at subpicosecond time scales. The method employs first-order finite elements for the spatial discretization and the two-step backward differentiation formula (BDF2) for the time discretization, where the inertial term is treated by a convex combination of BDF2 and the backward Euler method. We prove well-posedness and unconditional stability of the scheme, and obtain explicit bounds for the error in the realization of the iLLG-inherent unit length constraint satisfied by the magnetization. Moreover, we derive the discrete energy law satisfied by the approximations, which resembles the inherent dissipative energy law of the model. Finally, with a constructive approach, we prove unconditional convergence of the approximations toward a weak solution of the problem. Numerical experiments assess the performance of the scheme and validate the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Quadratic Returns for a Moving Water Tank: An Explicit Right Inverse and a Sylvester Representation
papers.abstract: Coron's return method established local nonlinear controllability of a moving water tank in sufficiently large time. We study the quadratic response at uniform equilibrium, where the acceleration input in the linearized model cannot excite the Fourier modes of the fluid with even indices. At three one-way wave crossings ($T=3$), we construct a nonzero smooth acceleration, whose first two final-state coefficients vanish. A planar curve reduces this cancellation to a scalar identity. At this reference acceleration, two integrations give an explicit control correction that preserves the linear return and produces any given leading change in the quadratic final state. The correction maps periodic $H^r$ targets with zero mean to $H^r$ controls for every nonnegative integer $r$. A contraction argument also gives local exact solvability of the quadratic final-state equation. Finally, a time-dependent Sylvester equation provides an alternative representation of the coupling responsible for the second-order correction. The associated change of state coordinates involves one spatial derivative, while the control correction preserves regularity in appropriate Sobolev spaces. These results concern the first two variation equations only. Keywords: Controllability, control of partial differential equations, return method, Saint-Venant equations, Sylvester equations.

papers.title: Instability of exact finite-amplitude acoustic-gravity waves
papers.abstract: Godin (\textit{J. Fluid Mech.}, vol. 767, 2015, pp. 52--64) showed that compressible fluids in a uniform gravity field support finite-amplitude incompressible wave motions, in which every parcel conserves pressure and density, and constructed exact Gerstner-type surface and edge waves, possibly carried by currents. Using the short-wavelength instability method for compressible flows, we show that these waves are linearly unstable above a critical steepness. The stability of each fluid level reduces to a Floquet problem depending on two parameters: the steepness $\mathfrak{e}=e^{ka_2}$ and $ν^2=(1-\mathfrak{e}^2)ν_0^2$, where $ν_0^2=\cos^2α\,N_0^2/Ω^2$, $N_0$ is the buoyancy frequency of the hydrostatic reference state, $α$ the inclination of the plane of motion and $Ω=(gk\cosα)^{1/2}$ the intrinsic orbital frequency. In an isentropic fluid, a level is unstable if $\mathfrak{e}>1/3$, recovering Leblanc's threshold for Gerstner waves (\textit{J. Fluid Mech.}, vol. 506, 2004, pp. 245--254) and extending it to compressible surface and edge waves; weak stable stratification lowers the threshold to $\frac13-\frac{32}{81}ν_0^2+O(ν_0^4)$. In an isothermal atmosphere, $ν_0^2=κ\cosα/(kH)$, where $H$ is the pressure scale height. For horizontal wavelengths near $5.5\,H/\cosα$, principal subharmonic resonance makes the critical steepness vanish. For the fast airglow wave observed by Hecht et al. (\textit{J. Geophys. Res.}, vol. 107, 2002, D20, 4444), which Godin interpreted with his solution, the lidar temperature places the layer in which this interpretation is consistent on this resonance, where the critical steepness is typically 0.1 instead of $1/3$. Instability is confined to a layer beneath the free surface of surface waves and to a wedge at the shoreline of edge waves.

papers.title: Intersection multiplicity of a sparse curve and a trinomial curve
papers.abstract: Let f $\in$ C[x, y] be a trinomial and let g $\in$ C[x, y] be a sparse polynomial with N monomials (N $\ge$ 1). We address the problem of bounding the local intersection multiplicity of the bivariate polynomial system f = g = 0 at an isolated root q $\in$ (C * )^ 2 only in terms of N . Our main result establishes that the local multiplicity of the system at any isolated solution q $\in$ (C * ) ^2 is at most (N -1)(N +2)/ 2 , independently of the degrees of f and g. Furthermore, we know that this bound is sharp for N = 3.

papers.title: The German Tank Problem & Navigating by Scent
papers.abstract: A robot searching for the source of an odor must eventually answer a notably hard question: have I arrived? Near the source, concentration gradients homogenize, turbulence corrupts the signal, and a small robot often lacks the positional accuracy to map the plume. Here, we describe a lightweight remedy inspired by a World War II statistics conundrum: the German tank problem. To approximate German armament production, Allied analysts developed an estimator based on serial numbers from captured tanks. Analogously, we use the same procedure over sampled chemical sensor readings from a robot to create estimates for the peak concentration of an odor plume, and therefore the odor's source. Treating each sensor reading as an observation, our unbiased estimator needs only a running maximum and a sample counter. A confidence bound turns both numbers into a principled rule that the robot or UAV can use to determine whether it should keep searching for the odor source. We derive the estimator and its bound, demonstrate its sample efficiency, and examine its robustness even when its assumptions fail. Finally, we summarize the estimator's role as the termination criterion for olfactory navigation.

papers.title: Convergence Analysis of Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Descent under Relaxed Assumptions
papers.abstract: We study convergence rates of Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Descent (NAG) method for convex optimization in both deterministic and stochastic settings. We focus on a more general smoothness condition raised from several machine learning problems empirically and theoretically. We show the accelerated convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}\left(1/T^2\right)$ in terms of the function value gap, given access to exact gradients of objective functions, matching the optimal rate for standard smooth convex optimization in \citep{nesterov1983method}. Under the relaxed affine-variance noise assumption for stochastic optimization, we establish the high-probability convergence rate of order $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sqrt{\log\left(1/δ\right)/T}\right)$ and this rate could improve to $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\log\left(1/δ\right)/T^2\right)$ when the noise parameters are sufficiently small. Here, $T$ denotes the total number of iterations and $δ$ is the probability margin. Up to logarithm factors, our probabilistic convergence rate reaches the same order of the expected rate obtained in \citep{ghadimi2016accelerated} where the assumptions of bounded variance noise and Lipschitz smoothness are required. We additionally establish the convergence rates of the studied algorithms in the non-convex setting.

papers.title: Weak mixing and non-recurrence along finitely generated multiplicative semigroups of $\mathbb N$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite nonempty set of primes, and let $S_{\mathcal P}$ be the multiplicative semigroup that they generate. We prove that there are an invertible weakly mixing measure-preserving transformation $T$ and a set $A$ of positive measure such that $A\cap T^{-r}A=\varnothing$ for every $r\in S_{\mathcal P}$. This gives a negative answer to Bergelson's 1996 question concerning recurrence along $\{2^m3^n:m,n\geq1\}$, and applies to every finitely generated multiplicative semigroup of positive integers. More generally, we give a sufficient condition for weakly mixing non-recurrence based on divisibility properties and separation by finitely many rotations of the circle. This criterion also applies to an infinitely generated multiplicative semigroup not contained in any $S_{\mathcal P}$ with $\mathcal P$ finite.

papers.title: Finitely many solutions for the prescribed scalar curvature problem at the critical flatness order
papers.abstract: We study the following prescribed scalar curvature problem $$ -Δu=K(y)u^{2^*-1},\ \ u>0 \,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^N, $$ where $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$. For $N\geq4$, we construct a positive $K(y)$ with maximum set $\{|y|=1\}$ and critical order of flatness $m=N-2$ at $|y|=1$, such that the equation admits only finitely many positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. To this end, we prove the compactness of the solution set for this equation by blow-up analysis and then apply Sard's theorem to choose $K$ for which each solution is non-degenerate and hence isolated, so that the solution set is finite. Our results also give a definite answer to Wei--Yan's conjecture in [J. Wei and S. Yan, JFA, 2010].

papers.title: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
papers.abstract: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family. We determine the minimum density for five of the nine Archimedean grids for which it was not known: it is $2/3$ for the truncated hexagonal grid, $3/7$ for the truncated square grid, and $1/3$ for the trihexagonal (kagome) grid, the elongated triangular grid and the snub hexagonal grid. All lower bounds are proved by the discharging method. For the three remaining non-regular Archimedean grids, we also obtain some bounds: the minimum density lies between $3/7$ and $13/30$ for the truncated trihexagonal grid, between $1/3$ and $11/30$ for the rhombitrihexagonal grid, and between $2/7$ and $9/28$ for the snub square grid. As a by-product, we prove that every identifying code of a cubic graph with the slow growth property in which every vertex lies on exactly one triangle (resp. $4$-cycle) has density at least $2/3$ (resp. $3/7$).

papers.title: Complete Determination of the Gallai--van der Waerden Number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\)
papers.abstract: This paper completely determines the Gallai--van der Waerden number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\) for all integers \(r\ge 3\): \[ \mathrm{GW}(3;3,3)=\mathrm{GW}(4;3,3)=9,\qquad \mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)=r\quad (r\ge 5). \]

papers.title: The longest increasing subsequences of Luce permutations and permutons
papers.abstract: We investigate the longest increasing subsequences (LIS) of random permutations distributed under the Luce model with weights $θ_1^{(n)} \ge \ldots \ge θ_n^{(n)}$. Our first main result provides a general formula for the growth rate of the LIS. For example, we get that the LIS of Luce permutations with Sukhatme weights $θ_k^{(n)} = n-k+1$ grows like $\sqrt{n}$. We also give simple conditions for the LIS to be of order $n^β$, for any given $β\in[1/2,1)$. Our second main result states that, if the weights are of the form $θ_k^{(n)} = f\big( (k-1)/n \big)$ for a sufficiently regular function $f$, then the LIS divided by $2\sqrt{n}$ converges in probability to a constant $K(f)$ described by a variational problem. Throughout, we make extensive use of coupling techniques; in particular, to prove our second main result, we argue that Luce random permutations behave similarly to random permutations sampled from the ``Luce permuton''.

papers.title: Boundary-Driven Nonequilibrium for the Coulomb Landau Equation
papers.abstract: We establish a nonlinear theory of the Coulomb Landau equation in smooth bounded domains with non-isothermal diffuse reflection. We construct a stationary state, prove its perturbative uniqueness and global nonlinear stability, and establish exponential convergence when the wall temperature approaches its stationary profile exponentially. We also establish stationary and global nonlinear well-posedness for prescribed inflow, together with asymptotic stability. The analysis combines a critical kinetic integrability gain with finite-exponent velocity-gradient estimates near grazing, allowing the nonlinear Coulomb estimates to close without $L_x^\infty$ control of velocity gradients.

papers.title: A New Modifications of the Milstein and Euler Methods and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
papers.abstract: The article presents a new modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the author in 2006. The article also provides a modification of the Euler method and the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients. The convergence rates of the proposed modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods are established.

papers.title: Minimum-Energy Control for Stochastic Linear Systems: A Data-Driven Approach with Finite-Sample Guarantees
papers.abstract: The open-loop minimum-energy control (MEC) problem asks for control inputs that minimize the control energy while ensuring the terminal state reaches a desired value. In this paper, we study the open-loop MEC problem for stochastic linear time-invariant systems. We consider a variety of stochastic constraints that enforce the terminal error to be small, and show that Stochastic MEC (SMEC) problem can be formulated as a QCQP. We obtain the optimal solution for SMEC and show that it generalizes the well-known Deterministic MEC problem by introducing novel stochastic variants of controllability and Gramian matrices. When the system dynamics is unknown, we obtain a direct data-driven solution to the SMEC problem using maximum-likelihood estimation and conformal calibration approaches. Finally, we quantify the sub-optimality and constraint violation of our data-driven solutions via finite-sample high-probability upper bounds, and highlight their dependence on the number of experiments, system dimension, and noise-to-signal ratio. We present numerical simulations to validate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Zero-free half-planes for Hecke $L$-functions over number fields and Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: In [Liu26a], varying the length and moment parameters in the cubic-theta argument of [Ope26a] gave the zero-free half-plane $Re(s)>B_{\mathrm{new}}=0.874957019420098946\ldots$ for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and for Dirichlet $L$-functions, and its optimality in the specified exponent comparison system. In this paper, we extend the argument to finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over cyclotomic fields containing $μ_{12}$ and, by class-field descent, to every pair $(K,η)$ whose cyclic class field has metabelian normal closure over $\mathbb Q$, including every finite-order character over every abelian number field. Then, adapting the averaged numerator estimate developed by Xu and Sang [XS26] for Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and combining it with a limiting contradiction argument, we obtain the boundary $B_\flat=0.874886647039964\ldots$, the root near $0.8749$ of $133488B^4-376596B^3+384534B^2-167541B+26231$; it is the exact infimum of the refined comparison system, unattained by finite chains starting above it. Since the analytic argument uses only $μ_{12}\subset F$, we run it over $F=K(ζ_{12})$ for an arbitrary number field $K$ and descend: every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over every number field is zero-free for $Re(s)>B_\flat$, giving a uniform Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis over number fields. The analytic argument uses the exceptional-theta constructions and local calculations of the preprint [Ope26b].

papers.title: FOMTools: Development and AI-Assisted Code Generation for First-Order Methods
papers.abstract: We present FOMTools, an open-source Python package for developing, analyzing, and deploying first-order algorithms for parametric linear and convex quadratic optimization. The user specifies an iteration in Python, with syntax close to its mathematical description. The package represents the iteration as a computation graph of affine and piecewise affine operations. To analyze worst-case performance, FOMTools formulates a mixed-integer verification problem that maximizes a convergence residual over a specified set of problem instances and initial iterates. For probabilistic performance analysis, a batched GPU simulator collects algorithm trajectories and computes statistical bounds on the probability of exceeding a specified convergence tolerance. From the same algorithm description, FOMTools generates specialized solver code for embedded hardware, multicore CPUs, and GPUs. The package first generates the numerical data, factorizations, and matrix-vector routines without any agent. A coding agent then translates the iteration into C or CUDA code and iteratively optimizes the implementation. After each phase, the package runs the generated code on sampled inputs and compares it with a reference execution. FOMTools also serves as a CVXPYgen backend, generating and optimizing solvers for parametric CVXPY problems. We demonstrate FOMTools on sparse coding, network optimization, optimal control, and portfolio rebalancing. The verification bounds reveal worst-case behavior that sampling misses. The generated solvers run up to two orders of magnitude faster than NumPy implementations, and they outperform hand-written GPU code and the OSQP solvers generated by CVXPYgen.

papers.title: On the hyperplane conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the hyperplane conjecture, proposed by Hosono, Lian, and Yau in arXiv:alg-geom/9511001, for Batyrev's mirror pairs of Calabi--Yau hypersurfaces and its orbifold generalization, without assuming that the lattice points in the defining reflexive polytope generate the ambient lattice. We then identify the pushforward of the extended hypersurface \(I\)-function with a generating series of normalized compact periods of the mirror, providing a period interpretation of the hypergeometric series governing ambient genus-zero orbifold Gromov--Witten theory. As an application of our method, we also identify the residue of the Gauss--Manin connection and the cup product morphism on the \(A\)-side.

papers.title: The Bourgain, Brezis, Mironescu localization for deterministic obstacle problems
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of families of fractional energies normalized according to the Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu formula and defined on functions satisfying a pinning condition on possibly aperiodic families of small obstacles. The result of the simultaneous limit depends crucially on the critical rescaling chosen for the obstacles.

papers.title: Sums of two dependent uniform random variables: a characterization by joint tail bounds
papers.abstract: Which laws can the sum of two uniform random variables have when nothing is known about how they depend on each other? For three or more uniform summands, convex order gives the answer; for two it does not, and the question has been open. We show that the attainable laws are exactly those that satisfy a family of explicit joint bounds on sums of tail probabilities, one bound for each finite set of thresholds. For laws with a density at most one, convex order alone decides. For densities at most two, convex order implies the simplest of the joint bounds, and the constant two cannot be raised for single-threshold bounds. The number of thresholds a law needs is set by the spacing of its atoms, not by how many atoms it has.

papers.title: Mahler Method and Vanishing Theorem
papers.abstract: This paper is motivated by the recent work of Adamczewski and Faverjon [5], who established the algebraic independence of values of Mahler functions satisfying linear functional equations. While their work is a landmark result, some proofs are long and complex. The primary aim of this paper is to simplify those proofs and provide new applications. In their proofs, a vanishing theorem for polynomials, rather than power series, is sufficient. We give a proof of the vanishing theorem without using Szemerédi's theorem or Corvaja-Zannier's theorem. In the case of a single transformation, we present a refined vanishing theorem, which allows us to simplify the proof of algebraic independence. We also provide an elementary proof of a vanishing theorem for $q_i$-Mahler functions with various $q_i$. As an application, we prove the algebraic independence of certain continued fractions, extending previous results by Hančl, Adamczewski, and Bundschuh and Väänänen in which only linear independence and transcendence had been established.

papers.title: Observing minimal submanifolds with isolated singularities on open sets of metrics
papers.abstract: We develop a perturbative theory for minimal submanifolds with only (strongly) isolated singularities, with respect to varying background Riemannian metrics. As an application, we obtain a general "sporadic persistence" criterion, thus naturally complementing the non-persistence theorem by the authors. In particular, such a criterion is satisfied by the spherical suspension in $\mathbb{S}^{3m+2}$ of the Veronese embedding of $\mathbb{K}\mathbb{P}^2$ for $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C},\mathbb{H},\mathbb{O}$ (the normed division algebras) in the round spheres of dimension $3m+1=4,7,13,25$ respectively, thereby providing families of continuously varying $(2m+1)$-dimensional stationary varifolds with isolated singularities that are observable on an open set of metrics. By our previous results, these phenomena cannot possibly occur in the codimension one scenario.

papers.title: Postnikov invariants for rational spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper we construct a theory of Postnikov invariants for (complete) homotopy Lie algebras that is preserved by the integration functor of Robert-Nicoud and Vallette. This result is in the same vein as Berglund's theorem, which relates the homology groups underlying a nilpotent homotopy Lie algebra to the homotopy groups of the associated space. We then deduce an integration functor from filtered Chevalley-Eilenberg cohomology groups to group cohomology groups.

papers.title: Uniform $L^2$-bounds for the $n$-th Calderón commutator on Lipschitz graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every real Lipschitz function $A$ and every integer $n\ge1$, $\|T_{A,n}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})}\le C\,\|A'\|_\infty^n$, where $T_{A,n}$ is the $n$-th Calderón commutator and $C$ is an absolute constant.

papers.title: Endpoint regularity of Radon transforms associated with real analytic phases in the plane
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the endpoint Sobolev regularity of Radon transforms associated with real-analytic functions in the plane. We establish all of the failure of endpoint regularity for real-analytic phases. On the one hand, the critical endpoint regularity $L^p(\mathbb{R}^2)\rightarrow L^p_s(\mathbb{R}^2)$, corresponding to extreme points of the reduced Newton polyhedron of phase function, is true if only and only if $p=2$. For generic extreme points, this failure of endpoint regularity generalizes a result of Christ \cite{christ}. On the other hand, we find that the endpoint Sobolev regularity also fails on a bounded segment of the reduced Newton polyhedron when the bisectrix $y=x$ intersects one of unbounded faces at a relative interior point. In particular, our results imply that the Radon transform is not bounded from $L^p$ into $L^p_{1/n}$ with $p=n/(n-1)$ or $p=n$, where the phase functions are real-valued homogeneous polynomials $S(x,y)=a_1x^{n-1}y+a_2x^{n-2}y^2+\cdots+a_{n-1}xy^{n-1}$ with $n\geq 3$ and $a_1a_{n-1}\neq0$. This answers a problem of Phong and Stein in 1994. Moreover, the main results of this paper also give examples which show failure of critical Sobolev regularity for degenerate Fourier integral operators satisfying finite type conditions formulated in \cite{Seeger93,seeger2}. Based on earlier results and our proof of several remaining cases, we conclude that all of other critical endpoint Sobolev estimates are true for Radon transforms associated with real-analytic phases in the plane. Therefore, all failures of endpoint regularity estimates are clearly determined.

papers.title: Modified support measures and Alexandrov-Fenchel type inequalities for nonsmooth h-convex bodies in hyperbolic space
papers.abstract: We establish the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality and its modified version for arbitrary, possibly nonsmooth, horospherically convex bodies in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}, n\geq 2$, and prove that equality in each inequality holds if and only if the h-convex body is a geodesic ball. A key ingredient is a rigidity theorem characterizing geodesic balls via proportionality between modified support measures of adjacent orders. Its proof combines the $C^{1,α}\cap W^{2,k+1}$ approximation of the outer parallel hypersurfaces by smooth strictly h-convex hypersurfaces with the estimates for the total variation norm of the signed measure associated with the proportionality relation along the shifted curvature flows independent of initial curvature bounds. For $0\leq k\leq n-1$, we construct weak flows preserving the $k$-th modified quermassintegral $\tilde{W}_k$ with arbitrary h-convex initial bodies as Hausdorff limits of the smooth flows. The rigidity theorem above characterizes the limit shape of the flow and gives a positive lower bound on the rate of decrease of $\tilde{W}_{k+1}$ for a short time whenever the initial h-convex body is not a geodesic ball, which characterizes the equality cases in the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality. For the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality, we establish the Hausdorff stability independent of curvature bounds described by the Alexandrov-Fenchel deficits for h-convex bodies, which characterizes the equality cases in the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality.

papers.title: Ray class groups in the cyclotomic tower
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $Σ$ be a nonempty finite set of rational primes different from $p$. In the cyclotomic tower $\mathbb{Q}(μ_{p^{n+1}})$, we determine the kernels of the natural maps from the minus $p$-primary ray class groups, with modulus the product of the primes above $Σ$, to the corresponding ordinary minus $p$-primary class groups. We give their character components and elementary divisors at every finite layer, including the layers before splitting stabilizes. In the norm inverse limit, we obtain an explicit integral cyclic decomposition of the local module modulo the single diagonal global Tate module. Its coinvariants recover the finite local kernels. Together with ordinary class-group control, this gives exact control for the minus ray class groups. We identify the local Frobenius factors with Bernoulli regularization factors. For nonexceptional characters, the classical main conjecture then yields regularized measure generators of the ray class characteristic ideals. The exceptional Teichmüller component is treated without the main conjecture: the single Tate correction corresponds to the single pole of the $p$-adic zeta function. At the bottom layer, the local calculation and Herbrand--Ribet yield characterwise nonvanishing criteria involving regularized Bernoulli values. For a single auxiliary prime, the exceptional component detects the Wieferich condition. We also deduce Eisenstein congruence consequences from existing modular-form theorems.

papers.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses: On Smale's sixth problem
papers.abstract: Combining local boundary analysis, algebraic curves and the computational statements specified in the appendix, we prove that the planar Newtonian five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to rotation, translation and scaling for every choice of positive masses. This gives the five-body statement of Smale's sixth problem. We use the singular-sequence classification of Albouy and Kaloshin and resolve the corresponding boundary equations through weighted blow-up charts, rank calculations and local compatibility conditions. For the two remaining diagrams, we prove that the product $Δ$ of all squared mutual distances vanishes. On a hypothetical solution curve containing a positive arc, a pole of a four-product therefore gives a zero of $Δ$. A pole of $Δ$ elsewhere on the completed curve, together with $Δ^4=\prod_{i<j}p_{ij}$, then contradicts the same local vanishing result. The computational statements for Diagrams~2, 3 and~6 involve exact algebra, interval arithmetic and ball arithmetic.

papers.title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: The 2005 polygon conjecture fails for all orders above four
papers.abstract: Let $Λ_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$, equivalently, of stochastic $n\times n$ matrices with off-diagonal entries at most $\frac1n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $Λ_n=S_n$; this holds for $n\le3$. We show that the conjecture fails for every $n\ge5$. The vertices of $S_n$ are eigenvalues of circulant Laplacians built from powers of the directed $n$-cycle. To first order, no perturbation of these circulants moves such an eigenvalue out of $S_n$; however, adding chords with nonconstant weights moves it along an edge of $S_n$ to first order and, with an explicit coefficient, beyond the supporting line of this edge to second order. Consequently, every edge of $S_n$ not incident to $0$ or $1$ contains interior points of $Λ_n$, except possibly, for even $n$, the two horizontal edges, whereas the four edges incident to $0$ or $1$ lie on $\partialΛ_n$. For $n=4$, whose only other edges are horizontal, the question was left open in the previous versions; it has since been settled, $Λ_4=S_4$, by a computer-assisted proof of L. Marshall, after an earlier claim by D.Z. Liu, who also proved that $Λ_n$ is not convex for $n\ge5$. We certify an explicit weighted counterexample for $n=5$, lying only $1.5\cdot10^{-3}$ outside $S_5$, and an unweighted one for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with a duplicated vertex. Its eigenvalue outside $S_7$ is also an eigenvalue of the two-chord digraph that ends the above perturbation; for the analogous digraphs of order $n$, the excess is asymptotic to $\frac{π^2}{2n^4}$. We also observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, describe $Λ_n$ in terms of eigenvectors, and prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness of radial bound states with prescribed number of nodes for nonlinear dispersive equations on spherically symmetric manifolds
papers.abstract: Standing waves $e^{iωt}u(x)$ of nonlinear dispersive equations, such as the nonlinear Schrödinger and Klein--Gordon equations, have a profile $u$ that solves the semilinear elliptic equation $Δu+f(u)=0$. We prove the existence of radial bound states with a prescribed number of nodal surfaces for this equation on a large class of spherically symmetric manifolds and for a broad class of nonlinearities $f$. Under further assumptions on the metric, we prove uniqueness of such bound states for the model nonlinearity $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u-u$. Both existence and uniqueness results apply to the hyperbolic spaces $\mathbb{H}^n_λ$ of any curvature $-λ^2$ and dimension $n\geq 3$, and to some manifolds with a singularity at the origin.

papers.title: Gaussian inequalities with different covariance matrices - the Heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality
papers.abstract: We establish the following novel heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality (involving general covariance matrices $Σ_1,Σ_2,Γ$) for origin-symmetric convex sets $K,L \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and $p,λ\in (0,1)$: \[ γ_{Σ_1}(K)^{1-p} γ_{Σ_2}(L)^p \le \left( \left( \frac{1-p}{1-λ} \right)^{1-p} \left( \frac{p}λ \right)^p \right)^{n} γ_Γ((1-λ) K + λL) , \] whenever $Γ\leq Σ_1 \sharp_p Σ_2$, the $p$-geometric mean of $Σ_1,Σ_2$. This immediately implies both the dimensional Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality of Eskenazis-Moschidis (by using $Σ_1 = Σ_2 = Γ$ and optimizing over $p$) and the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem of Cordero-Erausquin-Fradelizi-Maurey (by using $K=L$, $p=λ$ and diagonal covariances), fusing them into a single unified statement. In fact, the inequality applies to convex sets whose appropriate Gaussian barycenter is at the origin. Furthermore, it reveals a new *bilinear* version of the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem (involving *two* convex sets); in particular, for all $a,b > 0$ and $λ\in [0,1]$: \[ γ(a K)^{1-λ} γ(b L)^λ \leq γ\left ( a^{1-λ} b^λ\left ((1-λ) K + λL \right) \right ) . \] A more general heterovariant version of the (bilinear) (B)-theorem replaces dilation by general linear transformations. A different version yields a heterovariant form of the recently established Gaussian conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequality. By averaging these Gaussian inequalities with respect to the covariance matrices, we obtain dimensional Brunn-Minkowski and conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequalities for Gaussian mixtures. The proofs are based on the Gaussian Forward-Reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequality established in our previous work.

papers.title: A shape theorem for a radially excited random walk in dimensions $d \ge 2$
papers.abstract: NOTE (October 2026): This paper has been superseded by the joint paper "Limit shapes for centrally excited walks", by Ahmed Bou-Rabee, Tuan-Minh Nguyen, Yuval Peres and Arvind Singh (arXiv:2610.10162), which brings together the results and ideas of three independent drafts. We consider a once-excited random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d \ge 2$, where the walk on its first visit has a bias of constant strength $β>0$ toward the origin and moves like a simple symmetric random walk on subsequent visits to that site. We show that the walk is recurrent and prove an almost sure spherical shape theorem: the trace after $n$ steps is asymptotically a Euclidean ball centered at the origin, with radius proportional to $n^{1/(d+1)}$, and the local times have an asymptotically conical profile. This result confirms a conjecture of Kozma (2007) on the shape of the trace for this model.

papers.title: Scalar curvature bounds and tangent cones for Kähler--Ricci shrinkers
papers.abstract: We prove a uniform scalar curvature bound, depending only on the dimension, for Kähler--Ricci shrinkers. We also prove that every noncompact Kähler--Ricci shrinker has a unique tangent cone at infinity, naturally homeomorphic to the base of its polarized Fano fibration. For shrinkers with maximal volume growth, this cone is isometric to the metric completion of the regular part equipped with the intrinsic distance induced by the limiting Kähler metric.

papers.title: Classification of commutation relation for multi-chordal SLE
papers.abstract: We classify the linear solution spaces of the chordal Belavin--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (BPZ) equations, which arise in Dubédat's commutation relations for multiple Schramm--Loewner evolutions (SLE). Without imposing growth conditions, we determine the subspaces selected by successive conformal Ward identities and their exact dimensions. For every $κ>0$ and BPZ spectral parameter $λ\in\mathbb{R}$, we determine the spectrum and Jordan structure of the translation operator. When $λ=0$ and $κ\in(0,8)$, we further determine all admissible scaling exponents and the dimensions of the corresponding translation-invariant solution spaces. A triangular change of derivative coordinates yields a first-order system of rational Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov type, allowing us to represent the Ward operators explicitly and reduce the classification to finite-dimensional linear algebra. For $2N$ boundary points and $κ\in(0,8)$, translation-invariant BPZ solutions with $λ=0$ and the homogeneity required by Möbius covariance automatically satisfy the third Ward identity and the usual power-law bound. This recovers, under weaker assumptions, the Catalan dimension formula previously established by Flores and Kleban. At $κ=8$, the third Ward identity imposes an additional constraint when $N\ge2$, but the full Möbius-covariant solution space still has Catalan dimension, establishing completeness of the partition functions constructed from uniform spanning trees. Finally, at $κ=4$ and $λ>0$, we construct an explicit basis of positive BPZ solutions and identify its elements as partition functions for level lines of a Gaussian free field with suitable harmonic means.

papers.title: Flow Matching for Fast Posterior Sampling in Bayesian Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Sampling from the posterior is the central task of computational Bayesian inverse problems. The standard workhorse in Bayesian inference---Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)---is sequential, yields correlated samples, and must be rerun for each new observation. Conditional flow matching offers an amortized alternative: a transport map, trained once on joint samples of parameter and data, that yields independent approximate posterior samples for any observation at negligible online cost, without new likelihood evaluations. We give a careful, MCMC-literate assessment of flow matching for PDE-based inverse problems with function-valued parameters. Exploiting the flow's tractable density, we derive computable accuracy estimates for the learned posterior in total variation distance and Kullback--Leibler divergence and, moreover, propose a hybrid sampler that is made asymptotically exact by Metropolization. We validate the accuracy estimates and demonstrate amortization in several numerical examples, including electrical impedance tomography and a likelihood-free Lotka--Volterra model. Flow matching reproduces posterior means and credible bands closely at a fraction of the forward solves required by MCMC, but its accuracy degrades for concentrated posteriors and for observations that are atypical under the prior.

papers.title: Sections, pseudosections, and multisections of Lefschetz fibrations
papers.abstract: We show that not every symplectic Lefschetz fibration over the $2$--sphere admits a smooth section, settling a long-standing open problem. To prove this, we develop a method for studying sections via lifts of monodromy factorizations with point-pushing maps and the induced handle decomposition of the total space, and apply it to an infinite family of Lefschetz fibrations. In contrast, we show that every Lefschetz fibration over $S^2$ admits positive multisections. Some of these examples admit no multisections with spherical components. We also construct signature-zero Lefschetz fibrations of every odd genus $g\geq 7$, which in turn give symplectic Lefschetz fibrations of any prescribed signature in each of these genera.

papers.title: A new proof of characteristic-free Knörrer periodicity
papers.abstract: Let $R = S/(f)$ be a complete local hypersurface ring and let $A = S[\![u,v]\!]/(f+uv)$. Pfister and Popescu showed that the stable categories of maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules over $R$ and over $A$ are equivalent, with no assumption on the characteristic. We give a short proof. If $(Φ,Ψ)$ is a matrix factorization of $h$ and $\partial$ is a derivation, then $(\partialΨ,\partialΦ)$ is a null-homotopy for multiplication by $\partial h$. Since $u$ and $v$ are partial derivatives of $f+uv$, they act as zero on the stable category of $A$, so the Koszul complex on $u$ and $v$ splits in the singularity category, and this gives density. For the double branched cover $S[\![z]\!]/(f+z^2)$ the same argument yields $2z$: it recovers Knörrer's lemma up to free summands on the double branched cover when $2$ is a unit, and we show by an example that this lemma, and periodicity for the iterated double branched cover $S[\![z,w]\!]/(f+z^2+w^2)$, fail in characteristic two. We also compute the second syzygy over $A$ of a maximal Cohen-Macaulay $R$-module by an explicit resolution, and show that the change of basis used there cannot be given by a universal matrix formula.

papers.title: Uniqueness of four-body convex central configurations for all masses
papers.abstract: We prove that for every choice of four positive masses and every cyclic ordering of the bodies there is exactly one strictly convex planar central configuration with that ordering, up to similarity. This proves a conjecture of Albouy, Fu and Sun, also called the Simó-Yoccoz conjecture, and answers Problem 10 in the list of Albouy, Cabral and Santos. Uniqueness follows by a covering argument from the nondegeneracy of these configurations. We prove nondegeneracy by hand: Dziobek's relations reduce it to an eigenvalue bound for a $2\times2$ matrix that depends only on the shape of the configuration. As consequences, every degenerate planar four-body central configuration is concave, and the known symmetry theorems for kites, isosceles trapezoids and rhombi follow in a few lines.

papers.title: Online Stochastic Allocation with Increasing Returns
papers.abstract: We study online allocation with increasing returns, where an uncertain number of customers arrive sequentially and can be irrevocably assigned to any product with remaining capacity. Each assignment earns a base reward plus a bonus that is nondecreasing in the number of previous assignments to the same product. Prior work has focused primarily on fixed or diminishing returns. Under increasing returns, the central challenge is that concentrating assignments can unlock large future rewards, while a different product may be preferable if arrivals stop early. We show that classical approaches, including greedy and natural LP-based rounding algorithms, can perform arbitrarily poorly, even with homogeneous bonuses. We evaluate performance through competitive ratios relative to the hindsight offline optimum. For homogeneous bonuses, we establish a tight competitive ratio of $1/2$. For arbitrary heterogeneous bonuses, however, no online algorithm can guarantee a competitive ratio greater than $1/m$, where $m$ is the number of products. By imposing discrete concavity on the bonus functions, we limit the concentration of rewards in later assignments and restore constant guarantees. Under this structure, we develop a re-solving framework that repeatedly selects a planning horizon, constructs a feasible allocation plan from the current state, and executes its assignments in a specific order. For arbitrary arrival distributions, we design distribution-oblivious deterministic and randomized algorithms with competitive ratios of $0.2537$ and $0.3864$, respectively. For known increasing-failure-rate (IFR) arrival distributions, we exploit distributional information to obtain a deterministic $1/2$-competitive algorithm.

papers.title: A short proof of Bernstein's theorem via the Omori--Yau maximum principle
papers.abstract: We give a short, self-contained proof of Bernstein's theorem: every entire minimal graph in $R^3$ is a plane. The only global tool is the Omori-Yau maximum principle, which holds on entire minimal graphs with their induced metric. We apply it exactly once to a single explicit function $F$ built from the surface's angle function and principal curvatures. A pointwise differential inequality for $F$, combined with the Omori-Yau principle, forces it to attain its minimum value everywhere, which yields the planarity of the surface and hence Bernstein's theorem. As a by-product of our approach, we show that the same method, with a different function and with some extra work, also proves in a simple and self-contained way the generalization of Bernstein's theorem given by Osserman that a complete minimal surface in $R^3$ whose normals omit a neighbourhood of some direction must be a plane.

papers.title: Lower Bounds for Localised Moments of Automorphic $L$-functions
papers.abstract: In this article, we describe a method to obtain lower bounds for the $2k$-th moment of values of $L$-functions localised at the central point for all real $k > 0$. In particular, for the families of quadratic twists of self-dual irreducible unitary cuspidal automorphic representations of $\operatorname{GL}_D(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$ with $D\in\{2,3,4\}$, our results are new in the range $0<k<\tfrac12$ when $D\in\{2,3\}$, and new for all $k>0$ when $D=4$.

papers.title: Discrete Mixed Quantization for Cat Maps
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a mixed quantization technique for graph vector bundles that combines semiclassical analysis and quantum cat maps. We apply it to study the Kesten--McKay law and quantum ergodicity.

papers.title: Bounds for Unions of Several Parts in Balanced Graph Partitions
papers.abstract: Let $k\ge3$ and $1\le \ell\le k-1$. We study balanced $k$-partitions of a graph for which the union of any $\ell$ parts induces few edges. We show that every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges admits a balanced partition $V_1,\ldots,V_k$ such that \begin{equation*} \max_{\substack{A\in\binom{[k]}{\ell}}}e_G\left(\bigcup_{i\in A}V_i\right)\le\frac{\ell^2}{k^2}m+\frac{\ell^2(k-\ell)}{k^2}(n-1)+\frac{\ell(k-\ell)}{k(k-1)}\sqrt{\left(\binom{k}{\ell}-1\right)m}. \end{equation*} In the case $\ell=2$, our result confirms a conjecture of Bollobás and Scott in a stronger form.

papers.title: Exact Traces for Vector-Valued Morrey Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish an exact trace theorem for vector-valued time-Morrey spaces and complementary continuity theorems for time-BMO evolution classes. For a Banach couple $X_1\hookrightarrow X_0$, $1<p<\infty$ and $0<λ<1$, we prove that the trace of the class $u\in\mathcal M^{p,λ}(X_1)$, $u_t\in\mathcal M^{p,λ}(X_0)$ is exactly $(X_0,X_1)_{θ,\infty}$, where $θ=1-(1-λ)/p$. A constructive extension realizes every admissible trace, and counterexamples establish optimality of both the smoothness exponent and the weak fine index. Time-BMO control yields continuous finite-index interpolation traces and, under a mixed boundedness hypothesis, a logarithmic time modulus whose base-space logarithm is necessary. For the quadratic viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation on the torus, we characterize the bounded initial data generating Morrey-regular solutions by the exact Besov condition $u_0\in B_{2,\infty}^{2θ}$. The proof uses Hopf--Cole linearization and a direct composition argument, and requires no smallness assumption. Lacunary nonlinear solutions realize the sharp trace threshold. A forced Hamilton--Jacobi example exhibits genuinely logarithmic time regularity, and a forward--backward mean-field-game system illustrates initial and terminal trace compatibility. \par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} Morrey spaces; trace spaces; real interpolation; Hamilton--Jacobi equations; bounded mean oscillation.

papers.title: Affine reflection transforms of convex polygons with parallel opposite sides
papers.abstract: We study affine reflection transforms of convex polygons with parallel opposite sides. An opposite-side involution sends a pencil through an interior point to a piecewise smooth family of lines. Its completed envelope consists of conic arcs and transition segments. The completed transform has non-positive oriented area. Maximising the negative oriented area and dividing by the polygonal area gives an affine invariant that vanishes precisely for centrally symmetric polygons. Combining an identity for reflected chord vectors with the Rogers--Shephard inequality shows that this invariant is strictly less than $1$, with optimal universal constant $1$. The energy extends continuously to the boundary and vanishes there. We also compare chord counts under compatible smoothing and prove Hausdorff convergence to the smooth transform.

papers.title: Bounds on non-hermite Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information
papers.abstract: We obtain the relation between non-hermite skew information $NI_{ρ,α}(A)$, $NU_{ρ,α}(A)$, variance $NV_ρ(A)$ and $NJ_{ρ,α}(A)$ by using the maximal eigenvalue and the minimal eigenvalue of density $ρ$. And also we obtain their refinements.

papers.title: A Functional Central Limit Theorem for Locally Stationary Time Series in Banach Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish a functional central limit theorem for locally stationary time series in a separable Banach space $B$. The result requires no type-2 or cotype assumptions and thus covers spaces central to functional data analysis, such as $C([0,1])$ and $L^p([0,1])$. Under moment conditions, summable physical dependence coefficients and a bracketing entropy condition controlling the infinite-dimensional tails, the centered partial sum process converges weakly in $D([0,1],B)$ to a centered Gaussian process, whose covariance is the integrated local long-run covariance, an element of the projective tensor product. We also obtain a stochastic integral representation with respect to a cylindrical Brownian motion. As the limit depends on the unknown long-run covariance, we prove consistency of a block multiplier bootstrap for the partial sum process. This yields CUSUM tests for a constant mean of the full process, based on arbitrary continuous seminorms and valid under a time-varying long-run covariance. For linear projections, we derive a self-normalized test with a pivotal limit. In simulations, the supremum norm test detects localized changes that its $L^2$ counterpart largely misses, and applications to EEG and temperature data illustrate the methodology. Examples in $C([0,1])$ and $W^{1,p}_0([0,1])$ show how the entropy condition can be verified.

papers.title: Minimal Products via Weighted Spheres
papers.abstract: We establish an exact composition principle for spherical immersions coupled through coefficient profiles and norm-preserving bilinear maps. Under explicit mixed orthogonality, the spherical mean curvature vector splits into orthogonal input and profile contributions. The composition is minimal if and only if every input is minimal and the profile is $W$-minimal for the induced monomial weight. Tensor iteration allows weighted profiles to serve as inputs in further compositions. At fixed weights, Hsiang--Lawson reduction and Kapouleas--McGrath doubling yield closed embedded $W$-minimal profiles. When the effective exponents tend to infinity in positive limiting proportions, Gaussian transfer produces interior coefficient profiles from closed embedded self-shrinkers that are nondegenerate modulo rotations. The number of distinct corresponding profiles is bounded below by the Lusternik--Schnirelmann category of the rotation orbit.

papers.title: The Smoothability of Embedded Surfaces in 4-Manifolds Under Stabilizations
papers.abstract: We study the smooth stabilization number of a locally flat embedded surface in a smooth $4$-manifold, defined as the minimum number of connected sums with $S^2\times S^2$ needed to make the surface topologically isotopic to a smooth embedding. We prove that a nonsmoothable locally flat surface in a closed, simply connected smooth $4$-manifold becomes smoothable after a single stabilization if its homology class is primitive and noncharacteristic and its complement has abelian fundamental group. This yields infinitely many examples of nonsmoothable surfaces with smooth stabilization number one. We also exhibit examples for which a single stabilization produces infinitely many pairwise smoothly nonisotopic representatives in the same topological isotopy class. In contrast, we construct a locally flat genus-eight surface representing $6h$ in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ whose smooth stabilization number is exactly two. More generally, we show that smooth stabilization numbers of locally flat embedded surfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ are unbounded.

papers.title: The Hibi-Li Face-Number Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the face-number conjecture of Hibi and Li: for every finite poset, the order polytope has no more faces of any given dimension than the chain polytope. More generally, the face numbers increase weakly along the admissible family of chain--order polytopes when one order coordinate is replaced by a chain coordinate. We also prove that, unless the order and chain polytopes are unimodularly equivalent, all face-number inequalities in dimensions $2,\ldots,|P|-1$ are strict.

papers.title: Two-disjoint-cycle-cover edge bipancyclicity in Cartesian products
papers.abstract: For two even integers $r_1\leq r_2$, a graph $G$ of even order is \emph{2-DCC edge $[r_1,r_2]$-bipancyclic} if for every ordered pair $(e,f)$ of independent edges and every even integer $\ell\in[r_1,r_2]$, there exist two vertex-disjoint cycles $C_1$ and $C_2$ with $V(C_1)\cup V(C_2)=V(G)$, $|C_1|=\ell$, $|C_2|=|V(G)|-\ell$, $e\in E(C_1)$, and $f\in E(C_2)$. We study this property for Cartesian products $G=H_1\square\cdots\square H_d$ with $d\geq2$, where each factor is $K_2$ or an even-order bipartite edge-Hamiltonian graph. We prove that $G$ is 2-DCC edge $[4,|V(G)|/2]$-bipancyclic whenever $d\geq4$, and also for $d\in\{2,3\}$ under explicit Hamiltonian-cycle conditions on $H_i$. Here $1\leq i\leq d$. As applications, we give sharp characterizations for undirected toroidal meshes, star-cube networks, and hyperstar networks.

papers.title: Regularity of the Value Function in Multi-Asset Portfolio Selection with Proportional Transaction Costs
papers.abstract: This paper concerns the variational inequality arising from a specific singular control problem: portfolio selection under proportional transaction costs. This variational inequality is a gradient-constrained partial differential equation (PDE). Generally, the literature only guarantees the W^{2, \infty} regularity of the solution to such a PDE, and counterexamples exist for higher regularity. In this paper, by exploiting the concavity of the value function, we connect this gradient-constrained problem to an obstacle problem, and finally show that the solution is C^{2,α} except at the corner points where multiple gradient constraints bind. Especially, if there are two assets, then a global C^{2,α} solution can be guaranteed.

papers.title: Bad Reduction of Genus Two Curves with complex multiplication
papers.abstract: We study genus two curves whose Jacobians have complex multiplication by a biquadratic CM field. In this setting the Jacobian decomposes as a product of two elliptic curves with complex multiplication by orders in the same imaginary quadratic field. We derive upper bounds for the primes of stable bad reduction of such curves in terms of the discriminants of the CM orders. To do so, we give an explicit description of principally polarized abelian surfaces with CM by a biquadratic field via small CM cycles on an orthogonal Shimura variety of signature (3,2). We use it to prove an arithmetic intersection formula between such CM cycles with Humbert surfaces in terms of coefficients of incoherent Eisenstein series and representation numbers of ternary positive definite quadratic forms. Finally, employing the arithmetic properties of higher Green functions, we show that primes of stable bad reduction always exist.

papers.title: Limit shape, avalanches, and stabilisation of abelian sandpiles on comb lattices
papers.abstract: We study two aspects of the abelian sandpile model on comb lattices. First, we prove that the infinite-volume limit of the stationary measures is supported on the saturated configuration. We then investigate the shape of avalanches induced by adding a particle at the origin in finite boxes of size $(2n+1)\times(2n+1)$ around the origin. In the stationary distribution on these finite boxes, we show that avalanches reach the boundary along the vertical teeth with probability tending to $1$, while the horizontal spread is of order $\sqrt{n}$. Finally, we establish that the single-source limit shape for abelian sandpiles on the comb lattice agrees with the corresponding limit shapes for the divisible sandpile, internal diffusion-limited aggregation (IDLA), and rotor-router aggregation models. This establishes limit shape universality on the comb lattice.

papers.title: A Note on a Result of Chen Li: the Thinning Problem via the Kernel Method
papers.abstract: Recently, C. Li posted a preprint that resolves the fractional version of Talagrand's discrete convexity problem. In this note, we use the method of C. Li to answer another problem of Talagrand.

papers.title: Existence and Regularity of Stable Resonant Spectral Submanifolds and Linearization Maps
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of $C^{r_{*},α}$-regular sub-stable invariant manifolds and conjugacies for analytic maps near a fixed point in the presence of resonances, assuming an invertible semisimple linearization. The regularity order $r$ and the admissible Hölder exponents $α$ depend on the resonant indices and the relative rates of contraction. Our approach uses functional expansions based on logarithmic polynomials, which allow the invariance equation to be solved explicitly and algorithmically to arbitrary order. The existence results are obtained via a fixed-point argument in a suitable Banach space. We further present several analytic examples that illustrate the theorem and demonstrate the loss of regularity caused by resonances.

papers.title: Iterative Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) distillation can propagate teacher bias under covariate shift when target reward feedback is unavailable. We propose Iterative Calibration and Learning (IterCaL), which alternates source-reward teacher calibration through token-level branching with student learning on target prompts. We prove polynomial convergence in expected average KL to the oracle student, the reference-regularized target-reward maximizer within a potentially misspecified student class; a quantified source-to-target calibration discrepancy gives an explicit additive true-return term. Our separation shows that regularized direct teacher matching retains positive oracle-KL error at its population optimum for every shared reference penalty, even when the teacher is stronger than every student. On the same instance, IterCaL converges to the oracle using source rewards alone.

papers.title: On the largest prime factors less than $y$ of consecutive shifted primes
papers.abstract: For an integer $n > 1$, let $P^+(n)$ be the largest prime factor of $n$, and let $P_y^+(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$ not exceeding $y$. One of Erdős and Turán's conjectures asserts that the asymptotic density of integers $n$ satisfying $P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)$ is $1/2$. Furthermore, Wang conjectures that for $x\rightarrow\infty$, one has $\#\{p\leq x:P^+(p-1)<P^+(p+1)\}\sim π(x)/2$. In this paper, we show the following results. For any $3\leq y\ll x^{o(1)}$, for $x\rightarrow\infty$, we have \begin{align*} &\#\{n\leq x:P^+_y(n)<P^+_y(n+1)\}\sim \frac{1}{2}x, \\&\#\{p\leq x:P^+_y(p-1)<P^+_y(p+1)\}\sim \frac{1}{2}π(x), \end{align*} where the first result extends a previous range $3\leq y\ll \exp(\log x/(100\log\log x))$ due to Rivat (2001). For any $0<α<17/32$, let $y=x^α$. Then there exists $h(α)>0$ such that \begin{align*} \#\{p\leq x:P_y^+(p-1)<P_y^+(p+1)\}\geq(h(α)+o(1))π(x). \end{align*} In particular, the function $h$ satisfies $\lim_{α\rightarrow 0^+}h(α)=1/2$. Similar result also holds for $\#\{n\leq x:P_y^+(n)<P_y^+(n+1)\}$, which improves a previous result $\lim_{α\rightarrow 0^+} h(α)=1/4$ due to Wang (2019).

papers.title: On the Complexity of Finding Fixed Points for Set-Valued Contractions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the computational complexity of finding fixed points for set-valued contractions. We first formulate a computational problem for Nadler's fixed-point theorem: Projected-Nadler, and prove that it is $\mathsf{CLS}$-complete by showing its equivalence to Continuous-LocalOpt. We then establish a stronger converse for Nadler's fixed point theorem that can be applied as a tool to analyze the convergence rate of set-valued basic iteration procedure. Finally, we reduce large-margin triplet stationarity problem to Projected-Nadler. Together with its $\mathsf{CLS}$-hardness introduced in [arXiv:2509.16898], this yields $\mathsf{CLS}$-completeness of large-margin triplet stationarity.

papers.title: Duality and Baire like properties in topological abelian groups
papers.abstract: This article investigates the duality of abelian topological groups by delving into the interplay between the algebraic and topological properties of a group $G$ and those of its dual group. In particular, extending the notion of a $g$-barrelled group, we introduce and study the classes of $κ$-barrelled and $ω$-barrelled groups. Our first main result establishes that every $ω$-barrelled group is $\aleph_0$-barrelled (i.e., if every weakly convergent sequence in the dual group is equicontinuous, then every metrizable weakly compact subset of the dual group is also equicontinuous). From this, we deduce that the free topological abelian group $A(K)$ over a metrizable compact space $K$ is determined by the subgroup generated by any of its dense subsets. Furthermore, we prove that if $G$ is a $σ$-compact, $ω$-barrelled group, then its dual group $\widehat{G}_κ$ equipped with the compact-open topology is sequentially complete (complete if $G$ is hemicompact). We also solve an open question posed by Trigos-Arrieta by constructing an explicit example of an $ω$-barrelled metrizable group that fails to be $g$-barrelled. Finally, we investigate the dualization of groups lacking infinite compact subsets, proving that for a totally bounded abelian group $G$, every compact subset of $G$ is finite if and only if its dual group $\widehat{G}$, endowed with the finite-open topology, is unordered Baire-like.

papers.title: First-Derivative Chromatic Symmetric Reconstruction For Proper Trees
papers.abstract: Richard Stanley asked whether every tree $T$ is determined up to isomorphism by its chromatic symmetric function $X_T$. We approach this open problem by regarding $X_T$ as a polynomial in the power-sum symmetric functions $p_1, p_2, \dots$ and studying the invariant $Φ_T = \left.\frac{\partial {X_T}}{\partial p_1}\right\rvert_{p_1 = 0}$. We prove that $Φ_T$ distinguishes, among proper trees, every proper tree in which any non-leaf vertex with two or more non-leaf neighbors has a number of leaf neighbors occurring at no other non-leaf vertex. We give an equivalent formulation of Stanley's question in terms of $Φ_T$. Finally, we show that counts of spanning forests with at most $t$ edges cannot distinguish all $k$-vertex trees when $t<\left\lfloor k/2\right\rfloor$, for every $k\ge4$.

papers.title: Verified Linear Programming via Tolerance-Aware Precision Boosting
papers.abstract: Linear programming plays a fundamental role in computer science, with applications in optimization, formal verification, SMT solving, and numerous other domains. When exactness guarantees are required, numerical inaccuracies arising from floating-point arithmetic can compromise soundness, whereas exact rational arithmetic often incurs significant computational overhead. In this paper, we investigate the numerical stability of the simplex algorithm and establish conditions under which a precision-boosting floating-point implementation provably produces the same pivot decisions and final basis as an exact rational implementation, from which the final result is reconstructed and certified exactly. Our analysis shows that correctness depends on both arithmetic precision and a careful handling of numerical tolerances. Based on these results, we develop a tolerance-aware, precision-boosting simplex algorithm with formal correctness guarantees. Finally, we introduce a delta-complete termination criterion that allows the algorithm to terminate once certified upper and lower bounds on the optimal objective differ by at most a user-specified threshold delta, providing a certified, user-controlled optimality gap.

papers.title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
papers.abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ in which $2$ is invertible requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm for multiplication in this algebra costing $O(N \log N)$ arithmetic operations in $R$ and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage when the doubling parameters of $A_n$ are units whose square roots lie in a fixed commutative coefficient algebra $S$ finitely generated as an $R$-module and admitting an $R$-linear map $π\colon S \to R$ with $π(1) = 1$. In particular, over $\mathbb{R}$ and every finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ of odd characteristic, a quadratic field extension contains a square root of every possible doubling parameter, so the algorithm applies to every Cayley-Dickson tower over these fields, and the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ over them is at most $(9n-21)2^n+28$ when $n\ge2$. When the top doubling parameter is a non-square, as in the standard real tower, the bound is $(9n-15)2^{n-1}+10$. To the author's knowledge, the algorithm presented in this paper is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. When $R=\mathbb{R}$ with every doubling parameter equal to $-1$, the real quasilinear schedule uses fewer total arithmetic operations than both direct multiplication and a uniform algorithm of Cariow-Cariowa for $n\ge4$. An implementation for the standard real tower is available in the MIT-licensed C11 library fastCD, with a NumPy-backed Python interface. In single-core benchmarks against direct multiplication and the uniform Cariow-Cariowa method, the quasilinear implementation had the lowest mean time of the three at every tested dimension $N\ge32$, for both single and batched products, and was over $17$ times faster than direct multiplication at $N=1024$.

papers.title: Unimodality shenanigans in Ehrhart theory
papers.abstract: We construct counterexamples to a four-decade-old conjecture attributed to Stanley concerning the unimodality of $h^*$-polynomials of IDP polytopes. As additional applications of our main constructions, we also disprove a conjecture by Brenti on the log-concavity of $h^*$-polynomials of Gorenstein IDP polytopes, and a conjecture by Ferroni and Higashitani concerning the log-concavity of the Ehrhart series of IDP polytopes. We also answer their question about the existence of very ample polytopes with non-log-concave interior Ehrhart series. Our class of examples arises by taking Cayley sums of rectangular prisms, and hence they possess regular unimodular flag triangulations by a result of Haase, Paffenholz, Piechnik and Santos. Remarkably, for the unimodality conjecture we can even find smooth counterexamples.

papers.title: Links and singularities of stable maps from $3$-manifolds to surfaces
papers.abstract: For any two links in the $3$-sphere, we provide a visual construction of a stable map $f$ from the $3$-sphere to the Euclidean plane such that $f$ has no cusp points, the set of definite (resp. indefinite) fold points of $f$ is isotopic to the first (resp. second) given link, and $f$ does not have a certain type of singular fibers. Moreover, we obtain a similar result for any $3$-manifold by setting the target space to the $2$-sphere.

papers.title: The derived length of subgroups of the Cremona group
papers.abstract: We prove that the maximal derived length of a solvable subgroup of the plane Cremona group over $\mathbb C$ is equal to $5$. The main difficulty is the case of subgroups containing loxodromic elements. To treat this case, we prove that the maximal derived length of a finite solvable subgroup is $4$ and establish a centraliser theorem: the centraliser of a finite solvable subgroup of derived length $4$ contains no loxodromic element. The proof of the centraliser theorem relies on Blanc's classification of maximal algebraic subgroups and then uses equivariant Sarkisov theory, orbit estimates, superrigidity, and fixed curves of genus at least two.

papers.title: On a Brunn-Minkowski principle for first-order information functionals
papers.abstract: In this work we present the following general principle: every positive homogeneous functional on an abstract convex cone satisfying a suitable Brunn-Minkowski inequality gives rise to an information functional -defined as the quotient of the functional by its relative surface area- that satisfies a linear Brunn-Minkowski inequality. We also establish the dual counterpart of this principle for functionals satisfying an analogous convexity property, yielding reverse linear Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for the associated information functionals. Furthermore, we show that homogeneity is necessary within this principle by providing a counterexample to the expected result for the information functional associated to the standard Gaussian measure. As applications, we recover, via an alternative first-order argument, a classical result by Giannopoulos, Hartzoulaki and Paouris (2002) for the ratio of two consecutive quermassintegrals, together with a characterization of the equality case. The same argument extends to the setting of mixed discriminants of symmetric positive definite matrices. Finally, our approach yields new extensions of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality of Dembo, Cover and Thomas, for the classical information functional, both to the $L_p$ setting ($p \geq 1$), where the relative surface area is expressed in terms of Lutwak's first $L_p$ quermassintegral, and to the measure-theoretic framework, for measures with homogeneous densities satisfying some concavity. Moreover, we prove that our principle applies also in the context of the Blaschke addition, both in the volume and in the (mixed) affine surface area cases, obtaining new inequalities as an application of it.

papers.title: On the real-rootedness of Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of $(132,213)$-avoiding permutahedra
papers.abstract: Let $P_d$ be the convex hull of the permutations of $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ that avoid the patterns $132$ and $213$, and let $H_d(t)$ be its Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomial. We prove that all zeros of $H_d(t)$ are real and negative for $3\le d\le1000$ and for every $d\ge2^{62}$; for $d\le2$ the polynomial is constant. Expanding $H_d(t)$ in refined Eulerian polynomials does not suffice, since a coordinate is already negative at $d=7$. Let $A_{d,i}(t)$ enumerate all permutations of $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ with first entry $i$ by number of descents.
