Our theoretical results are supported by extensive numerical simulation studies. Further, we present an application to the analysis of a Canadian wildfire dataset.

papers.title: Permutation twisted cohomology, remixed
papers.abstract: For each endotrivial complex for a $p$-group arising from Bredon homology of a representation sphere, we construct $p$-local quasi-isomorphisms, called forerunners. These enable us to extend Balmer--Gallauer's results concerning the tensor-triangular geometry of permutation modules for elementary abelian $p$-groups to all $p$-groups. We construct an open cover of the Balmer spectrum under which all endotrivials are tt-line bundles, that is, every endotrivial is locally isomorphic to a shift of the tensor unit. We define a remixed permutation twisted cohomology ring for which the canonical comparison map from the Balmer spectrum to the homogeneous spectrum of the twisted cohomology ring is injective. If the twisted cohomology ring is Noetherian, the comparison map is an open immersion, and the open cover endows the Balmer spectrum with Dirac scheme structure. We prove Noetherianity holds for Dedekind groups and the dihedral group of order 8, and conjecture it holds for all $p$-groups.

papers.title: On the Blasius-Deligne conjecture for the standard $L$-functions of symplectic type
papers.abstract: The Blasius-Deligne conjecture for automorphic $L$-functions is about the period relations and the algebraicity of critical $L$-values. In this paper, we prove the Blasius-Deligne conjecture for standard $L$-functions attached to regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of $GL_{2n}$ of symplectic type, under the expected Galois invariance condition for these representations. The main results extend the classical work of G. Shimura and Y. Manin from $GL_2$ to $GL_{2n}$, and complete the approach that was initially taken by H. Grobner and A. Raghuram and by F. Januszewski, where a few technical assumptions were taken.

papers.title: Integral Points and Volume of Integral-Integral Affine Manifolds
papers.abstract: Using rational Ehrhart theory and Fourier analysis, we give an elementary proof that the volume of a closed manifold equipped with an integral-integral affine structure equals the number of its integral points.

papers.title: Hierarchical Matrices with Tucker Blocks: Construction and Forward Evaluation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce hierarchical matrices with Tucker blocks (HMTB) for data-sparse approximation of matrices arising from nonoscillatory and mildly oscillatory kernels. Building on the hierarchical matrix framework, HMTB matrices replace conventional low-rank blocks with Tucker representations. Using high-dimensional interpolation and tensor compression and contractions, we develop algorithms for constructing HMTB matrices and performing matrix-vector multiplication. For an $N \times N$ matrix, these algorithms have linear and quasi-linear complexities in $N$, respectively. Numerical comparisons with an interpolation-based $\mathcal{H}$-matrix implementation demonstrate storage savings and, in several cases, reduced construction times, while maintaining competitive forward-evaluation costs. The framework is also applicable to quasi-uniform grids.

papers.title: Coherent configurations and Frobenius structures
papers.abstract: We prove that coherent configurations can be represented as modules over Frobenius structures in the category of real nonnegative matrices. We generalize the notion of admissible morphism from association schemes to coherent configurations. We show that the Frobenius structure associated to a coherent configuration can be modified to become a dagger Frobenius structure, and use this to connect the coherent configurations to groupoids and $H^*$-algebras. We examine the properties of the dagger Frobenius structure with respect to admissible morphisms. We introduce the matrix $O$ obtained as the composition of comultiplication and multiplication of the dagger Frobenius structure and prove that we may obtain the valencies of colors, and thus recover the original coherent configuration, as an eigenvector of $O$. In the last part of the paper, we examine the spectrum of $O$ and apply it to generalize the Lagrange theorem from groups to association schemes.

papers.title: First-order aspects of Artin groups
papers.abstract: We prove several results on the model theory of Artin groups, focusing on Artin groups which are "far from right-angled Artin groups". The first result is that if $C$ is a class of Artin groups whose irreducible components are acylindrically hyperbolic and torsion-free, then the model theory of Artin groups of type $C$ reduces to the model theory of their irreducible components. The second result is that the problem of superstability of a given non-abelian Artin group $A$ reduces to certain dihedral parabolic subgroups of $A$ being $n$-pure in $A$, for certain large enough primes $n \in \mathbb{N}$. The third result is that two spherical Artin groups are elementarily equivalent if and only if they are isomorphic. Finally, we prove that the affine Artin groups of type $\tilde{A}_n$, for $n \geq 4$, can be distinguished from the other simply laced affine Artin groups using existential sentences; this uses known computations of second integral homology together with a direct calculation for simply laced Artin groups under the $K(π,1)$ assumption. These computations provide obstructions to the retractions forced by existential equivalence.

papers.title: Invariant Densities on Cylinders with an Interface: Existence, Uniqueness, and Exponential Asymptotics
papers.abstract: We study the stationary double-divergence equation on the infinite cylinder $\mathbb R\times\mathbb T^{d-1}$, whose coefficients coincide with two possibly different periodic media outside a bounded interface layer. Under the centering conditions for the two periodic media, we construct a positive invariant density that converges exponentially in $C^1$ at each end to a positive multiple of the corresponding periodic invariant density. Every bounded distributional solution is a scalar multiple of this density. The two asymptotic amplitudes are determined by the full interface problem, up to a common normalization. Motivated by the invariant-measure analysis of Hairer and Manson [Ann. Probab. 39(2011) 648-682], our proof uses only PDE methods: a transformation based on the periodic invariant densities, adjoint Neumann problems on finite cylinders, and energy estimates.

papers.title: Rational structures on quivers and a generalization of Gelfand's equivalence
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of rational structure on a quiver and associated representations to establish a coherent framework for studying quiver representations in separable field extensions. This notion is linked to a refinement of the notion of $K$-species, which we term étale $K$-species. We establish a categorical anti-equivalence between $K$-rational quivers and étale $K$-species, which extends to an equivalence of their respective representation categories. For $K$-rational quivers there is a canonical notion of base change, which suggests a corresponding notion of base change for (étale) $K$-species which we elaborate. As a primary application, we generalize Gelfand's celebrated equivalence between certain blocks of Harish-Chandra modules for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and representations of the Gelfand quiver to a rational setting. To this end, we define a $\mathbb{Q}$-rational structure on the Gelfand quiver and its representations. A key technical tool, which we call unipotent stabilization, is developed to construct the functor from rational Harish-Chandra modules to nilpotent rational quiver representations. We prove that this functor is an equivalence. A similar result is established for the cyclic quiver. Both results hold over every field $E$ of characteristic $0$, for suitable $E$-rational structures on the two quivers; for $E=\mathbb{C}$ they recover Gelfand's equivalence. In this rational framework the defining relation of the Gelfand quiver acquires a descent-theoretic meaning: its Galois orbit is stable, it descends to a single relation on the associated $\mathbb{Q}$-species, and a $\mathbb{Q}$-rational representation satisfies it if and only if the composite of the two arrows through the vertex $-$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-rational endomorphism of the space at the central vertex. This allows us to recast our results in the language of $\mathbb{Q}$-species.

papers.title: The first moment of primitive quartic \(L\)-functions with a secondary term
papers.abstract: Let $q\equiv3\pmod4$ be a fixed odd prime power. We study the first moment of central values of primitive quartic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $\F_q[T]$, with fixed genus $g$ and with $χ^2$ primitive. We obtain a main term $C_q q^{2g/3}$ and a secondary term $(α_r g+β_r)q^{g/2}$, with error $O_{q,\eps}(q^{(16/33+\eps)g})$, where $r\equiv g/3+1\pmod4$. The constants are explicit, with $C_q>0$ and $α_r<0$ for every $r$. We use a double Dirichlet series and the functional equation of the quartic Gauss sum generating series to compute the residues and obtain the continuation needed to separate both terms.

papers.title: The evolution equation and the eigenvalue problem for the Laplacian in a regular tree
papers.abstract: In this paper, our main goal is to study the evolution problem associated with the Laplacian operator with Dirichlet boundary conditions on a regular tree. To this end, we place special emphasis on the associated first eigenvalue problem, which provides the fundamental tool for describing the long-time dynamics. First, we prove existence and uniqueness of solutions when the initial condition is compatible with the boundary condition. Next, we address the asymptotic behavior of the solutions and show that they decay to zero exponentially fast. This decay rate is determined by the associated first eigenvalue, which we also analyze in detail.

papers.title: Non-Asymptotic Stability and Consistency Guarantees for Physics-Informed Neural Networks via Coercive Operator Analysis
papers.abstract: We present a unified theoretical framework for analyzing the stability and consistency of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), grounded in operator coercivity, variational formulations, and non-asymptotic perturbation theory. PINNs approximate solutions to partial differential equations (PDEs) by minimizing residual losses over sampled collocation and boundary points. We formalize both operator-level and variational notions of consistency, proving that residual minimization in Sobolev norms leads to convergence in energy and uniform norms under mild regularity. Deterministic stability bounds quantify how bounded perturbations to the network outputs propagate through the full composite loss, while probabilistic concentration results via McDiarmid's inequality yield sample complexity guarantees for residual-based generalization. A unified generalization bound links residual consistency, projection error, and perturbation sensitivity. Empirical results on elliptic, parabolic, and nonlinear PDEs confirm the predictive accuracy of our theoretical bounds across regimes. The framework identifies key structural principles, such as operator coercivity, activation smoothness, and sampling admissibility, that underlie robust and generalizable PINN training, offering principled guidance for the design and analysis of PDE-informed learning systems.

papers.title: $F$-injectivity does not imply $F$-fullness in normal domains
papers.abstract: We construct examples of Noetherian three-dimensional local geometrically normal domains of prime characteristic which are $F$-injective but not $F$-full. Along the way, we find examples of two-dimensional local geometrically normal domains which are $F$-injective but not $F$-anti-nilpotent. A crucial theme of our constructions is the behavior of $F$-injectivity along a purely inseparable finite base change.

papers.title: Rank three representations of Painlevé systems: I. Wild character varieties
papers.abstract: We give explicit cubic equations for the wild character varieties corresponding to the rank 3 representations of Painlevé equations, and compare them to the ones of their classical rank 2 representations.

papers.title: Structure of the Cayley-Dickson algebras
papers.abstract: Viewing the Cayley-Dickson process as a graded construction provides a rigorous definition of associativity consisting of three classes, which divides the non-associative parts into four types. These simplify the Moufang loop identities and Malcev's identity and categorise non-associative loops. Analysing the non-associativity structure of sedenions and higher level Cayley-Dickson algebras uncovers octonion and three quasi-octonion, power-associative subalgebras. Power-associativity is proved to grow by multiples of seven that introduce zero divisors in factors of 84 for all Cayley-Dickson algebras. It is convenient to replace the terminology hypercomplex numbers with ultracomplex numbers to capture the quasi-algebras and since sedenions and higher level Cayley-Dickson algebras contain quasi-algebras these are ultracomplex. The non-associative types reduce the 84 zero divisors in sedenions via three cycles and four modes down to seven primary zero divisor pairs providing new techniques to analyse the seven quasi-octonions loops in sedenions. The graded notation allows the eight octonion and seven quasi-octonion subalgebras of sedenions to be uniquely derived, up to representation. The zero divisors for split sedenion algebras are analysed and mappings between three of these are provided showing 180 zero divisors and the other split algebra is analogous to sedenions with 84 zero divisors. These split algebras are shown to involve quasi-octonion algebras with mixed signature.

papers.title: Prekosmic Grothendieck/Galois Categories
papers.abstract: We establish a generalized version of the duality between groups and the categories of their representations on sets. Given an abstract symmetric monoidal category $K$ called Galois prekosmos, we define pre-Galois objects in $K$ and study the categories of their representations internal to $K$. The motivating example of $K$ is the cartesian monoidal category $\textit{Set}$ of sets, and pre-Galois objects in $\textit{Set}$ are groups. We present an axiomatic definition of pre-Galois $K$-categories, which is a complete abstract characterization of the categories of representations of pre-Galois objects in $K$. The category of covering spaces over a well-connected topological space is a prototype of a pre-Galois $\textit{Set}$-category. We establish a perfect correspondence between pre-Galois objects in $K$ and pre-Galois $K$-categories pointed with pre-fiber functors. We also establish a generalized version of the duality between flat affine group schemes and the categories of their linear representations. Given an abstract symmetric monoidal category $K$ called Grothendieck prekosmos, we define what are pre-Grothendieck objects in $K$ and study the categories of their representations internal to $K$. The motivating example of $K$ is the symmetric monoidal category $\textit{Vec}_k$ of vector spaces over a field $k$, and pre-Grothendieck objects in $\textit{Vec}_k$ are affine group $k$-schemes. We present an axiomatic definition of pre-Grothendieck $K$-categories, which is a complete abstract characterization of the categories of representations of pre-Grothendieck objects in $K$. The indization of a neutral Tannakian category over a field $k$ is a prototype of a pre-Grothendieck $\textit{Vec}_k$-category. We establish a perfect correspondence between pre-Grothendieck objects in $K$ and pre-Grothendieck $K$-categories pointed with pre-fiber functors.

papers.title: On the minimax optimality of Flow Matching through the connection to kernel density estimation
papers.abstract: Flow Matching has recently gained attention in generative modeling as a simple and flexible alternative to diffusion models. While existing statistical guarantees adapt tools from the analysis of diffusion models, we take a different perspective by connecting Flow Matching to kernel density estimation. We first verify that the kernel density estimator matches the optimal rate of convergence in Wasserstein distance up to logarithmic factors, improving existing bounds for the Gaussian kernel. Based on this result, we prove that for sufficiently large networks, Flow Matching achieves the optimal rate up to logarithmic factors. If the target distribution lies on a lower-dimensional manifold, we show that the kernel density estimator profits from the smaller intrinsic dimension on a small tube around the manifold. The faster rate also applies to Flow Matching, providing a theoretical foundation for its empirical success in high-dimensional settings.

papers.title: Propositional Dynamic Logic has Craig Interpolation: a tableau-based proof
papers.abstract: We show that Propositional Dynamic Logic (PDL) has the Craig Interpolation Property. This question has been open for many years. Three proof attempts were published, but later criticized in the literature or retracted. Our proof is based on the main ideas from Borzechowski (1988, master thesis). We define a cyclic tableau system for PDL with a loading mechanism to recognize successful repeats. For this system, we show soundness and completeness via a game. To show interpolation, we modify Maehara's method to work for tableaux with repeats: we first define pre-interpolants at each node, and then use a quasi-tableau to define interpolants for clusters (strongly connected components). In different terms, our method solves the fixpoint equations that characterize the desired interpolants, and the method ensures that the solutions to these equations can be expressed within PDL. The proof is constructive and we show how to compute interpolants. We make available a Haskell implementation of the proof system that provides interpolants, and a formal verification of our proof in the interactive theorem prover Lean. Lastly, we discuss several questions for future work.

papers.title: Covariant derivatives in the representation-valued Bott-Shulman-Stasheff and Weil complex
papers.abstract:
For a Lie groupoid $G$, the differential forms on its nerve comprise a double complex. A natural question is if this statement extends to forms with values in a representation $V$ of $G$. In this paper, we research two types of covariant derivatives which commute with the simplicial differential, yielding two types of curved double complexes of forms with coefficients in $V$. The naive approach is to consider a linear connection $
abla$ on $V$, in which case $d^
abla$ commutes with the simplicial differential if and only if $
abla$ satisfies a certain (restrictive) invariance condition. The heart of this paper focuses on another, more compelling approach: using a multiplicative Ehresmann connection for a bundle of ideals. In this case, we obtain a geometrically richer curved double complex, where the cochain map is given by the horizontal exterior covariant derivative $D$, which generalizes the well-known operator from the theory of principal bundles. Moreover, both differential operators $d^
abla$ and $D$ are researched in the infinitesimal setting of Lie algebroids, as well as their relationship with the van Est map. We conclude by using the operator $D$ to study the curvature of an (infinitesimal) multiplicative Ehresmann connection.

papers.title: Criteria for a fiberwise Fujiki/Kahler family to be locally Moishezon/projective
papers.abstract: In this paper, we utilize the theory of non-Kähler loci by S. Boucksom to construct an integral $2$-cohomology class whose restriction to a general fiber is big, and then construct a relatively big line bundle via the exponential sequence. This leads to a local Moishezonness criterion for fibrations whose total spaces are compact complex manifolds in the Fujiki class $\mathscr{C}$, generalizing the bimeromorphic version of F. Campana's local projectivity theorem. We further combine a similar idea with the singular Demailly--Păun theorem by T. Collins--V. Tosatti to obtain a local projectivity criterion for fibrations from compact Kähler manifolds, yielding a new proof and a generalization of F. Campana's local projectivity theorem.

papers.title: Transition in the asymptotics of the joint degree distribution of uniform recursive directed acyclic graphs
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic joint degree distribution of uniformly chosen vertices in uniform recursive directed acyclic graphs, a natural generalization of random recursive trees. Here, a graph is built by adding vertices one-by-one and connecting each new vertex to $m\in\mathbb{N}$ uniformly selected vertices already present. Using a representation based on Kingman's coalescent, we establish a transition in the joint degree distribution at the threshold $(m+1)\log n$, arising from the interplay between geometric degree asymptotics and fluctuations in the coalescent construction. Our results extend previously known asymptotics toward this threshold and provide a unified description of the transition, including mixed regimes where prescribed degrees lie on different scales.

papers.title: Flexible random graph modelling for cell-cell interactions
papers.abstract: In this paper we explore generalisations to a random digraph model designed for modelling cell-cell interactions (RaCInG). In its baseline model -- tested both theoretically and in biological practice -- a fixed number of arcs are assigned uniformly at random to vertices that have suitable types to accept them. Generalisations to this model are explored in two directions: constructing an undirected graph version of the model, and incorporating spatial information. Both directions are driven by biological demands: better interpretability and adaptation to technological advances. We show not only that these generalisations are theoretically possible within the framework of RaCInG, but that they can be made rigorous, proving that RaCInG creates a flexible random graph framework to model cell-cell interactions.

papers.title: Generalization of terms via universal algebra
papers.abstract: We provide a new foundational approach to the generalization of terms up to equational theories. We interpret generalization problems in a universal-algebraic setting making a key use of projective and exact algebras in the variety associated to the considered equational theory. We prove that the generality poset of a problem and its type (i.e., the cardinality of a complete set of least general solutions) can be studied in this algebraic setting. Moreover, we identify a class of varieties where the study of the generality poset can be fully reduced to the study of the congruence lattice of the 1-generated free algebra. We apply our results to varieties of algebras and to (algebraizable) logics. In particular we obtain several examples of unitary type: abelian groups; commutative monoids and commutative semigroups; all varieties whose 1-generated free algebra is trivial, e.g., lattices, semilattices, varieties without constants whose operations are idempotent; Boolean algebras, Kleene algebras, and Gödel algebras, which are the equivalent algebraic semantics of, respectively, classical, 3-valued Kleene, and Gödel-Dummett logic. Finally, we prove that the variety of MV-algebras, the equivalent algebraic semantics of Lukasiewicz logic, has nullary type.

papers.title: Profile and neighbourhood complexity of graphs excluding a minor and tree-structured graphs
papers.abstract: The \emph{$r$-neighbourhood complexity} of a graph $G$ is the function counting, for a given integer $k$, the largest possible number, over all vertex-subsets $A$ of size $k$, of subsets of $A$ realized as the intersection between the $r$-neighbourhood of some vertex and $A$. A~refinement of this notion is the \emph{$r$-profile complexity}, that counts the maximum number of distinct distance-vectors from any vertex to the vertices of $A$, ignoring distances larger than~$r$. Typically, in structured graph classes such as graphs of bounded VC-dimension or chordal graphs, these functions are bounded, leading to insights into their structural properties and efficient algorithms. We improve existing bounds on the $r$-profile complexity (and thus on the $r$-neighbourhood complexity) for graphs in several structured graph classes. We show that the $r$-profile complexity of graphs excluding $K_h$ as a minor is in $O_h(r^{3h-3}k)$. For graphs of treewidth at most~$t$, we give a bound in $O_t(r^{t+1}k)$, which is tight up to a function of~$t$ as a factor. These bounds improve results of Joret and Rambaud and answer a question of their paper [Combinatorica, 2024]. We also apply our methods to other classes of bounded expansion such as graphs excluding a fixed complete graph as a subdivision. For outerplanar graphs, we can improve our treewidth bound by a factor of $r$ and conjecture that a similar improvement holds for graphs with bounded simple treewidth. For graphs of treelength at most~$\ell$, we give the upper bound of $O(k(r^2(\ell+1)^k))$, which we improve to $O\left (k\cdot (r 2^k + r^2k^2) \right)$ in the case of chordal graphs and $O(k^2r)$ for interval graphs. Our bounds also imply relations between the order, diameter and metric dimension of graphs in these classes, improving results from [Beaudou et al., SIDMA 2017].

papers.title: A continuous scale space of diffeomorphisms
papers.abstract: In this paper, we define and study a nested family of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces of vector fields that is indexed by a range of scales, from which we construct a reproducing kernel Hilbert space of scale-dependent vector fields. We provide a characterization of the reproducing kernel of that space, with numerical approximations ensuring quick evaluations when this kernel does not have a closed form. We then introduce a multiscale version of the large deformation diffeomorphic metric mapping (LDDMM) problem and prove the existence of solutions. Finally, we provide numerical experiments performing landmark matching using multiscale LDDMM.

papers.title: Archimedean period relations for Rankin-Selberg convolutions
papers.abstract: We formulate and prove the archimedean period relations for Rankin-Selberg convolutions of $\text{GL}(n)\times \text{GL}(n)$ and $\text{GL}(n)\times \text{GL}(n-1)$, for all generic cohomological representations. As a consequence, we prove the non-vanishing of the archimedean modular symbols. This extends the earlier results in [LLS24] for essentially tempered representations of $\text{GL}(n)\times\text{GL}(n-1)$.

papers.title: A particle system approach towards the global well-posedness of master equations for potential mean field games of control
papers.abstract: This paper studies the $N$-particle systems as well as the HJB/master equations for a class of generalized mean field control (MFC) problems and the corresponding potential mean field games of control (MFGC). A local in time classical solution for the HJB equation is generated via a probabilistic approach based on the mean field maximum principle. Given an extension of the so called displacement convexity condition, we obtain the uniform estimates on the HJB equation for the $N$-particle system. Such estimates imply the displacement convexity/semi-concavity and thus the prior estimates on the solution to the HJB equation for generalized MFC problems. The global well-posedness of HJB/master equation for generalized MFC/potential MFGC is then proved thanks to the local well-posedness and the prior estimates. In view of the nature of the displacement convexity condition, such well-posedness is also true for the degenerated case. Our analysis on the $N$-particle system also induces an Lipschitz approximator to the optimal feedback function in generalized MFC/potential MFGC where an algebraic convergence rate is obtained. Furthermore, an alternative approximate Nash equilibrium is proposed based on the $N$-particle system, where the approximation error is quantified thanks to the aforementioned uniform estimates.

papers.title: Quantum Master Equation and Open Gromov-Witten Theory 2
papers.abstract: We define the not-abelian Open-Gromov-Witten partition function.

papers.title: The Price of Failure Risk: Clipped Barrier Policy Gradients with Convex Regularization
papers.abstract: In many control problems, actions consume a resource budget, such as a wear allowance, and the probability of exhausting it within a given horizon must stay below a tolerance. A simple, widely used approach is to augment the state with the remaining budget, subtract an interior barrier from the utility and penalize exhaustion, so that policy-gradient methods can be applied unchanged. We clip the combined one-step reward from below at a level m to keep the returns of exploratory policies finite. The clip level is a price of failure risk, since the clipped value decomposes exactly into the utility before failure, the cost of the interior margin and m times a geometric failure risk. Consequently, an approximately optimal policy maximizes utility net of margin cost among policies with no greater risk. Its risk exceeds that of any comparison policy by at most order 1/m and can be certified from its value or from validation data. Our main result proves exponential convergence of the population policy-gradient flow for every parameter regularizer that is convex along generalized geodesics and sufficiently strong relative to the price. This extends the mean-field analysis from relative entropy to weight decay and to finite networks. Relative entropy adds parameter noise and a pull toward a prior, whereas weight decay provides only the pull. Action regularization bounds changes in failure risk by the relative entropy to a reference policy. The bounds are evaluated on an exact maintenance benchmark, a fuel-tank controller, a solvable flow and a benchmark-suite task.

papers.title: Existence and Uniqueness of Local and Global Solutions for a Partial Differential-Algebraic Equation of Index One
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use the theory of nonlinear semigroups to establish the existence and uniqueness of both local and global solutions for a partial differential-algebraic equation (PDAE) of index one. This method is applied to a reaction-diffusion system coupled with an elliptic equation in one dimension by transforming the PDAE into a system of linear evolution equations with a Lipschitz-continuous perturbation

papers.title: Algebraic tori in the complement of quartic surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $B\subset \mathbb{P}^3$ be an slc quartic surface. The existence of an embedding $\mathbb{G}_m^3\hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^3\setminus B$ implies that $B$ has coregularity zero. In this article, we initiate the classification of coregularity zero slc quartic surfaces $B\subset \mathbb{P}^3$ for which $\mathbb{P}^3\setminus B$ contains an algebraic torus $\mathbb{G}_m^3$, and equivalently, the classification of cluster type pairs $(\mathbb{P}^3,B)$. Along the way, we give criteria for a log Calabi--Yau pair $(X,B)$ over a toric variety $T$ to be of cluster type.

papers.title: Learning Maximal Regions of Attraction on Compact Sets using Taylor Lyapunov Networks
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of learning maximal Lyapunov functions to compute the maximal region of attraction of nonlinear dynamical systems using neural networks. Two obstacles limit existing neural-network approaches: 1) finite-width approximations can fail to preserve the strict Lyapunov inequalities near the equilibrium, where they become arbitrarily weak, and 2) training is necessarily performed on a bounded computational domain for which the classical Lyapunov and Zubov theorems do not directly apply. To address these issues, first we derive Lyapunov and Zubov theorems directly on a prescribed compact computational domain, characterizing the maximal region of attraction within that domain as the solution of a boundary-value PDE. Second, we introduce the Taylor Lyapunov network, an architecture that prescribes the quadratic leading-order term via the system's linearization and represents the higher-order remainder through a structured cubic factorization, guaranteeing that any network in this class is a valid local Lyapunov function by construction. Finally, we prove that Taylor Lyapunov networks are universal approximators of maximal Lyapunov functions on compact domains, and combine these results into an unsupervised, physics-informed training procedure. Numerical experiments on systems of varying dimensions and stability types show that the proposed architecture is efficient at estimating the maximum region of attraction.

papers.title: Simple Models of Randomization and Preservation Theorems
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to provide new, more uniform model-theoretic and combinatorial proofs of the preservation theorems established in [5] and [8]. More precisely, we show that randomization preserves both $NIP$ and stability: if a first-order theory $T$ has $NIP$, then so does $T^R$, and if $T$ is stable, then so is $T^R$. Our proofs rely on the systematic use of simple models of $T^R$ and quantitative combinatorial methods. In the $NIP$ case, we use indiscernible arrays and Rademacher mean width, whereas in the stable case, we use a Ramsey lemma for cross-blocks and sequential Rademacher mean width. Using simple models of $T^R$ has the advantage of allowing us to re-prove these theorems in a simpler and quantitative manner. We finally turn our attention to $NSOP$ in randomization. We show that based on the definition of $NSOP$ given in [14], $T^R$ is stable if and only if it is $NIP$ and $NSOP$.

papers.title: A First Course in Monte Carlo Methods
papers.abstract: This is a concise mathematical introduction to Monte Carlo methods, a rich family of algorithms with far-reaching applications in science and engineering. Monte Carlo methods are an exciting subject for mathematical statisticians and computational and applied mathematicians: the design and analysis of modern algorithms are rooted in a broad mathematical toolbox that includes ergodic theory of Markov chains, Hamiltonian dynamical systems, transport maps, stochastic differential equations, information theory, optimization, Riemannian geometry, and gradient flows, among many others. These lecture notes celebrate the breadth of mathematical ideas that have led to tangible advancements in Monte Carlo methods and their applications. To accommodate a diverse audience, the level of mathematical rigor varies from chapter to chapter, giving only an intuitive treatment to the most technically demanding subjects. The aim is not to be comprehensive or encyclopedic, but rather to illustrate some key principles in the design and analysis of Monte Carlo methods through a carefully-crafted choice of topics that emphasizes timeless over timely ideas. Algorithms are presented in a way that is conducive to conceptual understanding and mathematical analysis -- clarity and intuition are favored over state-of-the-art implementations that are harder to comprehend or rely on ad-hoc heuristics. To help readers navigate the expansive landscape of Monte Carlo methods, each algorithm is accompanied by a summary of its pros and cons, and by a discussion of the type of problems for which they are most useful. The presentation is self-contained, and therefore adequate for self-guided learning or as a teaching resource. Each chapter contains a section with bibliographic remarks that will be useful for those interested in conducting research on Monte Carlo methods and their applications.

papers.title: Boosting e-BH via conditional calibration
papers.abstract: The e-BH procedure is an e-value-based multiple testing procedure that provably controls the false discovery rate (FDR) under any dependence structure between the e-values. Despite this appealing theoretical FDR control guarantee, the e-BH procedure often suffers from low power in practice. In this paper, we propose a general framework that boosts the power of e-BH without sacrificing its FDR control under arbitrary dependence. This is achieved by the technique of conditional calibration, where we take as input the e-values and calibrate them to be a set of "boosted e-values" that are guaranteed to be no less -- and are often more -- powerful than the original ones. Our general framework is explicitly instantiated in three classes of multiple testing problems: (1) testing under parametric models, (2) conditional independence testing under the model-X setting, and (3) model-free conformalized selection. Extensive numerical experiments show that our proposed method significantly improves the power of e-BH while continuing to control the FDR. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through an application to an observational study dataset for identifying individuals whose counterfactuals satisfy certain properties.

papers.title: Convergence of stochastic integrals with applications to transport equations and conservation laws with noise
papers.abstract: Convergence of stochastic integrals driven by Wiener processes $W_n$, with $W_n \to W$ almost surely in $C_t$, is crucial in analyzing SPDEs. Our focus is on the convergence of the form $\int_0^T V_n\, \mathrm{d} W_n \to \int_0^T V\, \mathrm{d} W$, where $\{V_n\}$ is bounded in $L^p(Ω\times [0,T];X)$ for a Banach space $X$ and some finite $p > 2$. This is challenging when $V_n$ converges to $V$ weakly in the temporal variable. We supply convergence results to handle stochastic integral limits when strong temporal convergence is lacking. A key tool is a uniform mean $L^1$ time translation estimate on $V_n$, an estimate that is easily verified in many SPDEs. However, this estimate alone does not guarantee strong compactness of $(ω,t)\mapsto V_n(ω,t)$. Our findings, especially pertinent to equations exhibiting singular behavior, are substantiated by establishing several stability results for stochastic transport equations and conservation laws.

papers.title: A systematic approach to Diophantine equations: open problems
papers.abstract: This paper collects polynomial Diophantine equations that are simple to state but apparently difficult to solve.

papers.title: Diffusion Processes on $p$-Wasserstein Space over Banach Space
papers.abstract: To study diffusion processes on the p-Wasserstein space $\mathscr P_p$ for $p\in [1,\infty)$ over a separable, reflexive Banach space $X$, we present a criterion on the quasi-regularity of Dirichlet forms in $L^2(\mathscr P_p,Λ)$ for a reference probability $Λ$ on $\mathscr P_p$. It is formulated in terms of an upper bound condition with the uniform norm of the intrinsic derivative. We find a versatile class of quasi-regular local Dirichlet forms on $\mathscr P_p$ by using images of Dirichlet forms on the tangent space $L^p(X\to X,μ_0)$ at a reference point $μ_0\in\mathscr P_p$. The Ornstein--Uhlenbeck type Dirichlet form and process on $\mathscr P_2$ are an important example in this class. We derive an $L^2$-estimate for the corresponding heat kernel and an integration by parts formula for the invariant measure.

papers.title: Birational geometry of log Calabi-Yau pairs $(\mathbb{P}^3, D)$ of coregularity 2
papers.abstract: This paper aims to study the birational geometry of log Calabi-Yau pairs $(\mathbb{P}^3, D)$ of coregularity 2, where in this case $D$ is an irreducible normal quartic surface with canonical singularities. We completely classify which toric weighted blowups of a point will initiate a volume preserving Sarkisov link starting with this pair. Depending on the type of singularity, our results point out that some of these weights do not work generically for a general member of the corresponding coarse moduli space of quartics.

papers.title: On the decomposition group of a nonsingular plane cubic by a log Calabi-Yau geometrical perspective
papers.abstract: This paper aims to study the decomposition group of a nonsingular plane cubic under the light of the log Calabi-Yau geometry. Using this approach we prove that an appropriate algorithm of the Sarkisov program in dimension 2 applied to an element of this group is automatically volume preserving. From this, we deduce some properties of the (volume preserving) Sarkisov factorization of its elements. We also confirm an expectation by Blanc, Pan and Vust on the splitting property of the canonical complex of a nonsingular plane cubic. Within a similar context in dimension 3, we exhibit in detail an interesting counterexample for a possible generalization of a theorem by Pan in which there exists a Sarkisov factorization obtained algorithmically that is not volume preserving.

papers.title: Minimal doubling for small subsets in compact Lie groups
papers.abstract: We prove an asymptotically sharp bound for the minimal doubling of a small measurable subset of a compact connected Lie group, settling a conjecture of Breuillard and Green. Namely, let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group of positive dimension $d_G$ with Haar probability measure $μ_G$, and let $ε> 0$. We show that for all compact subsets $A$ of sufficiently small measure we have \[μ_G(A^2) \geq \left(2^{d_G-d_M} - ε\right)μ_G(A),\] where $d_M$ is the maximal dimension of a proper closed subgroup. This recovers, by a different method, the small-measure doubling theorem of Jing--Tran--Zhang for $G=\mathrm{SO}_3(\mathbb{R})$. More generally, for every $ε>0$ and any pair of non-empty compact subsets $A,B$ of sufficiently small measure, we prove the Brunn--Minkowski-type inequality: \[ μ_G(AB)^{\frac{1}{d_G-d_M}} \geq (1-ε)\left( μ_G(A)^{\frac{1}{d_G-d_M}} + μ_G(B)^{\frac{1}{d_G-d_M}}\right).\] We also prove an inverse theorem in the semi-simple case: for any fixed $K\geq1$ and $δ>0$, every compact $K$-approximate subgroup of sufficiently small positive Haar measure is covered by $C(d_G,K)$ translates of the $δ$-neighbourhood of a proper closed connected subgroup. Our approach combines this inverse theorem with optimal transport and its recent applications to the Brunn--Minkowski inequality.

papers.title: Monoidal structures on triangulated fibered categories
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a small category admitting binary products. There exists a canonical dictionary expressing the structure and properties of monoidal $\mathcal{S}$-fibered categories in terms of the external tensor product in place of the usual internal tensor product. In this paper, we specialize this dictionary to the setting of triangulated $\mathcal{S}$-fibered categories, by studying how the general translation process interacts with shift functors. Our results provide a satisfactory abstract framework to study monoidal structures from the perspective of perverse sheaves.

papers.title: Uniform existential definitions of valuations in function fields in one variable
papers.abstract: We study function fields of curves over a base field $K$ which is either a global field or a large field having a separable field extension of degree divisible by $4$. We show that, for any such function field, Hilbert's 10th Problem has a negative answer, the valuation rings containing $K$ are uniformly existentially definable, and the finitary holomorphy rings are definable by a universal-existential formula. In order to obtain these results, we develop further the usage of local-global principles for quadratic forms in function fields to definability of certain subrings. We include a first systematic presentation of this general method, without restriction on the characteristic.

papers.title: A quantum central path algorithm for linear optimization
papers.abstract: We propose a novel quantum algorithm for solving linear optimization problems by quantum-mechanical simulation of the central path. While interior point methods follow the central path with an iterative algorithm that works with successive linearizations of the perturbed KKT conditions, we perform a simulation working directly with the nonlinear complementarity equations. Using a two-stage quantum eigenpath traversal schedule, this approach yields an algorithm for solving linear optimization problems involving $m$ constraints and $n$ variables to $\varepsilon$-optimality using $\widetilde{O}\!\left((m+n)^{3/2}\,\varepsilon^{-1}+(m+n)^{1/2}\,\varepsilon^{-3/2}\right)$ queries to an oracle that evaluates a potential function. In the standard gate model (i.e., without access to quantum RAM), our algorithm can obtain $\varepsilon$-precise solutions to LO problems using at most $$\widetilde{O}\!\left(\left[\frac{(m+n)^{3/2}}{\varepsilon} + \frac{(m+n)^{1/2}}{\varepsilon^{3/2}}\right] \cdot \mathrm{nnz}(A)\right)$$ elementary gates, where $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$ is the total number of non-zero elements found in the constraint matrix.

papers.title: Diamonds: Homology and the Central Series of Groups
papers.abstract: We establish an analog of a theorem of Stallings which asserts the homomorphisms between the universal nilpotent quotients induced by a homomorphism $G \to H$ of groups are isomorphisms provided a pair of homological conditions are satisfied. Our analogy does not have a homomorphism between $G$ and $H$ but instead $G,H \leq G_0$ that satisfies a similar homological condition. We derive a few applications of this result. First, we show that there exist pairs of non-isomorphic number fields whose absolute Galois groups have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. We show that there exists pairs of non-isometric hyperbolic $n$-manifolds whose fundamental groups are residually nilpotent and have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. These are the first examples of residually nilpotent Kleinian groups with arbitrarily large nilpotent genus. Complex hyperbolic 2-manifold examples are given as well. Considering Riemann surfaces and complex hyperbolic 2-manifolds as projective curves and surfaces defined over a number field, we show the (outer) action of the absolute Galois group of the field of definition on the universal nilpotent quotients of the geometric fundamental groups are equivalent. This is in contrast to fact that the (outer) Galois action on the geometric fundamental group of a projective hyperbolic curve determines the curve by work of Mochizuki. In particular, the nilpotent representation theory of the geometric fundamental group is not anabelian.

papers.title: Gromov-Witten Generating Series of Elliptic Curves and Iterated Integrals of Eisenstein-Kronecker Forms
papers.abstract: We compute various types of iterated integrals of Eisenstein-Kronecker forms that are constructed from the Kronecker theta function. Furthermore, we relate the generating series of Gromov-Witten invariants of elliptic curves to these iterated integrals.

papers.title: A generalization of the Perelman gluing theorem and applications
papers.abstract: We extend a positive Ricci curvature gluing theorem of Perelman to a range of positive intermediate curvature conditions, ranging from positive scalar curvature up to (and including) positive sectional curvature. As an application of this, we demonstrate that the observer moduli space of metrics with positive intermediate Ricci curvatures can have non-trivial higher homotopy groups. Further applications include deriving a sufficient condition for the existence of a metric with positive intermediate Ricci curvature and totally geodesic boundary.

papers.title: Pointed Hopf superalgebras of dimension up to 10
papers.abstract: By utilizing the technique introduced in our previous work to construct Hopf superalgebras by reversing the Radford-Majid bosonization, we classify non-semisimple pointed Hopf superalgebras of dimension up to 10 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.

papers.title: On pairs of $r$-primitive and $k$-normal elements with prescribed traces over finite fields
papers.abstract: Given $\mathbb{F}_{q^{n}}$, a field with $q^n$ elements, where $q $ is a prime power and $n$ is positive integer. For $r_1,r_2,m_1,m_2 \in \mathbb{N}$, $k_1,k_2 \in \mathbb{N}\cup \{0\}$, a rational function $F = \frac{F_1}{F_2}$ in $\mathbb{F}_{q}[x]$ with deg($F_i$) $\leq m_i$; $i=1,2,$ satisfying some conditions, and $a,b \in \mathbb{F}_{q}$, we construct a sufficient condition on $(q,n)$ which guarantees the existence of an $r_1$-primitive, $k_1$-normal element $ε\in \mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ such that $F(ε)$ is $r_2$-primitive, $k_2$-normal with $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb{F}_{q^n}/\mathbb{F}_q}(ε) = a$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb{F}_{q^n}/\mathbb{F}_q}(ε^{-1}) = b$. For $m_1=10, \; m_2=11,\; r_1 = 3, \; r_2 = 2, \; k_1=2,\;k_2 = 1$, we establish bounds on $q$, for various $n$, to determine the existence of such elements in $\mathbb{F}_{q^{n}}$. Furthermore, we identify all such pairs $(q,n)$ excluding 10 possible values of $(q,n)$, in fields of characteristics 13.

papers.title: Modularity over $\mathbb{C}$ implies modularity over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We give an account of Mazur's proof that, for an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$, if it admits a nonconstant mapping from $X(N)$ defined over the complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$, for some $N$, then it also admits a nonconstant mapping from $X_0(M)$ for some (possibly different) $M$ defined over the rational numbers $\mathbb{Q}$. We also briefly discuss two open questions of Khare concerning uniformisations of elliptic curves by noncongruence modular curves. This expository note is based on the author's expository talk in March 2022 during the 2nd Trimester Program on "Modularity and the Generalised Fermat Equation" held online and organised by Bhaskaracharya Pratishthana in Pune, India.

papers.title: Wall divisors on irreducible symplectic orbifolds of Nikulin-type
papers.abstract: We determine the wall divisors on irreducible symplectic orbifolds which are deformation equivalent to a special type of examples, called Nikulin orbifolds. The Nikulin orbifolds are obtained as partial resolutions in codimension 2 of a quotient by a symplectic involution of a Hilbert scheme of 2 points on a K3 surface. This builds on the previous article arXiv:2009.04873 in which the theory of wall divisors was generalized to orbifold singularities.

papers.title: Topology of irregular isomonodromy times on a fixed pointed curve
papers.abstract: We will define and study (moduli) spaces of deformations of irregular classes on Riemann surfaces, which provide an intrinsic viewpoint on the `times' of irregular isomonodromy systems in general. Our aim is to study the deeper generalisation of the G-braid groups that occur as fundamental groups of such deformation spaces, with particular focus on the generalisation of the full G-braid groups.

papers.title: Frobenius kernels of algebraic supergroups and Steinberg's tensor product theorem
papers.abstract: For a split quasireductive supergroup $G$ defined over a field, we study structure and representation of Frobenius kernels $G_r$ of $G$ and we give a necessary and sufficient condition for $G_r$ to be unimodular in terms of the root system of $G$. We also establish Steinberg's tensor product theorem for $G$ under some natural assumptions.

papers.title: Local wild mapping class groups and cabled braids
papers.abstract: We will define and study some generalisations of pure $\mathfrak{g}$-braid groups that occur in the theory of connections on curves, for any complex reductive Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$. They make up local pieces of the wild mapping class groups, which are fundamental groups of (universal) deformations of wild Riemann surfaces, underlying the braiding of Stokes data and generalising the usual mapping class groups. We will establish a general product decomposition for the local wild mapping class groups, and in many cases define a fission tree controlling this decomposition. Further in type A we will show one obtains cabled versions of braid groups, related to braid operads.

papers.title: Aspects of Muchnik's paradox in restricted betting
papers.abstract: Muchnik's paradox says that enumerable betting strategies are not always reducible to enumerable strategies whose bets are restricted to either even rounds or odd rounds. In other words, there are outcome sequences x where an effectively enumerable strategy succeeds, but no such parity-restricted effectively enumerable strategy does. We characterize the effective Hausdorff dimension of such $x$, showing that it can be as low as 1/2 but not less. We also show that such reals that are random with respect to parity-restricted effectively enumerable strategies with packing dimension as low as $\log\sqrt3$. Finally we exhibit Muchnik's paradox in the case of computable integer-valued strategies.

papers.title: $L^p$-theory for the exterior Stokes problem with Navier's type slip-without-friction boundary conditions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the stationary Stokes equations in an exterior domain three-dimensional under a slip boundary condition without friction. We set the problem in weighted Sobolev spaces in order to control the behavior at infinity of the solutions. In this work, we try to investigate the existence and uniqueness up to an element of a nontrivial kernel of the weak solutions related to this problem in $L^p-$theory when $p>3$. Our proofs are based on obtaining inf-sup conditions that play a fundamental role.

papers.title: Small measure expansion in connected noncompact groups
papers.abstract: Assuming $G$ is unimodular and $K>1$, and that $μ(A^2) < K μ(A)$. We show that this is a continuous surjective group homomorphism $χ: G \to L$ with a compact kernel, where $L$ is a Lie group satisfying $$\dim(L) \leq \lfloor\log K\rfloor(\lfloor\log K\rfloor+1)/2.$$ This dimension bound is sharp, We also establish the relationship between $A$ and its image under the quotient map, and obtain a more general version of this result for the product set $AB$ without assuming unimodularity. We present two applications: (1) An inverse Kemperman theorem in noncompact groups. Let $G$ be a connected, noncompact, locally compact group with a left Haar measure $μ$, and let $A$ and $B$ be nonempty, compact subsets of $G$. We classify all cases where $G$, $A$, and $B$ exhibit nearly minimal expansion properties (in the unimodular case, this means $μ(AB)$ is close to $μ(A) + μ(B)$). This result completes the noncompact cases of the Kemperman inverse problem and resolves a question posed by Griesmer and Tao. (2) An effective generalized Margulis lemma for discrete subgroups of almost-connected locally compact groups acting properly by isometries. If $B(x,4r)$ can be covered by $K$ translates of $B(x,r)$ at one point and one scale, it gives a small radius $r/2M$, and the group generated at this radius has a subgroup of index at most $M \exp((\log K)^4)$ which is nilpotent modulo a finite normal subgroup. The nilpotency step is bounded by $(\log K)^2$, and \[ M\leq K^{\exp(C(\log K)^4\log\log K)} \] and $C$ is an absolute constant.

papers.title: Centro-Affine Differential Geometry and the Log-Minkowski Problem
papers.abstract: We interpret the log-Brunn-Minkowski conjecture of Böröczky-Lutwak-Yang-Zhang as a spectral problem in centro-affine differential geometry. In particular, we show that the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator coincides with the centro-affine Laplacian, thus obtaining a new avenue for tackling the conjecture using insights from affine differential geometry. As every strongly convex hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a centro-affine unit-sphere, it has constant centro-affine Ricci curvature equal to $n-2$, in stark contrast to the standard weighted Ricci curvature of the associated metric-measure space, which will in general be negative. In particular, we may use the classical argument of Lichnerowicz and a centro-affine Bochner formula to give a new proof of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality. For origin-symmetric convex bodies enjoying fairly generous curvature pinching bounds (improving with dimension), we are able to show global uniqueness in the $L^p$- and log-Minkowski problems, as well as the corresponding global $L^p$- and log-Minkowski conjectured inequalities. As a consequence, we resolve the isomorphic version of the log-Minkowski problem: for any origin-symmetric convex body $\bar K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, there exists an origin-symmetric convex body $K$ with $\bar K \subset K \subset 8 \bar K$, so that $K$ satisfies the log-Minkowski conjectured inequality, and so that $K$ is uniquely determined by its cone-volume measure $V_K$. If $\bar K$ is not extremely far from a Euclidean ball to begin with, an analogous isometric result, where $8$ is replaced by $1+ε$, is obtained as well.

papers.title: Adaptive Inference in Multivariate Nonparametric Regression Models Under Monotonicity
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of adaptive inference on a regression function at a point under a multivariate nonparametric regression setting. The regression function belongs to a Hölder class and is assumed to be monotone with respect to some or all of the arguments. We derive the minimax rate of convergence for confidence intervals (CIs) that adapt to the underlying smoothness, and provide an adaptive inference procedure that obtains this minimax rate. When the regression function is monotone in $k_{+}$ of its $k$ arguments, the minimax expected length over a Hölder class with exponent $γ'$ of CIs that maintain coverage over a rougher class with exponent $γ$ is of order $n^{-1/(2+k_{+}/γ'+(k-k_{+})/γ)}$. The rate is unchanged if the rougher class restricts the smoothness only at the point, along the nonmonotone arguments. Under monotonicity along a closed convex cone that contains no line, only the dimension of its linear span enters the rate. The procedure differs from that of Cai and Low (2004), intended to yield shorter CIs under practically relevant specifications. It is valid in finite samples under Gaussian errors with a known variance. The proposed method applies to general linear functionals of the regression function.

papers.title: Langevin equations solved by Markov chains (instead of integrals), two solutions with multiplicative noise and their properties
papers.abstract: Langevin equations are usually understood as integral equations, since continuous and Markov solutions are nowhere differentiable. This is avoidable by the fact that white Gaussian noise can be seen as a generalized derivative of the Wiener process. The simplest LE is thus solved by Wiener paths, which can be computed by a Markov chain. That crucial property persists for functions of these paths, and solutions of the general LE are therefore assumed to have that form. In short time steps these functions must be linear or quadratic. Both cases lead to sampled versions of existing stochastic intrgrals ('Ito' and 'anti-Ito' respectively). In physics they apply for Brownian motion in presence of a temperature gradient: without a feedback to the medium in the linear case, and for a tagged molecule in the quadratic one; in the latter case the Fokker-Planck equation describes a local equilibrium.

papers.title: On an affirmative solution to the non-commutative Michael's problem, with applications to automatic continuity theory
papers.abstract: In 1952, Michael posed a question about functional continuity of commutative Fréchet algebras in his memoir, known as Michael's problem in the literature. We settle this in the affirmative for the non-commutative Fréchet algebras, along with its equivalent form. Indeed, we continue our previous works to directly attack these problems. We show that the existence of a discontinuous character on the non-commutative test case for this problem -- the Fréchet algebra ${\cal U}_{nc}$ of all entire functions on $\ell^\infty$ -- allows us to generate another Fréchet algebra topology on ${\cal U}_{nc}$, inequivalent to the usual Fréchet algebra topology. An important tool is a topological version of the tensor algebra over a Banach space. The elementary, but crucial, idea is to express the test algebra ${\cal U}_{nc}$ as a {\it weighted Fréchet tensor algebra} over the Banach space $\ell^1$. We give some important applications in automatic continuity theory. In particular, we provide affirmative answers to significant, long-standing problems from 1967 (extending Johnson's result for non-commutative, semi-simple Fréchet algebras; Dales' survey, Question 9), 1976 (extending Esterle's result, giving another approach for Michael's problem for more general $(F)$-algebras), and 1978 (a weaker version of an equivalent form of the non-commutative Michael's problem; Dales' survey, p. 143).

papers.title: On avatars of the Singer-Wermer conjecture in Frechet algebras
papers.abstract: We construct two Fréchet algebras admitting countably many mutually inequivalent Fréchet algebra topologies. The second example is a modification of the maiden (and first) example of a non-Banach Fréchet algebra with two inequivalent Fréchet algebra topologies, considered by Read to show that the famous Singer-Wermer conjecture does not hold in the Fréchet case. We discuss a couple of avatars of the Singer-Wermer conjecture in Fréchet algebras. In particular, this conjecture (and so, its weaker version, too) does hold by the second example which also admits countably many mutually equivalent Fréchet algebra topologies. However the stronger version of this conjecture (i.e., the Kaplansky's conjecture) does not hold by the second example.

papers.title: Linear stability analysis for 2D shear flows near Couette in the isentropic Compressible Euler equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate linear stability properties of the 2D isentropic compressible Euler equations linearized around a shear flow given by a monotone profile, close to the Couette flow, with constant density, in the domain $\mathbb{T}\times \mathbb{R}$. We begin by directly investigating the Couette shear flow, where we characterize the linear growth of the compressible part of the fluid while proving time decay for the incompressible part (inviscid damping with slower rates). Then we extend the analysis to monotone shear flows near Couette, where we are able to give an upper bound, superlinear in time, for the compressible part of the fluid. The incompressible part enjoys an inviscid damping property, analogous to the Couette case. In the pure Couette case, we exploit the presence of an additional conservation law (which connects the vorticity and the density on the moving frame) in order to reduce the number of degrees of freedom of the system. The result then follows by using weighted energy estimates. In the general case, unfortunately, this conservation law no longer holds. Therefore we define a suitable weighted energy functional for the whole system, which can be used to estimate the irrotational component of the velocity but does not provide sharp bounds on the solenoidal component. However, even in the absence of the aforementioned additional conservation law, we are still able to show the existence of a functional relation which allows us to recover somehow the vorticity from the density, on the moving frame. By combining the weighted energy estimates with the functional relation we also recover the inviscid damping for the solenoidal component of the velocity.

papers.title: Negative Translations for Affine and Lukasiewicz Logic
papers.abstract: We investigate four well-known negative translations of classical logic into intuitionistic logic within a substructural setting. We find that in \emph{affine logic} the translation schemes due to Kolmogorov and Gödel both satisfy Troelstra's criteria for a negative translation. On the other hand, the schemes of Glivenko and Gentzen both fail for affine logic, but for different reasons: one can extend affine logic to make Glivenko work and Gentzen fail and {\it vice versa}. By contrast, in the setting of \emph{Łukasiewicz logic}, we can prove a general result asserting that a wide class of formula translations including those of Kolmogorov, Gödel, Gentzen and Glivenko not only satisfy Troelstra's criteria with respect to a natural intuitionistic fragment of Łukasiewicz logic but are all equivalent.

papers.title: Geometrization of almost extremal representations in $\text{PSL}_2\Bbb R$
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a closed surface of genus $g$. In this paper, we investigate the relationship between hyperbolic cone-structure on $S$ and representations of the fundamental group into $\text{PSL}_2\Bbb R$. We consider surfaces of genus greater than $g$ and we show that, under suitable conditions, every representation $ρ:π_1 S\longrightarrow \text{PSL}_2\Bbb R$ with Euler number $\mathcal{E}(ρ)=\pm\big(χ(S)+1\big)$ arises as holonomy of a hyperbolic cone-structure $σ$ on $S$ with a single cone point of angle $4π$. From this result, we derive that for surfaces of genus $2$ every representation with $\mathcal{E}(ρ)=\pm1$ arises as the holonomy of some hyperbolic cone-structure.

papers.title: A law of the iterated logarithm for random multiplicative functions on integers with a large prime factor
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a Rademacher random multiplicative function supported on the squarefree integers. We investigate the almost sure fluctuations of the restricted sum $M^{>}(x)=\sum_{n\le x;~ P(n)>x^{1/2}}f(n)$, where $P(n)$ is the largest prime factor of $n$. With $Q(x)$ being the conditional variance of $M^{>}(x)$ given the values of $f$ at primes not exceeding $x^{1/2}$, we prove that, almost surely, the upper and lower limits of $M^{>}(x)(2Q(x)\log\log Q(x))^{-1/2}$ as $x\to\infty$ are $1$ and $-1$, respectively. Furthermore, it is shown that the almost sure cluster set of the normalized sum is $[-1,1]$.

papers.title: The Hibi--Li (2016) conjecture is fully resolved
papers.abstract: Hibi and Li conjectured that the order polytope $\mathcal{O}(P)$ of a finite poset $P$ has at most as many faces of each dimension as its chain polytope $\mathcal{C}(P)$, and that equality in some dimension $k$ with $1\leq k\leq|P|-1$ forces the two polytopes to be unimodularly equivalent. Fourier proved the inequality in a 2026 preprint. Let $X$ be the five-element poset in which an element lies above two incomparable elements and below two other incomparable elements. Building on Fourier's proof, we show that if an $n$-element poset contains $X$ as an induced subposet, then, for every $k$ with $2\leq k\leq n-1$, its chain polytope has at least $\binom{n-3}{k-2}$ more $k$-dimensional faces than its order polytope, and that for every $n\geq5$ some $n$-element poset containing $X$ attains all these bounds at once. Since Hibi and Li showed that $\mathcal{O}(P)$ and $\mathcal{C}(P)$ are unimodularly equivalent exactly when $P$ does not contain $X$, this proves the equality statement for these $k$. For $k=1$ the equality statement is false: $\mathcal{O}(X)$ and $\mathcal{C}(X)$ have equally many edges (Hibi, Li, Sahara and Shikama) but are not unimodularly equivalent. With Fourier's inequality, these results settle the conjecture. Every result is formally verified in Lean 4, with only published results and two results of Fourier's preprint as axioms.

papers.title: A Diophantine generalization of Fourier's irrationality trick
papers.abstract: We revisit Fourier's method for proving the irrationality of $e$ and generalize it into a unified Diophantine framework, which applies to a broad class of series with bounded or mildly growing integer numerators, and suitably growing, divisible denominators. Using integer linear forms, we establish a general criterion that recovers classical irrationality results while also generating new ones within a single structural approach.

papers.title: Asymptotic stability of clique-saturating edges near Turán thresholds
papers.abstract: Let $f_{p+1}(n,m)$ denote the minimum number of $K_{p+1}$-saturating edges in an $n$-vertex $K_{p+1}$-free graph with $m$ edges. In this paper, we investigate the stability of this parameter near the Turán thresholds, with particular emphasis on the role of the minimum degree. We introduce the refined parameter $f_{p+1,p}(n,m,δ)$. It is defined for $K_{p+1}$-free graphs on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges, minimum degree $δ$, and containing at least a copy of $K_p$. For every fixed integer $p\ge3$, we establish a stability result when the number of edges is $\mathrm{ex}(n,K_p)+o(n^2)$, showing that \[ f_{p+1,p} (n,m,δ)=\left(\frac{(p-2)^2}{2(p-1)^3}+o(1)\right)n^2, \ \text{for }\ m=\mathrm{ex}(n,K_p)+o(n^2), \ δ\geq \left(\frac{p-2}{p-1}+o(1)\right)n. \] We further obtain a stability theorem in the regime where the number of edges is quadratically smaller than $\operatorname{ex}(n,K_{p+1})$. More precisely, for $0 \leq c< \frac{1}{2p(3p-1)}$, \[ f_{p+1,p} (n,m,δ)=\left(\frac{1}{2p}+o(1)\right)n^2, \ \text{for }\ m=\operatorname{ex}(n,K_{p+1})-(c+o(1))n^2, \ δ\geq \left(\frac{p-1}{p}-2c+o(1)\right)n. \]

papers.title: Four runners that are barely lonely
papers.abstract: For positive integers $v_1,\dots,v_n$ let $\mathrm{ML}(v_1,\dots,v_n)=\max_t\min_i\|v_it\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the distance to the nearest integer. Kravitz asked which values below $1/n$ occur. For $n=4$, Jain and Kravitz showed that the values below $1/4$ are $m/(4m+2)$, $m\ge2$, up to finitely many undetermined exceptions. We settle the four-runner case completely. A primitive quadruple has $\mathrm{ML}<1/4$ if and only if it is, up to order, $\{1,2,3,4k\}$, or $\{x,y,x+y,x+2y\}$ with $\gcd(x,y)=1$ and $y\not\equiv x,2x\pmod 4$, or $\{1,3,4,14\}$. The values below $1/4$ are exactly $m/(4m+2)$ with $m\ge2$, $m\ne3$, so $3/14$ is the only exception, and Conjecture 4.1 of Fan and Sun holds. A density lemma bounds the length of a quadruple on neither critical subtorus by $512$, and an exact search over 800,816,099 quadruples completes the proof. The same method shows that the two-dimensional subtori of $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^4$ with loneliness below $2/5$ take exactly the three-runner values in that range, which between $1/3$ and $2/5$ are the fractions $p/q$ with $1\le 2q-5p\le 4$. Hence the accumulation points of the four-runner spectrum in $(0,2/5]$ are the three-runner values there, as Giri and Kravitz conjectured, and $9/25$ is not the loneliness of a two-dimensional subtorus. For every $n$, assuming the conjecture for $n-1$ and $n-2$ speeds, we prove $\mathrm{ML}(v)>1/n-(n(n-1))^{n-2}/(2|v|)$, which is sharp in $|v|$, and that every $n$-tuple with $\mathrm{ML}<1/n$ and $|v|\ge n(n(n-1))^{2n-4}$ lies on a two-dimensional subtorus of loneliness $1/n$. This answers a question of Cordella. For five speeds, a two-dimensional subtorus of $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^5$ with loneliness below $2/9$ is the product of a coordinate circle with the circle of $\{1,2,3,4\}$ or $\{1,3,4,7\}$. We also give infinitely many subtori whose maximizers lie off every circle with a repeated speed.

papers.title: Sharp bounds, stability, and arithmetic fluctuations for induced pentagons
papers.abstract: We prove that every graph with $m>0$ edges contains at most $\frac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}(\frac{m}{5})^{5/2}$ induced pentagons. Equality holds precisely for balanced blow-ups of the Clebsch graph, together with isolated vertices. The bound and equality classification extend to arbitrary nonnegative vertex weights and to all graphons, including fractional graphons. Moreover, a deficit of $\varepsilon$ in the normalized ratio can be repaired by $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon}m)$ edge edits on the original vertex set, producing an exactly balanced Clebsch blow-up and isolates. The exponent $1/2$ is optimal. We further separate the linear cost of adjacency errors from the quadratic cost of class imbalance. This yields an arithmetic description of the finite-edge deficit and its explicit second-order term, with a uniform power-saving remainder. For each fixed integer $j$, the exact extremal count at $m=40k^2+j$ is eventually an integer coefficient polynomial in $k$, computable by a finite enumeration; we do not quantify its threshold of validity. The proof combines global variational conditions, an active-density bound, and an exact rational certificate on the $1,044$ graphs of order seven. A positive-slope identity permits a single rational reference density. An exact conditional span excludes triangles at equality, after which degree and codegree identities determine the Clebsch structure. All finite certificates admit independent verification using integer arithmetic.

papers.title: Nodal radial solutions for a zero-mass $(p,q)$-Laplacian equation with Hardy-Hénon type weight
papers.abstract: We establish the existence of radial nodal solutions for a class of zero-mass $(p,q)$-Laplacian equations in $\mathbb{R}^N$ with a Hardy-Hénon type weight $|x|^α$. The absence of lower-order potential terms motivates the use of a homogeneous radial variational framework adapted to the mixed $p$- and $q$-growth structure. A key ingredient is a weighted Sobolev embedding theorem that establishes continuity and compactness in the appropriate range of exponents and identifies the sharp interval for continuous embedding. Building on these results, we construct sign-changing radial solutions through a variational method based on radial partitions and critical levels. The main result asserts that, for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, the problem admits a radial weak solution with exactly $k$ nodal zeros. The proof combines minimization on Nehari manifolds over radial subdomains with an optimization procedure that determines the nodal radii and ensures the compatibility of the solution across nodal interfaces.

papers.title: Bases for the Top-Degree Garsia-Haiman Module
papers.abstract: We introduce two new monomial bases for the top $t$-degree component of the Garsia-Haiman module $V_μ$ for every partition $μ$. Both bases are indexed by column-strict standard fillings of shape $μ$; the first has exponents governed by entrywise refinements of Haglund's combinatorial statistics for the modified Macdonald polynomials $\widetilde{H}_μ(X;q,t)$. The second basis has exponents governed by an insertion algorithm of Bhattacharya-Ratheesh-Viswanath, and gives a basis realization of the ``fermionic formula" of the $m_{1^n}$-coefficient of the $q$-Whittaker polynomial. Our proof uses orbit harmonics, and is inspired by the original approach of Garsia and Haiman.

papers.title: On a positivity conjecture of Fasi and Higham for Padé approximants to the matrix exponential
papers.abstract: We study the positivity conjecture of Fasi and Higham [SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 40 (2019), Conjecture 3.2], which concerns the Taylor coefficients of the reciprocal of the denominator $q_{k,m}(z)$ of the Padé approximant to the matrix exponential. The conjecture asserts that these coefficients are positive whenever $m$ is odd. We prove full positivity for $k=0$ and eventual positivity whenever the unique positive real zero of $q_{k,m}$ is the unique zero of minimal modulus. We also give an explicit computable sufficient threshold beyond which all coefficients are positive. Using Hermite scaling with leading-coefficient normalization, we prove that this spectral minimality holds for each fixed odd $m$ and all sufficiently large $k$. The unrestricted conjecture is nevertheless false. We give exact rational counterexamples and prove a transient scaling theorem showing that on the scale $n\asymp\sqrt{k+1}$ the normalized coefficients converge to an explicit oscillatory Hermite profile. For $m=5$ this profile is negative at one point, yielding infinitely many counterexamples. The counterexamples are not diagonal, and the diagonal case $k=m$, which is the case relevant in practice, remains open. These results do not imply a failure of the Fasi--Higham algorithm. Rather, they delimit the range in which the auxiliary positivity conjecture can be used as a theorem.

papers.title: Solving the Minkowski problem by continuation from the unit sphere: spherical harmonic discretization and error estimates
papers.abstract: Given a positive function $ρ$ on the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^2$, the classical Minkowski problem asks for a closed convex surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with Gauss curvature $1/ρ(ν)$ at the point with outer normal $ν$. In terms of the support function $h$, it is the Monge--Ampère equation $\det(\nabla^2h+hσ)=ρ$ on $\mathbb{S}^2$, uniquely solvable up to translation when $ρ$ has zero first moment. We solve it by continuation from the sphere: along the linear path $ρ_t=(1-t)+tρ$, the solution $h(t)$ evolves in the artificial time $t$, and its velocity $\partial_th$ solves a linear elliptic equation in divergence form whose kernel consists of the translations. In time we use the explicit Euler or trapezoidal method with step $τ$; in space, spherical harmonics of degree at most $L$ with a Lagrange multiplier for the kernel. For $ρ\in H^{s+2}(\mathbb{S}^2)$ with real $s\ge4$, we prove that all numerical solutions stay strictly convex, with $H^1$ errors $O(τ+L^{-(s+1)})$ for Euler and $O(τ^3+L^{-(s+1)})$ for the trapezoidal scheme, including data quadrature, under independent thresholds for $τ$ and $L$. The proof rests on a priori estimates for the perturbed equation satisfied by each iterate, which keep every step uniformly elliptic, and on the exactly quadratic determinant, which raises the trapezoidal order from two to three. The continuation thus supplies a good initial guess for Newton's method: from the final state it converges quadratically to the Galerkin solution, itself within $O(L^{-(s+1)})$ of the exact solution, whereas started directly from the sphere its first undamped step left the convex cone in our ellipsoid test. Experiments illustrate the rates, use the multiplier as a compatibility diagnostic, reconstruct convex polyhedra from facet normals and areas, and locate umbilics with indices.

papers.title: Exponential-Nemytskii Neural Operators: Learning Field Evolution Across Step Sizes
papers.abstract: In variable-step operator learning, agreement at observed step sizes does not by itself determine predictions at other temporal resolutions. We propose an operator whose step-size dependence is prescribed by a first-order Duhamel approximation of semilinear dynamics. It combines exact linear propagation with a local nonlinear function of the field and its derivatives, allowing evaluation below the observation interval without supervision densely sampled across step sizes. Under suitable conditions and at fixed spatial resolution, we prove that agreement between models at two step sizes controls their prediction differences throughout a prescribed range. We also give conditions for local identifiability of both components from two step sizes, supporting interpretation of the learned structure. A latent extension applies the same construction to learned fields. We evaluate the base model on two synthetic problems and the extension on two real datasets against several baselines.

papers.title: Comparing metric completions of triangulated categories with Verdier quotients
papers.abstract: Neeman's metric on a triangulated category assigns lengths to morphisms and allows us to construct triangulated metric completions of the category. We prove that the metric completion of a triangulated category with respect to a constant metric is always a subcategory of the Verdier quotient by the thick subcategory generated by cones of zero-length morphisms, and we provide a sufficient criterion for equality.
