papers.abstract: For a nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, let $ν(G)$ be the smallest {nonnegative} integer $\ell$ such that every zero-sum free sequence $T$ over $G$ of length at least $\ell$ has the following property: all nonzero elements of $G$ that do not occur as a subsequence sum of $T$ lie in a proper coset of some subgroup of $G$. It is easy to check that $\mathsf d (G)-1 \le ν(G) \le \mathsf d (G)$, where $\mathsf d (G)$ is the small Davenport constant of $G$. A conjecture by Gao from the year 2000 stated that equality should always hold at the lower bound. This conjecture has since been confirmed for many families of groups (including all p-groups and groups of rank at most two). In this paper, we disprove the conjecture.

papers.title: A proof of the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture for small volumes under a Ricci curvature lower bound
papers.abstract: We prove the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture, also known as the Aubin conjecture, in the small volume regime under a lower Ricci curvature bound, for any dimension $n\geq 2$. More precisely, we show that if $(M^n,g)$ is a Cartan-Hadamard manifold satisfying $\mathrm{Sec}_g\leq\bar k\leq 0$ and $\mathrm{Ric}_g\geq (n-1)\underline k$, then its isoperimetric profile is at least that of the model space of curvature $\bar k$ for small enough volumes. We also reduce the proof of the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture to establishing rigidity in the equality case.

papers.title: Generalized Bratteli diagrams without probability tail invariant measures
papers.abstract: The paper focuses on the following problem: given a generalized Bratteli diagram $B$, determine conditions under which the tail equivalence relation $\mathcal R$ does not admit a tail invariant probability measure on the path space $X_B$. We give several sufficient conditions, formulated in terms of the incidence matrices, that guarantee the nonexistence of such a measure. We also discuss a new spectral method for finding tail invariant measures for a class of stationary generalized Bratteli diagrams. This method allowed us to answer affirmatively an open problem formulated in arXiv:2212.13803.

papers.title: Multigraded Local Cohomology Categories: Homological Structure and Canonical Sources
papers.abstract: Let $S=\kk[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with its standard $\mathbb N^n$-grading, and let $\mathfrak m=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$. We study the essential images of the functors $M\mapsto H^i_{\mathfrak m}(M(-\mathbf1))$ on categories of positively determined $S$-modules, where $\mathbf1=(1,\ldots,1)$. For a fixed determining bound $\mathbf t\in\mathbb N^n$ and $0\le i<n$, we identify the image in degree $i$ with the category of finite-dimensional representations of the subposet of $[\mathbf0,\mathbf t]$ consisting of multidegrees with at least $n-i$ positive coordinates. These images are Serre subcategories of the category of negatively $\mathbf t$-determined modules. The top-degree image consists precisely of second cosyzygies in that category and is extension-closed, but is not abelian when $\mathbf t\ne\mathbf0$. For the non-top image categories, we determine attached primes from projective covers and compute the Bass numbers at $\mathfrak m$ and the injective dimensions over $S$ of projective and injective objects. In every non-top degree, we construct an exact functorial section selecting, for each nonzero target, a source of minimal projective dimension $n-i$ and maximal depth $i$ among all its sources. If $n\ge2$ and $\mathbf t\ge\mathbf1$, no fully faithful section exists in degrees $1$ and $n-1$, even without requiring exactness. In top degree, graded Matlis duality followed by $S$-duality gives a fully faithful functorial section. We also describe the global images obtained by varying the determining bound. The non-top global categories have enough injectives and no nonzero projective objects, while the top category corresponds to second cosyzygies in the category of finite-support representations of $\mathbb N^n$.

papers.title: Existence of regular sets in circulant quartic graphs: a complete characterization
papers.abstract: Let $Γ=(V,E)$ be a graph and let $a,b$ be nonnegative integers. A nonempty proper subset $C\subset V$ is an \emph{$(a,b)$-regular set} if each vertex of $C$ has exactly $a$ neighbors in $C$ and each vertex outside $C$ has exactly $b$ neighbors in $C$. Perfect codes and total perfect codes are the $(0,1)$- and $(1,1)$-regular sets. For every connected circulant quartic graph $\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_n,\{x^{\pm k},x^{\pm\ell}\})$ and every pair $(a,b)$ we decide, in terms of $n$, $k$ and $\ell$, whether an $(a,b)$-regular set exists. Existence is proved by exhibiting unions of residue classes; non-existence comes from a Fourier-analytic obstruction combined with the fact that certain sums of roots of unity cannot vanish.

papers.title: The list size of random linear and LDPC codes at capacity
papers.abstract: We show that for every prime power $q$ and $ρ\in(0,1-\frac1q)$ there exists $\varepsilon_0(q, ρ) > 0$ such that for all positive $\varepsilon < \varepsilon_0(q, ρ)$, a random linear code over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of rate $1-h_q(ρ)-\varepsilon$ has list size $\lfloor h_q(ρ)/\varepsilon\rfloor$ or $\lfloor h_q(ρ)/\varepsilon\rfloor+1$ with probability $1-o(1)$. Before this work, the list size was known only up to a constant factor for $q\ge3$, and for $q=2$ it was known to be either $\lfloor h_2(ρ)/\varepsilon\rfloor-1$, $\lfloor h_2(ρ)/\varepsilon\rfloor$ or $\lfloor h_2(ρ)/\varepsilon\rfloor+1$. We also show that the same two-point concentration holds for the list size of random LDPC codes. This follows from a general theorem establishing that random LDPC codes and random linear codes have the same threshold rate for distance, list decoding, list recovery from errors and any other \emph{convex} property, which answers a question of Mosheiff, Resch, Ron-Zewi, Silas and Wootters.

papers.title: Momentum in large-batch training: Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, Nesterov improves data efficiency
papers.abstract: We study when and how momentum improves large-batch training in the one-pass regime, using power-law kernel regression as a tractable setting. We first characterize stochastic stability through the \emph{critical learning rate}, defined as the largest learning rate for stable training, and obtain $η_{\mathrm{SGD}}^{\mathrm{crit}}\eqsim 1$, $η_{\mathrm{Polyak}}^{\mathrm{crit}}\eqsim \min\{1,B(1-β)\}$, and $η_{\mathrm{Nesterov}}^{\mathrm{crit}}\eqsim \min\{1,B^q(1-β)\}$, where $B$ is the batch size, $β\in[0,1)$ is the momentum factor, and \(q>1\) is the capacity exponent governing spectral decay. Within the stable region, we derive scaling laws for the full risk dynamics, capturing the progression from an early transient through power-law decay to a noise floor. We then optimize the final-step risk under a fixed data budget, obtaining a three-regime phase diagram that reveals how the benefits of momentum change with batch size. Notably, Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, the largest batch size preserving the optimal small-batch data-scaling exponent, thereby allowing fewer sequential updates without sacrificing data efficiency. In contrast, Nesterov improves the optimal data-scaling exponent in the large-batch regime through look-ahead-induced suppression of noise amplification. Experiments on PLK regression quantitatively support the theoretical scaling predictions, while neural-network experiments provide qualitative evidence for the predicted batch-size dependence and stability behavior.

papers.title: Total positivity in coordinate algebras
papers.abstract: We define the totally positive part of the coordinate algebra associated to a Cartan datum of simply laced type. We show its relation to the canonical basis of the corresponding plus part of the enveloping algebra.

papers.title: Equivariant formality and representation theory
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group and $K$ its connected Lie subgroup. Using the $K$-theoretic version of equivariant formality developed in [F2] which involves analysis of vector bundles over $G/K$, we find two characterizations of equivariant formality of the isotropy action of $K$ on $G/K$. The first one equates equivariant formality with a "smoothness" condition of the restriction map of the representation ring of $G$ to that of $K$. The second characterization asserts that equivariant formality amounts to the equivariant $K$-theoretic index pairing of two certain special $K$-theory classes being nontrivial in some sense. By applying these characterizations, we are able to give a representation theoretic criterion for equivariant formality of the isotropy action by a circle subgroup, as well as an invariant theory criterion for the case where $K$ is a torus of dimension one less than the rank of $G$, culminating in a complete classification of equivariant formality where $G$ is further assumed to be simple.

papers.title: Higher-order Approximate Symmetries
papers.abstract: The Fushchych--Shtelen (FS) construction of approximate symmetries, based on a triangular system for the coefficients of a solution expansion, is extended to arbitrary order. A coefficient-map formulation establishes, under explicit hypotheses, a correspondence with the Baikov--Gazizov--Ibragimov (BGI) method. The two approaches are compared for a perturbed cubic wave equation. Nonlinearities admitting an FS point symmetry with prescribed projection onto the unperturbed dilation are classified through second order, up to equivalences. They comprise a power family and logarithmic families at exceptional exponents. Nonlinearities admitting second-order BGI point symmetries that continue this dilation are also classified. Among perturbations nontrivial at first order, these form a proper subfamily of one FS family; another family is admitted by both methods when the perturbation first enters at second order. Joint reduction by the Lorentz algebra and the inherited FS dilation yields explicit invariant solutions for all FS normal forms and recovers the first-order solutions of Fushchych and Shtelen. For the common family with a nontrivial first-order perturbation, the logarithmic corrections arise from expanding a power law with a perturbation-dependent exponent. Periodic traveling waves illustrate the long-scale validity of the FS expansion. The first correction is obtained by quadrature, second-order secular terms are identified, and phase renormalization yields bounded approximations. For integer-power members of the power family, the amplitude dependence of the corrected wavenumber agrees with the symmetry scaling weights.

papers.title: Properties of the $\mathcal V$-Monoid of Weighted Leavitt Path Algebras
papers.abstract: For a row-finite weighted graph $(E,w)$, Preusser showed that the monoid $\mathcal{V}(L_k(E,w))$ of finitely generated projective modules over the weighted Leavitt path algebra $L_k(E,w)$ is isomorphic to a combinatorially defined weighted graph monoid $\mathcal{M}(E,w)$. We study two structural properties of $\mathcal{M}(E,w)$: confluence and cancellativity. We introduce a reduction system on the free commutative monoid presenting $\mathcal{M}(E,w)$, obtain sufficient conditions for non-confluence by constructing explicit non-confluent triples, and provide a complete confluence characterization for certain classes of weighted graphs. Turning to cancellativity, we work within Preusser's class of weighted graphs satisfying Condition (LPA), for which $L_k(E,w)$ is isomorphic to an unweighted Leavitt path algebra $L_k(F)$ via a two-step construction. We introduce an auxiliary graph associated to the intermediate step of this construction and use it to give a graph-theoretic characterization of when $\mathcal{M}(E,w)$ is cancellative. Finally, under Condition (LPA), we show that Preusser's construction upgrades to a graded isomorphism $L_k(E,w) \cong_{\operatorname{gr}} L_k(F)$ with respect to the standard $\mathbb{Z}^{λ(E,w)}$-grading of weighted Leavitt path algebras, yielding $\mathcal{V}^{\operatorname{gr}}(L_k(E,w)) \cong \mathcal{V}^{\operatorname{gr}}(L_k(F))$ as $\mathbb{Z}^{λ(E,w)}$-monoids.

papers.title: Compactifications of Abelian Group Bundles and a Topological Halmos--von Neumann-type Theorem
papers.abstract: The topological Halmos--von Neumann theorem is a fundamental result of topological dynamics that completely classifies continuous actions of abelian topological groups which are ergodic and have discrete spectrum. It rests on a correspondence between such actions (up to the choice of a distinguished point), compactifications of the acting group and subgroups of its dual group. We generalize both the classical statement and the underlying categorical equivalences to the framework of open group bundles over locally compact base spaces. As a byproduct, we establish a Pontryagin-type duality between étale Hausdorff abelian group bundles and open proper Hausdorff abelian group bundles, extending the classical duality between discrete and compact abelian groups.

papers.title: On bubbling of Fueter maps
papers.abstract: We study bubbling for sequences of solutions of the Hamiltonian-perturbed Fueter equation. By Walpuski's compactness theorem, a bounded-energy sequence converges weakly to a Fueter map, with energy loss recorded by a defect measure supported on a codimension 2 rectifiable set. Assuming that the limiting map has no non-removable singularities and the bubbles attach to it on a subset of the bubbling locus of positive measure, we show that the limiting Hamiltonian lies in an exceptional subset of infinite codimension. The proof combines quantitative control of rational sweepout loci in hyperkähler manifolds with a transversality argument. We expect the attachment assumption to be automatic and follow from a suitable no-neck result. This strongly suggests that, in the absence of non-removable singularities, bubbling of Hamiltonian-perturbed Fueter maps is highly nongeneric.

papers.title: Stable Symmetric Series, Differential Operators, and Jack Deformations
papers.abstract: We introduce stable symmetric series which encode normalized conjugacy classes and their multiplication operators simultaneously for all symmetric groups. This gives a direct route from the Ivanov--Kerov algebra to shifted symmetric functions and to differential operators in $U(\mathcal W_{1+\infty})$. Using the Goulden--Jackson product, we extend the construction to Jack polynomials, recover shifted Jack eigenvalues and Pieri-type relations, and obtain explicit candidate operators in degrees three and four. Their real and quaternionic specializations to zonal polynomials are verified by Gaussian matrix integrals and exhaustive Wick enumeration.

papers.title: Complexity of Arc-Decompositions involving Perfect Matchings and Cycle Factors
papers.abstract: For two digraph properties $P_1$ and $P_2$, a $(P_1,P_2)$-arc-decomposition of a digraph $D$ is a partition $A(D)=A_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}A_2$ such that the spanning subdigraphs $D[A_1]$ and $D[A_2]$ have properties $P_1$ and $P_2$, respectively. We prove that it is NP-complete to decide whether a digraph admits an arc-decomposition with properties $(P_1,P_2)$ where $(P_1,P_2)\in \{$(perfect matching, having no odd cycle), (perfect matching, strong), (perfect matching, having an out-branching), (cycle factor, having no odd cycle)$\}$. All four problems remain NP-complete even when restricted to strongly connected digraphs. We also prove that every strongly connected digraph with minimum semi-degree at least three contains two vertex-disjoint cycles whose simultaneous arc deletion leaves the digraph strongly connected. These results settle some open problems posed by Bang-Jensen, Bessy, Gonçalves, and Picasarri-Arrieta [Theoret. Comput. Sci. 928 (2022), 167--182].

papers.title: A general-purpose multi-path stacked coupling for stochastic reaction networks
papers.abstract: Stochastic reaction networks are continuous-time Markov chain models for interacting populations, with applications in biochemistry, epidemiology, ecology, and related areas. Coupling multiple stochastic reaction networks effectively is a fundamental challenge in stochastic simulation. Existing variance-reducing coupling methods are typically designed for pairs of processes, though specialized multi-path constructions have been developed for particular applications. To fill this gap, we introduce the multi-path stacked coupling (MSC), a space-time Poisson construction that jointly simulates a finite collection of stochastic reaction networks with common reaction channels and reaction vectors, but possibly different intensity functions and initial conditions. Each pairwise marginal of MSC has the same law as the corresponding split-coupled pair, allowing existing variance bounds to transfer directly; in finite-state settings, we also obtain first-order expansions for the mean and second moment of finite-difference numerators. We demonstrate the framework through three sensitivity estimation tasks requiring several nearby parameterized paths: estimating many first derivatives simultaneously, estimating a single first derivative using a wider finite-difference stencil, and estimating higher-order derivatives. Numerical experiments on a processive phosphorylation network demonstrate strong performance in each of the three application areas considered, consistent with the theoretical advantages of MSC: across all three applications, MSC achieves the smallest root mean square error (RMSE) among the methods considered over the tested computational budgets.

papers.title: Interior curvature estimates for convex solutions of a prescribed curvature quotient equation
papers.abstract: In this note, we prove a priori interior curvature bounds for convex solutions to an elliptic Weingarten curvature quotient equation. The proof avoids integral estimates, doubling inequalities and compactness arguments. It relies on a concavity inequality for the equation operator and a novel choice of the auxiliary function to carry out an elementary maximum-principle argument. As an application, we obtain interior curvature bounds for convex solutions of a prescribed special Lagrangian curvature equation in dimensions three and four.

papers.title: Kähler landscapes for complex neural network descents and guarantees including a search and destroy of the Calabi-Yau manifold
papers.abstract: We study landscapes for complex-parameterized networks. Our approach is motivated with an information-theoretic manifold perspective of the parameter and via classical optimization guarantees although of complex geometric variety such as through Dolbeault asymptotics. The descent path admits a Kähler information metric under a cross-entropy via the Wirtinger Hessian on the log-likelihood potential. We restrict attention to a descent update rule with natural gradient descent via a differentiated loss scaled by the inverse metric, so the descent path remains in the holomorphic tangent bundle. We emphasize Calabi-Yau information manifolds which profane theoretical guarantees via an ill-curvature-conditioned, or lack thereof, landscape. We focus on Calabi-Yau metrics specifically in a non-compact setting with a global potential, so defined geometrically rather than invoking the topological requirements of the Calabi conjecture. In non-compact settings, we can write the metric determinant with respect to a background in terms of a function, pluriharmonic or real. Using Yau's Liouville theorem, we get a partial eigenvalue blow-up effect. In an empirical setting, a Ricci-flat metric will not form, but a blow-up can be a local condition and can hold empirically on open sets even partially in generalized Kähler cases due to lower bounds on the Ricci potential. Moreover, it has been discovered that negative curvature subverts the loss landscape, specifically sectional curvature, so we expand on this and draw interconnections to negative-definite Ricci curvature. Our arguments primarily exist via geometric modality, although we establish roots in deep learning theory such as through asymptotics at initialization and connections through failure modes of neural network guarantees under vanishing and negative Ricci curvature.

papers.title: Understanding Non-Split 2-Group Symmetry: (3+1)D SymTFT, Anomaly and Bordism
papers.abstract: We present a systematic study of finite, non-split 2-group symmetries with a non-trivial Postnikov class, focusing on the simplest example with a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 0-form symmetry and a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ 1-form symmetry, intertwined together by the non-trivial Postnikov class in $H^3(B\mathbb{Z}_2;\mathbb{Z}_2)\cong\mathbb{Z}_2$, denoted by $\mathcal{G}$. We classify the anomalies of this 2-group symmetry for physical theories in $d$-dimensional spacetime, by computing the oriented bordism groups $Ω_{d+1}^{\rm SO}(B\mathcal{G})$ and the spin bordism groups $Ω_{d+1}^{\rm Spin}(B\mathcal{G})$ for $d\leq 5$. For the case of $d=3$, we investigate the Symmetry TFT/TO of the 2-group symmetry $\mathcal{G}$ using the language of fusion 2-categories, as well as (3+1)D TQFT actions, for the cases without or with the 2-group anomaly classified by $\operatorname{Hom}\left(\widetildeΩ_4^{\rm SO}(B\mathcal{G}),U(1)\right) \cong H^4(B\mathcal{G};U(1))\cong\mathbb{Z}_2$. We classify the minimal topological and physical boundary conditions of the Symmetry TFTs, and carry out the categorical Landau paradigm for such a non-split finite 2-group.

papers.title: Mirror functor for deformed preprojective algebras
papers.abstract: We construct noncommutative mirrors from the bulk-deformed Floer theory of compact immersed Lagrangians equipped with higher rank flat bundles, whose Floer theory can have non-zero curvature terms due to contributions of stable constant discs. For a nodal union of Lagrangian spheres, codimension-two bulk cycles meeting the compact core produce the additive deformed preprojective relations and the corresponding framed Maurer-Cartan spaces at nonzero complex moment-map levels. In particular, our localized mirror functors produce noncommutative ADHM and Nakajima monadic complexes. We obtain local charts and gluing maps of the noncommutative mirror varieties via explicit computations of Lagrangian deformation spaces and Fukaya isomorphisms between them. These constructions recover noncommutative spaces studied by Kapustin-Kuznetsov-Orlov, Baranovsky-Ginzburg-Kuznetsov, and Kawamata, with further examples in dimension three. We also establish the categorical framework in the unobstructed setting. For a compact $\mathbb Z$-graded unobstructed immersed Lagrangian $\mathbb{L}$ without nonpositive-degree immersed generators, Koszul duality identifies the derived Fukaya subcategory generated by $\mathbb{L}$ with the derived category of modules with finite-dimensional total cohomology over its extended localized mirror $\tilde{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{L}}$. This construction starts from the Floer algebra of the compact reference brane and does not require a global wrapped generator. Applications to plumbings recover known split-generation results for compact objects.

papers.title: A Fitting criterion for quasi-Gorenstein local rings
papers.abstract: We prove that a Noetherian local ring $R$ with canonical module $ω_R$ is quasi-Gorenstein if and only if $\Fitt_1^R(ω_R) \cong ω_R$. This settles the expectation of Eisenbud, Ficarra, Herzog, and Moradi on canonical ideals.

papers.title: A dichotomy for minimal submanifolds
papers.abstract: We survey a circle of recent results showing that a minimal submanifold obeys a dichotomy: either it fills up space, spreading out like a space-filling curve, or it is confined, and confinement forces quantitative restrictions. On the confined side these restrictions are both geometric and function-theoretic: Euclidean volume growth, an optimal rate of convergence of the density, complex-curve rigidity for stable surfaces in $\bf{R}^4$, and a Liouville theorem forcing slowly growing harmonic functions on minimal disks to be constant. A prototypical restriction is Euclidean volume growth, which in these results is forced by the geometry rather than assumed. The mechanism is a volume doubling theorem that converts geometric confinement into quantitative rigidity: a stationary integral varifold trapped in a thin slab at a given scale cannot double its volume by more than a universal factor. We explain how this principle, and the height-excess bounds behind it, produce Euclidean volume growth for submanifolds of sublinearly growing height in every dimension and codimension, the optimal density rate in a slab, the complex-curve and Liouville rigidity above, a higher-codimension Bernstein theorem for disks, one-sided volume bounds, and an optimal stable Bernstein theorem in all dimensions generalizing Moser, Bombieri-De Giorgi-Miranda, Caffarelli-Nirenberg-Spruck and Ecker-Huisken. We describe three regimes with sharp borderlines. In narrow cones the volume grows polynomially with exponent $n+O(\varepsilon^2)$, and the order $\varepsilon^2$ is attained; in wide cones the growth can be arbitrarily fast. For holomorphic curves in $\mathbb{C}^2$, there are also three regimes and the borderline is determined by the Kähler angle.

papers.title: Notes on the Kuznetsov component of cubic sevenfolds
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be a cubic 7-fold. When $Y$ is smooth, its Kuznetsov component is a Calabi-Yau category of dimension 3, and we construct an embedding of the Kuznetsov component into the derived category of Clifford modules over $\mathbb{P}^4$. When $Y$ is a general cubic 7-fold singular along a line, we construct an explicit weakly crepant categorical resolution of its Kuznetsov component by the derived category of a smooth Calabi-Yau 3-fold, recovering a result of Favero-Kelly. In this construction, we express the resolution functor explicitly as a composition of geometric functors and mutations, and identify its kernel with a category equivalent to a pull-back of the derived category of a stacky curve.

papers.title: Analysis and structure-preserving discretization of the Heat-GLM system
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a prototype hyperbolic system arising from the coupling of Generalized-Lagrangian-Multiplier (GLM) curl-cleaning with linear acoustics. We first show that, in the absence of dissipation, the equations can be rigorously derived from an underlying variational principle and that the resulting system is symmetric-hyperbolic. Further analysis shows that it not only conserves the total energy but also admits a set of invariants consisting of quadratic combinations of differential operators applied to the state variables. The addition of a stiff relaxation source term allows the system to be extended to dissipative dynamics, describing, for example, Cattaneo-type heat transfer processes that are asymptotically compatible with the Fourier law in the stiff relaxation limit; in this case, the total energy and invariants are dissipated accordingly. A new semi-implicit compatible numerical scheme on staggered grids is developed to solve this system while exactly preserving its key properties at the discrete level. In particular, we prove that the scheme is asymptotic-preserving in the Fourier limit, with a convergence rate depending on the initial data. We also show that the scheme conserves exactly the total energy as well as all the invariants in the absence of relaxation, and dissipates them consistently in its presence. These findings are demonstrated on a set of representative test cases.

papers.title: Essential-Surface Complexes of Knot Exteriors: Image, Kernel, and Reconstruction
papers.abstract: This is an expository article. The curve complex of a surface is deliberately forgetful, yet in most cases its automorphism group recovers the mapping class group. We explain what happens when the same question is asked for the essential-surface complex $\mathcal{ES}(E)$ of a knot exterior $E=E(K)$, equivalently Schultens's initial surface complex $\mathcal{S}_0(E)$. The discussion is organized around three questions: which combinatorial symmetries are geometric (the image), which homeomorphisms are invisible (the kernel), and how much of $E$ can be read off from the complex (reconstruction). The basic objects are first drawn in classical examples, and the general framework is introduced only afterwards. We collect the elementary structural facts that organize the subject -- the flag property, the layering by boundary slope, finite dimension, unbounded dimension for iterated cables, and Kakimizu's complexes as full subcomplexes -- and compare with handlebodies and connected sums of $S^2\times S^1$, where image and kernel are known completely. Along the way we record two short consequences that we have not found stated in this form: for a slope-separated knot every orientation-preserving mapping class acts trivially, and the image is $\mathbb{Z}/2$ exactly when the knot is amphichiral and a nonzero boundary slope occurs; and for a connected sum of nonfibered prime knots the decomposing-annulus twist translates Banks's winding coordinate. A table separates what is classical from what is recorded here. The article closes with a three-task formulation of the rigidity problem, a list of problems with their current status, a worked two-bridge recipe, and a guide to further reading.

papers.title: On the embedding rigidity problem for uniformly locally finite coarse spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct countable uniformly locally finite metric spaces $X$ and $Y$ such that $C_u^*(X)$ is isomorphic to a hereditary $C^*$-subalgebra of $C_u^*(Y)$, but neither space coarsely embeds into the other. This gives a negative answer to the embedding rigidity problem for uniformly locally finite coarse spaces. On the positive side, we prove that a hereditary embedding $C_u^*(X)\to C_u^*(Y)$ implies an injective coarse embedding $X\to Y$ whenever $C_u^*(Y)$ contains no block-rank-one ghost projection. In particular, this strengthens the coarse embedding theorem of Braga, Farah, and Vignati by obtaining injectivity under the same hypothesis that every sparse subspace of $Y$ yields only compact ghost projections.

papers.title: Elliptic Superlevel Sets in the Class $\OO_C$: Boundary-Layer Geometry and Stability of the Return Map
papers.abstract: We study elliptic superlevel geometry and return dynamics for the class $\mathcal{O}_{C}$. Let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^{N}$ be a compact strictly convex core, and $Ω\in \mathcal{O}_{C}$ a bounded domain whose boundary is a global normal graph over $\partial C$ with inward normals returning to $\operatorname{int} C$. For $-Δu = f$ in $Ω$ ($u=0$ on $\partialΩ$), with $f \geq 0$, $f \not\equiv 0$, $\operatorname{supp} f \Subset \operatorname{int} C$, we analyze the superlevel sets $Ω_{t} = \{u > t\}$ for $t \downarrow 0$. We prove that for small $t > 0$, $\partialΩ_{t}$ is a global normal graph given by $\partialΩ_{t} = \{c + d_{t}(c)ν(c) : c \in \partial C\}$, satisfying $\|d_{t} - d_{0}\|_{C^{1}} = O(t)$ and $d_{t} = d_{0} - t b_{0} + o_{C^{1}}(t)$, where $b_{0}$ depends on the Hopf derivative and transversality. Using normal-graph formulas, we show $Ω_{t} \in \mathcal{O}_{C}$. The return maps $F_{t} : \partial C \to \partial C$ are well-defined, satisfying $\|F_{t} - F_{0}\|_{L^{\infty}} = O(t)$ and $F_{t} = F_{0} + t \mathcal{A}_{0} + o_{L^{\infty}}(t)$. For any sequence $t_{n} \downarrow 0$, the non-autonomous system $x_{n+1} = F_{t_{n}}(x_{n})$ is asymptotically autonomous with background map $F_{0}$. These results bridge elliptic boundary-layer deformation and return-map dynamics relative to a convex core.

papers.title: p-adic Properties of Translated Division Polynomials and Somos Sequences
papers.abstract: We study the periodicity and $p$-adic convergence of sequences of values of the translated division polynomials $(Ψ_n(P))_{n\geq 0}$, $(Φ_n(P))_{n\geq 0}$, and $(Ω_n(P))_{n\geq 0}$ evaluated at a pair of points on an elliptic curve. We prove that these sequences are purely periodic over finite fields. We then use their periodicity properties to prove that certain subsequences are $\mathbb{Z}_p$-Cauchy. Applying this result to Somos 4 and Somos 5 sequences yields analogous convergence results. We also establish pure periodicity modulo prime powers for the even- and odd-indexed subsequences of Somos 5 sequences under suitable hypotheses.

papers.title: Sketch-and-Restart: Randomized Sketching in Quadrature-Based Restarting for Matrix Functions
papers.abstract: We develop a sketch-and-restart framework for computing the action of a matrix function on a vector, $f(A) b$, where $A$ is large, sparse, and non-Hermitian. The framework combines quadrature-based restarting with Arnoldi-like decompositions generated by sketched or truncated Arnoldi processes. Within this framework, we develop two classes of restarted algorithms. The first uses a fixed Krylov subspace dimension and is based either on the sketched Arnoldi process or on a new sketched harmonic Arnoldi process proposed in this work. The second class chooses the Krylov subspace dimension adaptively by running the truncated Arnoldi process until the condition number of the generated basis, estimated from its sketch, exceeds a prescribed threshold. We also establish the convergence of the restarted sketched harmonic Arnoldi method for Stieltjes functions under the assumption that $A$ is positive real. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, including the computational savings achieved through sketching, the storage reduction enabled by adaptive truncation, and the acceleration obtained from thick restarting.

papers.title: Statistics on Yau's conjecture: Variance asymptotics
papers.abstract: We investigate the probabilistic counterpart of Yau's conjecture on the nodal volume of Laplace eigenfunctions on compact manifolds, by studying the high-frequency variance asymptotics of Riemannian random waves. Theorem A gives quantitative bounds on the fluctuations of their nodal volume for all regimes of spectral windows, including the monochromatic one, of spectral size 1. For every non-monochromatic window the variance has the exact order $1/N$, where $N$ is the dimension of the underlying space of eigenfunctions, on any compact manifold. In the monochromatic regime, on manifolds without conjugate points and in particular on negatively curved ones, we prove that the variance is $o(1/N)$: this improves the previous best bound, cf. Canzani and Hanin 2020, to its square divided by a logarithmic factor, and exhibits a form of Berry's cancellation, relative to the natural scale $1/N$, for monochromatic random waves on such chaotic manifolds. Our proofs rely on a local and global analysis combining the Kac-Rice formula, the Wiener--Itô chaos decomposition recently obtained by the authors Stecconi and Todino 2025, and a sharp analysis of the error in the pointwise Weyl law associated to an arbitrary spectral window (Theorem B). We also introduce a general machinery (Theorem C) that yields variance decay for the nodal volume of an arbitrary Gaussian field under broad geometric conditions, subject to correlation decay assumptions.

papers.title: General position on Brauer--Severi surfaces
papers.abstract: The blowing-up of the projective plane at a finite set of points yields a del Pezzo surface if and only if the points lie in general position. In this note, we generalize this result to Brauer--Severi surfaces over arbitrary ground fields. Using Galois descent, intersection theory and combinatorial arguments, we provide explicit arithmetic and geometric conditions on the centre of the blowing-up.

papers.title: An Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian solver for relativistic detonation waves
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the dynamics of relativistic detonation waves theoretically and numerically. The reaction is physically accounted for by an extra term in the definition of the total energy density and by an additional equation for the evolution of the mass fraction of the reactant, while leaving formally unmodified the equations of mass and energy-momentum conservation. In this way, the Rankine-Hugoniot relations maintain the same formal structure of the inert version. For the numerical solution we use a finite volume ALE scheme with a second order TVD space-time reconstruction for the homogeneous part of the system, where the mesh velocity is chosen equal to the shock speed, and we combine it through operator splitting with a locally implicit algorithm for the potentially stiff reaction source terms that arise in the equation of the reactant. We furthermore propose a particularly efficient algorithm for the conversion from the conserved to the primitive variables, which for the relativistic Euler equations is known to be nontrivial. Following this approach, we can successfully solve the Zel'dovich-von Neumann-Doering profile of a relativistic detonation wave, up to Lorentz factors of the shock front $γ_s\sim 7$. Our analysis allowed us to highlight a new special relativistic effect, which has remained unnoticed so far. While in Newtonian detonations the Zel'dovich pressure jump decreases monotonically with the mass flux through the shock front, in the relativistic case it shows a minimum and then rises monotonically as a function of the mass flux. This may have interesting physical implications on the amount of energy that can be extracted from a relativistic detonation wave.

papers.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. Part 8: Isomorphism series, digraph and graph of $C_n(R)$
papers.abstract: This article is the $8^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}. In this study, we define {\em isomorphic set}, {\em isomorphism series}, {\em isomorphism digraph} or {\em isomorphism diagram} $\mathcal{D}$ and {\em isomorphism graph} $\mathcal{G}$ of circulant graphs and obtain these corresponding to $C_{16}(R)$, $C_{27}(S)$ and $C_{54}(1,3,17,19)$ and present the isomorphism digraph and the isomorphism graph of $C_{432}(T)$ which has isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 2,3 and of $C_{6750}(U)$ which has isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 3,5 where $T$ = $\{16, 27, 48, 54, 128, 160, 189\}$ and $U$ = $\{135, 243, 250, 750, 1107, 1593, 2000, 2457, 2500, 2943\}$. We also define {\em diameter of isomorphic set} of $C_n(R)$ and {\em isomorphic distance} between any two circulant graphs. We find that the order of isomorphic sets of $C_{432}(T)$ and $C_{6750}(U)$ are 36 and 450 and their diameters are 3 and 3, respectively.

papers.title: Anti-Zariski pairs
papers.abstract: In 1929, O. Zariski found a pair of complex plane algebraic curves of the same degree and with the same collection of singularities, but embedded into the plane in a topologically different way. Accordingly, such curves belong to different components of the equisingular family. This phenomenon has been intensively studied till now. In this note, we propose a different insight on this subject: Two curves $C',C''\subset\PP^2$ form an {\it anti-Zariski pair}, if $(\PP^2,C')$ and $(\PP^2,C'')$ are homeomorhic, but $C'$ and $C''$ belong to different components of the equisingular family. We exhibit examples of anti-Zariski pairs and discuss related issues.

papers.title: Derived categories of log del Pezzo surfaces with $\frac13(1,1)$ singularities
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a log del Pezzo surface with only $\frac13(1,1)$ singularities. We compare the derived categories of its minimal resolution, canonical stack, and singular surface. For every family in the Corti--Heuberger classification, Orlov's blow-up formula and the Ishii--Ueda correspondence give explicit full exceptional collections on the canonical stacks, of length $12-K_X^2+\frac{4k}{3}$ when $X$ has $k$ singular points. In the one-point index-one cascade, the canonical stacks are blow-ups of the weighted projective stack $\mathbb P(1,1,3)$ at distinct smooth points and admit explicit full strong exceptional collections of line bundles. For quasismooth hypersurfaces $X_{10}\subset\mathbb P(1,2,3,5)$, we construct a full strong exceptional collection of $13$ objects with an explicitly computed Euler matrix. The exceptional lattice determines the Brauer group: $\mathrm{Br}(X)=0$ for $k\leq5$, while $\mathrm{Br}(X)\cong\mathbb Z/3$ for $k=6$. We construct semiorthogonal decompositions of $D^b(\mathrm{coh}\,X)$ for the one- and three-point cascades and of a Brauer-twisted derived category for the six-point cascade.

papers.title: Uniqueness of the blow-up for some Alt-Phillips cones
papers.abstract: We establish uniqueness of blow-ups, with sharp quantitative convergence, for several classes of singular minimizing cones in the Alt-Phillips problem, in the range $γ\in(0,2)$. As a consequence, we obtain uniqueness at every free boundary point in dimensions $d=2,3,4$ for $γ\in(1,2)$, and in dimensions $d\geq 5$ for $γ\in\left(1,\frac32\right)$. The proof of uniqueness is based on three new logarithmic epiperimetric inequalities. The sharp distinction between polynomial and logarithmic convergence is governed by a finite-dimensional integrability condition (sub-integrability) for the spherical linearized problem. We prove this sharpness for the radial cone and its cylindrical extensions through an explicit integrability and bifurcation analysis, showing in particular that logarithmic convergence may be sharp even in dimension two. In contrast, we show that the one-dimensional cone is exceptional: although the integrability condition fails, the convergence is polynomial. Finally, we characterize the minimality of the radial cone in terms of $d$ and $γ$ by means of a one-dimensional calibration argument, exhibiting in dimension $d\geq6$ a nontrivial regime in which the radial cone is stable but not minimizing.

papers.title: PhysGuard: Fisher-Guided Gradient Projection for Sim-to-Real Neural PDE Surrogates
papers.abstract: Neural operator models trained on simulation data often lose accuracy when applied to experimental measurements due to the sim-to-real gap. Standard fine-tuning with limited real data can reduce this gap, but it may also damage the core physics-relevant representations learned during pretraining. Although knowledge-preserving adaptation has been widely investigated in vision or language tasks, it remains unclear whether these methods are suitable for neural operators whose architectures and protected knowledge are fundamentally different. Neural operators need to preserve core-scale physical structures rather than semantic or visual features. We propose PhysGuard, a physics-preserving framework for accurate sim-to-real adaptation of neural operators. Specifically, PhysGuard uses the empirical Fisher Information Matrix computed on simulation data to identify physics-critical parameter directions, then restricts fine-tuning updates to directions that do not interfere with them. A layer-wise Gram-matrix formulation makes this efficient for models with millions of parameters, while an adaptive threshold automatically determines the protected subspace size. A spectral probe experiment shows that the dominant Fisher directions are strongly associated with low-frequency output structures. Experiments on benchmark across four neural operator architectures and different physical systems show that PhysGuard performs strongly on most evaluation metrics compared to baselines. The benefits are most evident under severe domain shift, where it reduces low-frequency error by up to 32% compared to standard fine-tuning while maintaining adaptability. Our code is available at https://github.com/Data-Driven-Computational-Geotechnics/PhysGuard.

papers.title: Boltzmann-like occupation of nonequilibrium steady states on dense disordered networks
papers.abstract: A central problem in statistical physics is to extend the Boltzmann distribution to nonequilibrium steady states (NESS). We prove that NESS on large dense disordered networks have Boltzmann-like occupation despite extensive entropy production. One consequence is that such NESS can conceal their nonequilibrium nature from measurements of static response to energy perturbations. We further prove that the active-matter heuristic of "low rattling" is asymptotically exact for these NESS. Intuitively, they spend a greater fraction of their time in states they leave more slowly. We show that rattling effectively extends the Boltzmann distribution to such NESS, as well as the broader class of "equiaccessible" steady states, which play a role in our analysis akin to that of equilibrium in linear response.

papers.title: Twin Algebras: Condensable Algebras beyond Anyons
papers.abstract: Condensable algebras in 2+1d non-chiral topological orders characterize gapped boundary conditions and interfaces. Applied to the Symmetry Topological Field Theory, they allow classification of symmetric gapped phases and impose sharp constraints on possible phase transitions. A condensable algebra is specified not only by its underlying set of anyons, which end on the boundary or interface, but also by its algebra structure. We introduce the concept of twin condensable algebras, which have the same anyon decomposition, but inequivalent algebra structure. We revisit the classification of condensable algebras in $\mathcal{Z}(\text{Vec}_G^ω)$, i.e. in group-theoretical topological orders for finite groups $G$ with anomaly $ω$. In this context we are able to identify twin algebras that arise from different mechanisms, such as subgroup data, SPT cocycles, and symmetry actions. In particular, we construct infinite families of examples of twins from so-called Gassmann triples, and exhibit cases in which the reduced topological orders are inequivalent despite having identical anyon content. Physically, twin algebras describe distinct symmetric phases that have isomorphic spaces of ground states, but inequivalent order parameters. Such twin phases never exhibit relative spontaneous symmetry breaking, and can be used to construct phase transitions without hidden symmetry breaking, which are intrinsically beyond Landau transitions.

papers.title: Minimal submanifolds confined in space
papers.abstract: Already in $\mathbb{R}^4$, there are many minimal hypersurfaces but few structural results. The half-space theorem fails there: higher-dimensional catenoids are among the many examples contained in a slab. Nevertheless, we show that in any dimension and codimension, the height of a minimal submanifold controls its volume growth: confinement to a narrow cone forces polynomial growth, and sublinear height forces Euclidean growth, the slowest possible. Thus volume bounds, which regularity theory assumes, follow from height alone. The key is a volume doubling theorem that converts geometric confinement into quantitative rigidity: if an $n$-dimensional stationary integral varifold lies in a thin slab at a given scale, then its volume doubling ratio at that scale is bounded by a universal constant. Iterating this gives the polynomial growth bounds above. Sublinear height is exactly the borderline for Euclidean growth: examples grow at least like $r^{n+4ε^2/5}$ in cones of aperture $ε$. From Euclidean volume growth, we obtain an optimal Bernstein theorem, in all dimensions, for stable minimal hypersurfaces with sublinear height growth, generalizing results of Moser, Bombieri--De Giorgi--Miranda, Trudinger, Caffarelli--Nirenberg--Spruck, and Ecker--Huisken.

papers.title: A Study on Type-2 Isomorphic Circulant Graphs: Part 7: $C_{432}(R)$, $C_{6750}(S)$ - each has 2 types of Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs
papers.abstract: In this study, we obtain two families of circulant graphs, (i) family of circulant graphs $C_{432}(R)$, each has isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 2 as well as $m$ = 3; and (ii) family of circulant graphs $C_{6750}(S)$, each has isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 3 as well as $m$ = 5. This article is the $7^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}.

papers.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. PART 9: Computer programs to show Type-1 $\&$ -2 isomorphic circulant graphs
papers.abstract: Elspas and Turner \cite{eltu} raised a question on the isomorphism of $C_{16}(1,3,7)$ and $C_{16}(2,3,5)$ and Vilfred \cite{v96} gave its answer by defining Type-2 isomorphism of $C_n(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ $\ni$ $m$ = $\gcd(n, r) > 1$ and also modified to $m$ and $m^3$ divides $\gcd(n, r)$ and $n$, respectively, $r\in R$ and $r,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and studied such graphs \cite{v13,v20, v2-1}. Using a $C^{++}$ computer program, the authors obtained families of Type-2 isomorphic $C_{n}(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ = 2,3,5,7 for $n\in\mathbb{N}$ as well as $C_{np^3}(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ = $p$ where $p$ is a prime and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. In this paper, we present the $C^{++}$ program and also a VB program POLY415.EXE which is used to show how Type-1 and Type-2 isomorphisms of a circulant graph take place as well as for checking and finding Type-1 and Type-2 circulant graphs of a given order. This article is the $9^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}.

papers.title: Tautological modular forms of level two and degree two
papers.abstract: We show how to use divisors on the projectivized Hodge bundle to construct special vector-valued modular forms and then apply invariant theory to construct all vector-valued Siegel modular forms of level two and degree two. Thus we construct all modular forms in terms of certain basic modular forms that are intimately connected to the moduli of curves of genus two.

papers.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. Part 6: Abelian groups $(T2_{n,m}(C_n(R)), \circ)$ and $(V_{n,m}(C_n(R)), \circ)$
papers.abstract: This article is the $6^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}. In this part, we define $V_{n,m}(C_n(R))$ and Type-2 set $T2_{n,m}(C_n(R))$ of $C_n(R)$ and present their properties. We prove that $(V_{n,m}(C_n(R)), \circ)$ is an Abelian group and $(T2_{n,m}(C_n(R)), \circ)$ is a subgroup of $(V_{n,m}(C_n(R)), \circ)$ where $T2_{n,m}(C_n(R))$ = $\{C_n(R)\}$ $\cup$ $\{C_n(S):$ $C_n(S)$ is Typ-2 isomorphic to $C_n(R)$ w.r.t. $m \}$ and $(T2_{n,m}(C_n(R)), \circ)$ is the Type-2 group of $C_n(R)$ w.r.t. $m$. We also present many examples of Type-1 and Type-2 groups where $T1_{n}(C_n(R))$ = $\{C_n(xR): x\in\varphi_{n}\}$ is the Type-1 set of $C_n(R)$ and $(T1_{n}(C_n(R)), \circ')$ is its Type-1 group.

papers.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. Part 4: 960 triples of Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs $C_{54}(R)$
papers.abstract: This article is the $4^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10} and is a continuation of Part 3. Here, we obtain all 960 triples of Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs of order 54 and each triple of isomorphic circulant graphs is of Type-2 isomorphic w.r.t. $m$ = 3.

papers.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. Part 5: Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs of orders 48, 81, 96
papers.abstract: This article is the $5^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10} and is a continuation of Part 4. Here, we study Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs of $C_{48}(r_1,r_2,r_3)$, $C_{81}(r_1,r_2,r_3)$ and $C_{96}(r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4)$. We find that for $n$ = 48,96, total number of pairs of isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 2 of the forms $C_{n}(r_1,r_2,r_3)$ and $C_{n}(s_1,s_2,s_3)$ are 18 and 72, respectively, and total number of triples of isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 3 of the form $C_{81}(x_1,x_2,x_3)$, $C_{81}(y_1,y_2,y_3)$ and $C_{81}(z_1,z_2,z_3)$ are 27.

papers.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. Part 3: 384 pairs of Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs $C_{32}(R)$
papers.abstract: This article is the $3^{rd}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10} and is a continuation of Part 2. Here, we obtain all 384 pairs of Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs of order 32.

papers.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. Part 1: Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs $C_n(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ = 2
papers.abstract: This article is the first part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}. Circulant graphs $C_n(R)$ and $C_n(S)$ are said to be \emph{Adam's isomorphic} if there exist some $a\in \mathbb{Z}_n^*$ such that $S = a R$ under arithmetic reflexive modulo $n$ \cite{ad67}. In 1970, Elspas and Turner \cite{eltu} raised a question on the isomorphism of $C_{16}(1,3,7)$ and $C_{16}(2,3,5)$. The author \cite{v96} further modify the definition to $m$ and $m^3$ are divisors of $\gcd(n, r)$ and $n$, respectively, and $r\in R$. Using the modified definition \ref{d16}, we present our study on Type-2 isomorphism of circulant graphs $C_n(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ = 2. We reprove that $(i)$ $C_{16}(1,2,7)$ and $C_{16}(2,3,5)$ are Type-2 isomorphic w.r.t. $m$ = 2; $(ii)$ For $n \geq 2$, $k \geq 3$, $1 \leq 2s-1 \leq 2n-1$, $n \neq 2s-1$, $R$ = $\{2, 2s-1, 4n-(2s-1)\}$ and $S$ = $\{2, 2n-(2s-1), 2n+2s-1\}$, $C_{8n}(R)$ and $C_{8n}(S)$ are Type-2 isomorphic w.r.t. $m$ = 2, $n,s\in\mathbb{N}$; and $(iii)$ For $n \geq 2$, $1 \leq 2s-1 < 2s'-1 \leq [\frac{n}{2}]$, $0 \leq t \leq [\frac{n}{2}]$, $R$ = $\{2,2s-1, 2s'-1\}$ and $n,s,s'\in \mathbb{N}$, if $θ_{n,2,t}(C_n(R))$ and $C_n(R)$ are isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 2 for some $t$, then $n \equiv 0~(mod ~ 8)$, $2s-1+2s'-1$ = $\frac{n}{2}$, $2s-1 \neq \frac{n}{8}$, $t$ = $\frac{n}{8}$ or $\frac{3n}{8}$, $1 \leq 2s-1 \leq \frac{n}{4}$ and $n \geq 16$ where $θ_{n,m,t}$ is a transformation used to define Type-2 isomorphism of a circulant graph. At the end, we present a VB program POLY215.EXE which shows how Type-2 isomorphism w.r.t. $m$ = 2 of $C_{8n}(R)$ takes place for $R = \{2, 2s-1, 4n-(2s-1)\}$, $n \geq 2$ and $n,s\in {\mathbb N}$.

papers.title: Bistability, Absolute Concentration Robustness, and Hysteresis in Dual-Site Futile Cycles with Bifunctional Enzymes
papers.abstract: Bifunctional enzymes, which catalyze both the forward and reverse steps of a substrate modification reaction, arise naturally in bacterial two-component signaling systems and metabolic regulation. Beyond their well-known role in conferring absolute concentration robustness (ACR) on substrate species, bifunctional enzymes profoundly shape the dynamical landscape of the networks in which they appear. We study a class of dual-site futile cycles in which the reverse modification steps are carried out by bifunctional enzyme-substrate compounds, and provide a complete mathematical analysis of all four such networks, characterizing the existence, number, and stability of steady states, as well as the bifurcation structure as total substrate is varied. All four networks admit boundary steady states, in contrast to the non-bifunctional case. The networks differ in the number and stability of boundary steady states, in the maximum number of positive steady states (ranging from two to four), and in whether bistability is present. In two networks, a transcritical bifurcation connects the boundary and positive steady state branches; in one case this is a backward bifurcation, producing hysteresis. Perhaps the most striking phenomenon occurs in one of the four networks, which simultaneously exhibits bistability and ACR in the final modification state, where the system can settle into either of two stable steady states with different intermediate concentrations yet identical final product concentration.

papers.title: Phases of Muon: When Muon Eclipses SignSGD
papers.abstract: Muon and related spectral optimizers have recently demonstrated strong empirical performance as scalable stochastic methods, often outperforming Adam. Yet their behavior remains poorly understood. We analyze stochastic Muon, which orthogonalizes an exponential moving average of minibatch gradients, on a high-dimensional matrix-valued least squares problem, and we compare it with stochastic SignSGD, a simple baseline comparable to Adam. We derive explicit deterministic dynamics that provide a tractable framework for studying learning behavior. We show that Muon has non-linear sensitivity to the effective batch $B_{\rm eff}=B(1+β)/(1-β)$. With exact whitening and small $B_{\rm eff}$ Muon fails to resolve smaller eigenmodes, slowing down convergence. Momentum and finite Newton--Shulz iterations can act as a ridge which lessen this effect. This behavior is in contrast with SignSGD which has no transition, leading to different optimal learning rates, but with matching convergence rate up to a constant factor in the isotropic setting. For anisotropic data, large batch setting Muon performs a square-root preconditioning with respect to the data covariance spectrum while SignSGD provides no preconditioning for generic covariances. We analyze time to target loss in a power law covariance model and derive a phase diagram in the data exponent $α$ and target exponent $ζ$. Muon is favored for steep covariance spectra with rich targets ($α>2$, $ζ<α+1$), SignSGD is favored for flat spectra ($α<1$), and in other regions the winner depends on how the target loss scales with dimension. Our results shed light on why replacing Adam with Muon is not trivial even from a pure optimization perspective.

papers.title: Volumetric density estimates for nonlocal minimal surfaces
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that viscosity subsolutions to nonlocal mean curvature-type equations satisfy universal volumetric estimates at all scales provided their boundary has zero Lebesgue measure. Our results hold for a general class of symmetric kernels including kernels that are comparable to the fractional Laplacian. Furthermore, we prove that subsolutions with low density (with respect to a universal constant) necessarily have `fat boundary', that is, have topological boundary with positive Lebesgue measure.

papers.title: Parametric Statistical Inference in the Zone of Moderate Deviation Probabilities
papers.abstract: A parametric theory of statistical inference is developed for the moderate deviation probability zone. The new approach to the proofs is based on the Taylor series expansion of the logarithm of the likelihood ratio based on the Hellinger distance. The Large Deviation Principle in the moderate deviation probability zone is proven for Bayesian estimators and maximum likelihood estimators. A uniform approximation of the logarithm of the likelihood ratio and Theorem on concentration of the posterior Bayesian measure are also established for the zone of moderate deviation probabilities.

papers.title: On $q$-convex hypersurfaces in Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that any closed, convex hypersurface in an $(n+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with $\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$-positive curvature operator is a rational homology sphere with finite fundamental group. The same conclusion holds for any $\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$-convex hypersurface, provided that the mean curvature satisfies a sharp pinching condition. Both results follow from more general vanishing and estimation theorems for the Betti numbers of closed $q$-convex immersed hypersurfaces in $(n+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds, under a lower bound on the average of the smallest $(n-p)$ eigenvalues of the curvature operator.

papers.title: Short-wave signal versus indirect prey-taxis
papers.abstract: We address a short-wave asymptotic for one class of quasi-linear second-order PDE systems involving the cross-diffusion described by the so-called Patlak-Keller-Segel law. It is common to employ these equations for modeling the predator-prey community with the prey-taxis, which means the interactions of two species of particles or cells or anything else through which the species called "predators" is capable of moving directionally while searching for the other species called "prey." However, we suppose the predators to be sensitive not to the prey density but to a cue produced by the prey. Additionally, the production of the cue is assumed to be sensitive to the intensity of an external field, which is independent of the community state. This is what we call the external signal. It can be due to the spatiotemporal inhomogeneity of the environment arising from natural or artificial reasons. We assume that the external signal takes a general short-wave form and construct a complete formal asymptotic expansion for the short-wave solutions (modulo solving a chain of the so-called slow systems) with no restrictions on the spatial dimension or kinetics of inter- or intra-specific reactions. Further, we apply the short-wave asymptotic to studying the stability or instability induced by the external signal following Kapitza's theory for the upside-down pendulum. Applying the general results to some special classes of external signals, we get examples of suppressing the taxical transport, examples of the robustness of the species equilibrium to the signal up to a very strong stabilization or, oppositely, destabilization, and something like blurring the borderline in the parametric space between the areas of stability and instability of this equilibrium.

papers.title: Structure-Aware Variational Learning of a Class of Generalized Diffusions
papers.abstract: Learning the underlying potential energy of stochastic gradient systems from partial and noisy observations is a fundamental problem arising in physics, chemistry, and data-driven modeling. Classical approaches often rely on direct regression of governing equations or velocity fields, which can be sensitive to noise and external perturbations and may fail when observations are incomplete. In this work, we propose a structure-aware, energy-based learning framework for inferring unknown potential functions in generalized diffusion processes, grounded in the energetic variational approach. Starting from the energy-dissipation law associated with the Fokker-Planck equation, we construct loss functions based on the De Giorgi dissipation functional, which consistently couple the free energy and the dissipation mechanism of the system. This formulation avoids explicit enforcement of the governing partial differential equation and preserves the underlying variational structure of the dynamics. Through numerical experiments in one, two, and three dimensions, we demonstrate that the proposed energy-based loss exhibits enhanced robustness with respect to observation time, noise level, and the diversity and amount of available training data. These results highlight the effectiveness of energy-dissipation principles as a reliable foundation for learning stochastic diffusion dynamics from data.

papers.title: Analytical properties of $q$-metallic numbers
papers.abstract: For an integer $n\geq 1$, consider the $n$-th metallic number $φ_n=\frac{n+\sqrt{n^2+4}}{2}$ (e.g. $φ_1$ is the golden number) and denote by $[φ_n]_q$ its $q$-deformation in the sense of S. Morier-Genoud and V. Ovsienko. This is an algebraic continued fraction which admits an expansion into a power series $[φ_n]_q =\sum_{l=0}^{+\infty} κ_l(φ_n) q^l$ around $q=0$, with integral coefficients. By using techniques from analytic combinatorics, we establish several properties of the sequence $( κ_l(φ_n))_{l\geq 0}$ of Taylor coefficients: characterisation by recurrences or by differential equations, closed-form expressions when $n=1,2,3$, and asymptotics. We also present some remarkable identities induced by the action of the modular group $PSL(2,Z)$ and address, mainly through computer experimentations, the question of the logarithmic behaviour of the sequence $( κ_l(φ_n))_{l\geq 0}$. A particular accent is put on the comparison between the $q$-deformation $[φ_1]_q$ of the golden ratio and RNA secondary structures, the former being actually a signed version of the latter. By doing so, we would be pleased to bring the interest of combinatoricians to the newly discovered world of $q$-numbers.

papers.title: Restricted Projections to Hyperplanes in $\mathbb{R}^n$
papers.abstract: We study dimensions of sets projected to an $(n-2)$-dimensional family of hyperplanes in $\mathbb{R}^n$ under curvature conditions. Let $n\ge 4$, $Σ\subset S^{n-1}$ be an $(n-2)$-dimensional $C^2$ manifold such that $Σ$ has sectional curvature $>1$ and $Z \subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$ be analytic. If $\dimπ_{T_yS^{n-1}}(Z) \le n-2$ for some $y \in S^{n-1}$, then $\dim π_{T_xS^{n-1}}(Z) = \dim Z$ for $\mathcal{H}^{n-2}$-a.e. $x \in Σ$.

papers.title: Unified Communication Compression Beyond Global Error Bounds for Distributed Nonconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a unified compression algorithm for distributed nonconvex opitmization with both the locally- and globally-bounded communication compressors, including 1-bit compressors, saturating quantizers, and the globally-bounded compressors with both relative and absolute compression errors, as well as additional arbitrary bounded noise. We provide a rigorous convergence analysis in nonconvex settings and establish linear convergence under the Polyak-Lojasiewicz (P-L) condition. Notably, we establish an $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ convergence rate for the locally-bounded class in the distributed nonconvex setting, matching that achieved by the centralized algorithms with 1-bit compressors, where $T$ denotes the total number of iterations. Moreover, one initial uncompressed communication round further yields an order-wise improvement to $\mathcal{O}(1/T^{2/3})$. For the P-L setting and the globally-bounded class, we recover state-of-the-art convergence rates.

papers.title: Solvable Lie Foliations on Compact Five-Manifolds: Classification, Cohomological Obstruction, and Non-Homogeneous Examples
papers.abstract: We study $\GA$-Lie foliations on compact five-manifolds. We establish a structural classification of the holonomy group $Γ$ into five types according to its algebraic structure inside $\GA$. For three of these types (I, II, IIIa) we prove homogeneity via Meigniez's theorem and the Matsumoto--Tsuchiya theorem. For Type~IIIb we prove non-homogeneity by exhibiting a non-polycyclic holonomy group, extending the Dathe--Ndiaye construction \cite{DN11}. We introduce a cohomological class $[F]\in H^2(Γ^{\mathrm{ab}},[Γ,Γ])$ as a \emph{necessary} obstruction to homogeneity: if $\mathcal{F}$ is homogeneous and $Γ$ is polycyclic then $[F]=0$. We show that Type IIIb foliations satisfy $[F]\neq 0$. For Type IIIc, we prove that certain foliations are non-homogeneous by a direct argument when the generating translations are $\Q(λ)$-linearly independent; we exhibit explicit homogeneous examples showing that this type is \emph{not} universally non-homogeneous. Finally, we construct the first known non-homogeneous $\mathrm{Sol}$-Lie foliation in dimension five by a verified lattice deformation.

papers.title: Persistence of the Wiener sausage: sampling stability and limit theorems for Betti-curve functionals of planar Brownian motion
papers.abstract: We study the persistent homology of the offset filtration generated by the range of a planar Brownian motion with constant nonzero drift (Wiener sausages of increasing radius). We prove what are, to our knowledge, the first law of large numbers and central limit theorem for its smoothed Betti-curve functionals. For every bounded Borel weight $ψ$ supported in a compact radius window $[r_0,r_1]\subset(0,\infty)$, the functional $Φ_ψ(T)=\int_{r_0}^{r_1}β_1(T,r)ψ(r)\,dr$, where $β_1(T,r)$ counts the holes of the radius-$r$ sausage at time $T$, satisfies $Φ_ψ(T)/T\toρ_ψ$ almost surely and in every $L^p$, for a deterministic constant $ρ_ψ$. This yields a finite positive Betti-curve intensity measure on the radius axis, which we identify as absolutely continuous through a fixed-radius law of large numbers along regeneration times, valid at almost every radius. We also prove Gaussian fluctuations at scale $\sqrt{T}$, for one weight and jointly for finitely many, with a Green-Kubo variance over the regeneration cycles. The proof combines a renewal structure along the drift direction, obtained by the method of Sznitman and Zerner without invoking the strong Markov property at the cut times, with a Mayer-Vietoris control of the non-additivity of topology under concatenation and a deterministic bound on the integrated hole count of a planar offset proved in a companion paper. A sampling theorem bounds the bottleneck distance between the diagram of the continuous filtration and that of a time-sampled point cloud by the pathwise modulus of continuity, placing these objects in a data-analytic framework.

papers.title: Area and antipodal distance in convex hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We establish a lower bound for the surface area of a closed, convex hypersurface in Euclidean space in terms of its displacement under continuous maps. As a result, a hypothesized lower bound for the volume of a Riemannian $n$-sphere, proved by Berger in dimension $n=2$ and disproved by Croke in dimensions $n \geq 3$, is valid for convex hypersurfaces in all dimensions. We also establish a sharp lower bound for the mean width of a convex hypersurface.

papers.title: Conditional Sampling via Wasserstein Autoencoders and Triangular Transport
papers.abstract: We present Conditional Wasserstein Autoencoders (CWAEs), a framework for conditional simulation that exploits low-dimensional structure in both the conditioned and the conditioning variables. The key idea is to modify a Wasserstein autoencoder to use a (block-) triangular decoder and impose an appropriate independence assumption on the latent variables. We show that the resulting model gives an autoencoder that can exploit low-dimensional structure while simultaneously the decoder can be used for conditional simulation. We explore various theoretical properties of CWAEs, including their connections to conditional optimal transport (OT) problems. We also present alternative formulations that lead to three architectural variants forming the foundation of our algorithms. We present a series of numerical experiments that demonstrate that our different CWAE variants achieve substantial reductions in approximation error relative to the low-rank ensemble Kalman filter (LREnKF), particularly in problems where the support of the conditional measures is truly low-dimensional.

papers.title: Wavefront sets for genuine representations of $\rm GL$-covers of Kazhdan--Patterson or Savin types
papers.abstract: First, we consider general Brylinski--Deligne covers of the $p$-adic general linear groups, and discuss the theory of Bernstein--Zelevinsky derivatives. We also recall the Zelevinsky-type classification of the irreducible genuine spectrum for the Kazhdan--Patterson and Savin covers. Following this, for these two special families of covers, we determine the wavefront sets of their irreducible genuine representations, expressed in terms of the iterated degrees of the highest Bernstein--Zelevinsky derivatives. Finally, for Kazhdan--Patterson covers, we reinterpret this result on the wavefront set using a version of the local Langlands correspondence and the covering Barbasch--Vogan duality.

papers.title: Normal forms in cubical type theory
papers.abstract: This note documents the specification of normal forms in cubical type theory. The definition is already present in the proof of normalization for cubical type theory, but we present it in a more traditional style explicitly for reference.

papers.title: On aggregation-quantization permutability problem for discrete-time Markov chains
papers.abstract: Given random walk on a graph, the corresponding discrete-time quantum walk can be constructed using the method proposed by Szegedy. On the other hand, given a partition of the set of states of a Markov chain, one can study the corresponding aggregated process. We extend the aggregation technique to the level of quantum Markov chains. We provide conditions under which application of these two operations - Szegedy's quantization and aggregation - give the same result. These consist of the strong lumpability of the underlying Markov chain supplemented by nonlinear relations, generalizing Kolmogorov's cycle condition, that account for the coefficients of both the original and the aggregated transition matrices. In particular, we show that the conditions are satisfied in the case of the random walk on graphs equipped with equitable partitions. We present several examples, which include the classical/quantum walks on Platonic solids. We discuss also relation of discrete-time classical/quantum walks on $N$-dimensional hypercube and the Ehrenfests urn model with $N$ particles. We apply our technique for of discrete-time walks on Cayley graphs of free groups. We also compare our results with those obtained using Cantero-Moral-Velazquez uniformization of unitary matrices.

papers.title: Arithmetic limiting laws over shifted primes: dimension zero, Fourier decay, and absolute continuity
papers.abstract: For primes $p$, let $c(p)=\frac{\varphi(p-1)}{p-1}\prod_{j\ge1}(1-p^{-j})$. Let $μ_G$ be its classical shifted-totient limiting law over primes and $μ_f$ its image under $x\mapsto-\log x$. Both laws have Hausdorff dimension zero, packing dimension one on every positive-mass Borel set, and almost-everywhere lower and upper local dimensions $(0,1)$. The four totient and divisor-sum laws over integers and shifted primes, and their logarithmic images, have lower and upper Shannon information dimensions in $(0.5503615,0.570489495)$. For convolution powers $μ_f^{*k}$, both information dimensions tend to one as $k\to\infty$, while each finite power has Hausdorff dimension zero. $μ_G$ gives full mass to absolutely normal Liouville numbers. Both Fourier transforms are $O((\log|τ|)^{-1/3}(\log\log|τ|)^{1/3})$. The empirical laws of $c(p)$ and $\varphi(p-1)/(p-1)$ for $p\le x$ have sharp Kolmogorov order $1/\log x$ in fixed reduced progressions; over unrestricted primes, they and their logarithmic images converge in $1$-Wasserstein distance at rate $O_B((\log x)^{-B})$ for every fixed $B>0$, possibly with ineffective constants. For $μ_f$, we obtain concentration expansions to every fixed inverse-logarithmic order, quantitative maximizer localization near $\log3$, and Fourier resonance bounds. For $U_T$ uniform on $[0,T]$, $(\log T)\widehat{μ_f}(U_T)$ converges in distribution to a circularly symmetric random Euler product, with convergence of modulus moments for every fixed real $s>-1$. Strongly additive functions with prime values $(\log\ell)^{-A}$ have absolutely continuous integer and shifted-prime laws for $A>0$. We give certified number-theoretic transform prime searches. A lattice appendix determines second and third distinct nonzero squared norms of type-$A$ tensor products and gives cyclotomic smoothing bounds. These results are unconditional.

papers.title: From Global Optimization to Exact Coordinates: Heilbronn's Triangle Problem on the Unit Square Using Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Optimization
papers.abstract: We develop a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) approach for the Heilbronn triangle problem on the unit square. The formulation exploits the boundary structure of optimal configurations, which we establish rigorously, to fix coordinates and orientation variables a priori. With this formulation, a general-purpose global solver solves the case $n=9$ to global optimality within its numerical tolerances in about eight minutes on a laptop and without any precomputation, compared with about 23 hours of total computation for the best previous approach. The same model also solves $n=10$ for the first time, in under seven hours, and confirms the configuration of Comellas and Yebra (2002). The numerical solutions then guide an exact symbolic reconstruction, and the minimum triangle area of every reconstructed configuration is verified in exact arithmetic. This yields exact coordinates for all $n\le 10$, including the configurations of Comellas and Yebra (2002) for $n=9$ and $n=10$, together with rigorous lower bounds. Finally, we derive structural properties of optimal configurations, formulate a conjecture on the number of critical triangles, and pose an open question. All code and data are publicly available.

papers.title: Finite-energy solutions to Einstein-scalar field Lichnerowicz equations on complete Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We consider the singular elliptic problem of the form \[ -Δu + V(x)u = \mathcal{B}(x)|u|^{2^*-2}u + \frac{\mathcal{A}(x)}{|u|^{2^*}u}, \qquad u\in H^1(M), \] where the coefficients are allowed to have low regularity. Under natural spectral assumptions on $-Δ+V$, geometric assumptions on the manifold $M$ ensuring the Sobolev embedding $H^1(M)\hookrightarrow L^{2^*}(M)$, and a suitable global integrability/smallness condition involving $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$, and a function $ψ\in H^1(M)$, we prove the existence of a nonnegative finite-energy supersolution. If, in addition, the Ricci curvature is nonnegative and $\mathcal{B}\ge 0$, we obtain a positive finite-energy solution. The proof relies on a family of $\varepsilon$-regularized problems, mountain pass arguments, and a limiting procedure in which Harnack's inequality plays a crucial role in handling the singular term on noncompact manifolds. We also prove a nonexistence result showing that the global integrability condition on $\mathcal{A}$ is, in a precise sense, necessary for the existence of nonnegative supersolutions.

papers.title: Prismatoid Band-Unfolding Revisited
papers.abstract: It remains unknown if every prismatoid has a nonoverlapping edge-unfolding, a special case of the long-unsolved "Dürer's problem." Recently nested prismatoids have been settled [Rad24] by mixing (in some sense) the two natural unfoldings, petal-unfolding and band-unfolding. Band-unfolding fails due to a specific counterexample [O'R13b]. The main contribution of this paper is a characterization when a band-unfolding of a nested prismatoid does in fact result in a nonoverlapping unfolding. In particular, we show that the mentioned counterexample is in a sense the only possible counterexample. Although this result does not expand the class of shapes known to have an edge-unfolding, its proof expands our understanding in several ways, developing tools that may help resolve the non-nested case.

papers.title: Demi Weak Dunford-Pettis Operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, our main goal is to introduce the class of Demi Weak Dunford-Pettis operators. We also investigate its relationship with the classes of weak Dunford-Pettis and demi Dunford-Pettis operators, as well as conditions under which this class coincide with the classes of demi Dunford-Pettis and demicompact operators. In the final section, we study some properties of this new class in the setting of Banach lattices.

papers.title: Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Online Learning
papers.abstract: We study online Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization (DRO), where the ambiguity set is a Wasserstein ball centered at the empirical distribution and evolves with each observation.
